findings.title: Dashboard bypasses the canonical liveness model bu-86c4c.17 built — fleet state forks into a second dialect
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/overview/model.ts:151-153 (local HEALTHY/DEGRADED/OFFLINE status sets), model.ts:271-311 (deriveButlerIndexRow: own 5-min stale threshold from useButlers + useButlerHeartbeats); vs frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:1-15 (GET /api/butlers/board: server-side canonical activity verb + cron-cadence expectations, 'shared by every consumer'); frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:79-93 (sessionPatch invalidates ["butlers","board"] but NOT the dashboard's ["butlers"]/["system-butler-heartbeats"] keys; heartbeatPatch:136-138 is a deliberate no-op)
findings.detail: The epic's judgment-layer bead landed ONE canonical liveness verdict (running/idle/overdue/offline, cadence-aware: 'silent 3d, expected daily') on /butlers and /system — but the flagship Overview still hand-rolls its own client-side liveness from two separately-polled queries. Consequences: (1) the dashboard and the board can render contradictory verdicts for the same butler at the same instant; (2) the dashboard has zero cadence awareness — a weekly butler and a broken hourly butler both read 'healthy' while heartbeats beat; (3) the event bus live-patches the board key, so /butlers updates in the same beat while / lags its 30s poll — the single pane the owner is told to trust is the stalest fleet-health surface in the app.

findings.title: Approve/Deny/Defer on the dashboard fire immediately with neither undo window nor confirm — two safety contracts for the same verbs
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:139-141 (onApprove/onDeny/onDefer call mutate() directly); vs frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1308-1325 (scheduleDecision wraps the same mutations in UNDO_WINDOW_MS with a toast Undo action); frontend/src/hooks/use-approval-decisions.ts:71-89 (approve dispatches the tool on success — irreversible)
findings.detail: On /approvals a keyboard decision gets a grace window with an Undo toast before the mutation runs; on the dashboard's Needs-attention rows the identical verb executes instantly — one accidental click on the page the owner lands on first dispatches an irreversible tool execution with no recovery path. Design-bar recovery bias: 'never replace a confirm with an undo that can't undo' — here there is neither. The shared hook exists (use-approval-decisions.ts) but the undo-window logic stayed page-local in ApprovalsPage instead of moving into it.

findings.title: Cost Today renders a bold $0.00 when the spend-summary fetch fails; Most Expensive Sessions renders 'No session data available' on error
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:121 (costQuery.isError → costData null), :233 (totalCostUsd={costData?.total_cost_usd ?? 0}), :125 (topSessions = isError ? []); frontend/src/components/costs/CostWidget.tsx:8-22,54 (no summary-error prop — only dailyCostsError for the sparkline); frontend/src/components/costs/TopSessionsTable.tsx:57-68 (empty === error)
findings.detail: Truth amnesty (bu-86c4c.1/.2) landed for the sparkline (honest 'trend unavailable') and the KPI strip (em-dashes on error) but stopped one prop short: the widget's headline number and the sessions table still let a failed fetch impersonate a zero-spend, zero-session day. NOT-LANDED residue of the fabrication/error-as-empty sin on the exact surface the epic targeted — a dead spend API reads as 'the fleet spent nothing today', the opposite of earned calm.

findings.title: The cost band is a second visual instrument: shadcn cards, Title Case sans headings, badges and ghost buttons on a page the spec says is card-free
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md §Density and Spacing ('rule-separated rows… never cards; padding: 24px on a list item is card thinking and forbidden') and §Eyebrow Section Titles; frontend/src/components/costs/CostWidget.tsx:34-52 (Card/CardHeader/CardTitle 'Cost Today', ghost Button, bg-primary/60 bars, animate-pulse); TopSessionsTable.tsx:40-75 (Card, Badge, Title Case table); DashboardPage.tsx:114-120 comment shows dashboard-domain-pages spec REQUIRES these widgets — the two specs disagree
findings.detail: Everything above the fold is Dispatch (mono eyebrows, hairline rules, serif voice); the full-width band below is the pre-redesign shadcn dialect — cards, bold Title Case CardTitles, secondary badges, en-US-hardcoded timestamps (TopSessionsTable.tsx:31), a primary-tinted sparkline outside the chart tokens. The page visibly reads as two hands. Per design-bar doctrine the spec disagreement itself (dashboard-domain-pages mandates CostWidget/TopSessionsTable; dashboard-design-language forbids cards) is a finding: one of the two specs must yield.

findings.title: Failed-notification signal is event-dead: the bus patches keys the dashboard never reads, and the stats hook has no poll
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:100-104 (notificationPatch invalidates ["messenger-delivery-stats"], ["messenger-queue-depth"], ["timeline"] — not ["notification-stats"] or ["notifications"]); frontend/src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:32-37 (useNotificationStats: no refetchInterval, no staleTime); frontend/src/lib/query-client.ts (staleTime 30s, refetch only on focus)
findings.detail: The dashboard's 'N failed notifications' rows (attention list + Now list, model.ts:499-515,590-603) read ["notification-stats"]. A notification that fails after page load emits a live event on the bus, the registry consumes it — and invalidates only messenger-page keys. On the pane designed to be left open, the delivery-failure signal never appears until the owner blurs and refocuses the tab. Stale state silently presented as current; the declarative-registry promise ('adding a surface means adding one entry') was not kept in sync with the surfaces that already existed.

findings.title: KPI 'Healthy' counts by status string only, contradicting the attention list on the same screen
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/overview/model.ts:258 (healthyButlers = butlers.filter(isHealthyStatus(butler.status)) — heartbeats ignored); vs model.ts:184-186 + 271-311 (attention rows derive stale/offline FROM heartbeats)
findings.detail: A butler with status 'ok' but a 20-minute-dead heartbeat produces an '<name> heartbeat is stale' attention row while the KPI strip directly beneath reports it inside 'Healthy: 9/9'. Two verdicts about the same butler, four hundred pixels apart, from the same render pass. Falls out automatically if the KPI consumes the canonical board verdict (finding 1).

findings.title: Now-list activity rows discard the event identity they hold — drill-down dead end into an unanchorable /timeline
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/overview/model.ts:614-623 (row id is now:activity:${event.id} but href is flat "/timeline"; event.data with session_id discarded); frontend/src/pages/TimelinePage.tsx:76-88 (filters are useState only — the page accepts no deep-link/search params at all)
findings.detail: The freshest signals on the page (last two timeline events) link to the generic chronicle, where the owner must re-find the event they just clicked. The drill-down sweep (bu-86c4c.4) gave attention rows real per-butler anchors but the Now column kept flat hrefs; not covered by bu-9d5vp (KPI cells/egress/audit/spend) or bu-ddo0n (attention strip/scrubber). Session-type events could link straight to /sessions/<id> today; the rest need TimelinePage to accept ?event=/?butler= params.

findings.title: The verdict prose is a 5-minute-stale cache with zero clause-doors, and its loading fallback asserts unproven health
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/dashboard_briefing.py:17-19 (per-owner LRU+TTL 5-min cache), frontend/src/hooks/use-briefing.ts:23-36 (mirrored 5-min refetch); frontend/src/components/overview/Headline.tsx:33-34 + Elaboration.tsx:32-34 (plain-text render, no links); frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:160-161 (fallback: 'Butlers are running.' before any source has loaded)
findings.detail: The attention list beneath the headline updates on the live event bus; the judgment above it can lag five minutes — 'All quiet.' over a critical issue row that arrived 3 minutes ago is a coherence break at the page's most prominent surface. The north-star property 'every clause of that prose is a door' is absent: neither headline nor elaboration carries a single anchor. And while everything loads, the fallback elaboration asserts 'Butlers are running.' — a claim the page cannot yet prove, mildly violating no-fabrication in the very voice meant to embody it.

audits.jarvis_gap: The epic's landings genuinely hold on this page — the attention list, KPI strip, and butler index all distinguish error from empty; the event bus is mounted app-wide; inline decisions exist; the briefing is a real classified verdict, not decoration. What separates it from JARVIS is coherence and follow-through: the page runs TWO liveness models (its own client-side one vs the canonical server verdict the same epic built), TWO visual dialects (Dispatch above, legacy shadcn cards below), TWO safety contracts for the identical approve verb (undo-window on /approvals, instant-fire here), and a live event bus that patches keys the page's notification signal never reads. The verdict prose — the page's soul — is a 5-minute cache with no clause-doors sitting above a live-updating evidence list it can contradict. Each seam is small; together they make the single pane read as assembled rather than built by one hand, and earned calm leaks out through exactly those seams.

moves.title: Move the Overview onto the canonical board verdict (one liveness model, live by default)
moves.why: Kills the fleet-state fork (findings 1 and 6) at the root: ButlerIndex, the runtime attention rows, and the Healthy KPI all consume GET /api/butlers/board's server-computed activity verb + cadence status instead of model.ts's private status sets. The dashboard gains cadence judgment ('silent 3d, expected daily' instead of a flat 'healthy'), stops disagreeing with /butlers and /system, and becomes live for free — the event bus already patches ["butlers","board"] on every session event.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/overview/model.ts (delete deriveButlerIndexRow + status sets; take BoardRow[] as input), frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx (swap useButlers+useButlerHeartbeats for useButlerStatusBoard), frontend/src/hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts (already exposes activity/cellTone/cadence), event-cache-registry.ts (no change needed — board key is patched)
moves.slice_plan: 1) model.ts accepts BoardRow[] and maps activity verb → attention rows + KPI healthy count (tests first, pure function); 2) DashboardPage swaps hooks, deletes the two dead queries; 3) ButlerIndex subtitle renders cadence status ('overdue · expected daily') and cost from the board row; 4) delete HEALTHY/DEGRADED/OFFLINE_STATUSES + stale-threshold logic and their tests.

moves.title: One decision safety contract: fold the undo window into useApprovalDecisionMutations
moves.why: The same verb must carry the same recovery everywhere (finding 2). Approve dispatches an irreversible tool execution; today the flagship page fires it on a single un-undoable click while /approvals gives a grace window. Moving scheduleDecision/UNDO_WINDOW_MS into the shared hook makes every current and future decision surface (dashboard, approvals, upcoming chat widget bu-p6ey8) inherit apply-in-frame optimism WITH the undo toast — the exact north-star action contract.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-approval-decisions.ts (add withUndoWindow wrapper + module-scoped scheduled-decision store lifted from ApprovalsPage.tsx:1280-1325), frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:139-141, frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx (delete its local copy), frontend/src/components/overview/AttentionList.tsx (row shows 'Approving in 5s · Undo' state)
moves.slice_plan: 1) extract scheduleDecision into the hook behind an option, unit-test timer/cancel/rollback; 2) ApprovalsPage consumes the extracted version (behavior-identical, its tests prove it); 3) dashboard rows opt in; row renders the pending-undo state inline so the toast isn't the only affordance.

moves.title: Retire the shadcn cost band: spend verdict as a Dispatch strip, truth-complete on error
moves.why: Fixes the page's largest dialect break and its last error-impersonates-empty hole in one move (findings 3 and 4). One Spend (/spend, bu-86c4c.11) already owns cost depth — the Overview needs a verdict-sized spend surface, not two legacy cards duplicating it in a foreign visual language. Also resolves the dashboard-domain-pages vs dashboard-design-language spec conflict by amending the former.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:221-242 (delete band), frontend/src/components/costs/CostWidget.tsx + TopSessionsTable.tsx (retire from this page), frontend/src/components/overview/KpiStrip.tsx (add 'Spend · today' cell: mega-number, em-dash + source-named note when costQuery.isError, RowLink to /spend), openspec/specs/dashboard-domain-pages (spec delta via spec workflow), frontend e2e specs referencing cost-widget testids
moves.slice_plan: 1) spec delta: Overview's cost obligation becomes 'one honest spend KPI + top-session line, Dispatch dialect, links to /spend'; 2) add the KPI cell with error/empty/loaded states (em-dash on error, never 0); 3) one rule-separated 'most expensive session today' row in the Now column linking to /sessions/<id>; 4) delete the band + update e2e fixtures.

moves.title: Close the event-bus coverage holes with a registry↔hook contract test
moves.why: Finding 5 is one instance of a class: the declarative registry drifts from the query keys surfaces actually use, and nothing fails when it does. Patch notificationPatch to invalidate ["notification-stats"]/["notifications"], then add a test that walks every query key the Overview (and each live page) mounts and asserts it is covered by either a registry patch or an explicit poll — so the next new surface can't silently go event-dead.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:100-104, frontend/src/hooks/use-notifications.ts:32-37, new frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.coverage.test.ts (import dashboard hook key constants; assert patch-or-poll), src/butlers/api/routers/events.py EVENT_TYPES comment sync
moves.slice_plan: 1) one-line registry fix + regression test that a notification event invalidates notification-stats; 2) export key constants from hooks that inline them today; 3) coverage test enumerating Overview's nine query keys against the registry + refetchInterval presence.

moves.title: Clause-doored live verdict: the headline judges the same model the page renders
moves.why: The north star's signature property — 'every clause of that prose is a door' — is absent at its most prominent location, and the cached verdict can contradict live evidence beneath it (finding 8). Compute state_class client-side from the SAME live triage model (attention rows, board verdicts, pending approvals) so headline and evidence can never disagree; keep the LLM elaboration as flavor but return it as structured clause spans with anchor targets so each clause links to its evidence (approval id, butler, issue group).
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/overview/model.ts (add classifyTriage(state) mirroring briefing/classify.py rules), frontend/src/components/overview/Headline.tsx + Elaboration.tsx (render clause spans as RowLink-styled inline anchors), src/butlers/api/routers/dashboard_briefing.py + briefing/prompts.py (elaboration returns [{text, href}] clauses; voice-lint per clause), src/butlers/api/briefing/classify.py (share thresholds via the API so the two classifiers can't drift)
moves.slice_plan: 1) client-side state_class from the live model drives the headline immediately (templated headline_for strings ported; briefing endpoint keeps serving elaboration only); 2) briefing response gains clauses[] with typed anchors, plain string kept during migration; 3) Elaboration renders clause anchors (keyboard-focusable, Dispatch underline-on-hover); 4) invalidate the server cache on high-severity fleet events so the LLM voice re-writes within the beat, not the TTL.

audits.ideal: The Overview opens with a verdict computed from the exact same live model as every row beneath it — "Good morning. Two things need you." — where "two things" is a door to the attention list, each elaboration clause anchors to its evidence (the approval, the stale butler, the issue group), and the prose re-writes itself within a heartbeat of the fleet changing because headline, KPI strip, butler index, and Now column all consume one canonical server verdict (activity verb + cadence expectation) patched by the event bus in the same frame. The attention list is the only place a signal appears (no triple-rendering across KPI/Now/attention), every row is one keystroke from root evidence (j/k roving focus, enter to drill, a/d/x to decide with a 5-second undo toast identical to /approvals), and every decision applies optimistically with visible rollback. Failure states name themselves in the row where the data would have been — a dead spend source is an em-dash captioned "spend source unreachable", never $0.00 — and the entire page, cost surface included, speaks one Dispatch dialect: hairline rules, mono eyebrows, serif voice, no cards, so the owner verifies fleet health in five seconds, clears the queue in under a minute, and never wonders whether the calm is earned or fabricated.

findings.title: Restore succeeds but the board keeps showing QUARANTINED for up to 30s
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-general.ts:57-59 — useSetEligibility's onSuccess invalidates only ["switchboard-registry"], a key the board never consumes (board key is ["butlers","board"], use-butler-status-board.ts:189). ButlersPage.tsx:133-144 fires the mutation and toasts "restored", but no invalidation, no optimistic patch, and no fleet-bus event type covers eligibility transitions (event-cache-registry.ts:148-156 has session/approval/spend/... but no eligibility/registry type), so the red rail + QUARANTINED chip persist until the next 30s poll while the toast claims success.
findings.detail: Direct violation of 'every owner action applies in the same frame'. After the 5s undo window elapses and the mutation succeeds, isRestorePending goes false and the chip reverts to QUARANTINED (stale cache), inviting a second restore click. Fix is one line of invalidation plus an optimistic row patch; the streaming half is an 'eligibility' event type on the bus so server-side quarantines also arrive live instead of on poll.

findings.title: "All N butlers healthy" renders when liveness is unknowable — error impersonating health
findings.evidence: Backend rule 3 maps heartbeat-unavailable rows to activity="unknown" (src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py:568-569; heartbeat_unavailable = registry_source_error OR schema_unreachable, line 643). The frontend's needs-you filter excludes "unknown" (use-butler-status-board.ts:174 NEEDS_YOU_ACTIVITIES = offline|quarantined|overdue), so when the switchboard registry query fails fleet-wide (butlers.py:790-792) every row is unknown, needsYou is empty, and NeedsYouStrip.tsx:59-67 renders the calm all-clear line "All N butlers healthy".
findings.detail: The board's lead judgment line asserts health it cannot prove, directly contradicting the amber sources-degraded pill in the same header. Same failure per-entry: one butler with schema_unreachable disappears from the strip entirely (its chip shows "—" in the grid, but the verdict line still says all healthy). The all-clear must be gated on zero unknown rows and zero source errors, and unknown rows should surface as 'N unverifiable (registry down)'.

findings.title: Hourly-stripe query failure fabricates a confident zero-activity stripe and SESS·24H = 0
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py:497-503 — _fetch_board_hourly_stripe swallows any exception and returns ([0]*24, 0) with no degradation flag. schema_unreachable is only set by pool KeyError or the two session queries (lines 616-641); if those succeed but the stripe query times out, the row ships hourly_total=0 and an all-zero stripe. StatusBoardCell.tsx:281-284 then renders SESS 24H as a confident "0" and ActivityStripe paints 24 empty cells; the zeros also fold into aggregates.total_sessions_24h (butlers.py:731) shown in BoardFooter.
findings.detail: Classic errors-impersonating-empty, one layer below the truth-marking the epic added. The UI already has the honest affordance ('data unavailable', StatusBoardCell.tsx:324-333) — it just never fires for this failure mode because the backend collapses it to zeros. Needs a per-row stripe_unavailable flag instead of zero-fill.

findings.title: scheduled_tasks query failure fabricates an OVERDUE alarm via the 5-minute fallback
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py:480-488 — _fetch_enabled_crons degrades any query failure to [], indistinguishable from 'butler has no cron schedule'. cadence_seconds becomes None and line 672 applies the 5-minute _DEFAULT_STALE_SECONDS rule, so a weekly-cadence butler whose scheduled_tasks query timed out is flagged activity="overdue"/amber and pushed into the needs-you strip after 5 minutes of ordinary silence.
findings.detail: A transient DB timeout manufactures a false 'needs you' alarm — the inverse of finding 3 and equally corrosive to earned calm (false alarms train the owner to ignore the strip). Query failure must yield cadence_status="unknown" (a state the model already has, line 664), not the no-schedule fallback.

findings.title: Header pill counts overdue and unknown butlers as "healthy", contradicting the strip beside it
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butlers/BoardHeader.tsx:36-38 — healthyCount = total - offline - quarantined, so overdue and unknown rows count as healthy; pillDotClass (lines 50-55) shows a green dot when healthy===total. With 2 butlers overdue, the header renders a green "14/14 reporting" (aria-label "14 of 14 reporting healthy", line 110) directly above a strip saying "2 things need you". Also pillDotClass returns green for total===0 (line 51) — an empty fleet reads healthy.
findings.detail: Two verdicts on one header disagree. Either the pill should subtract overdue/unknown, or its copy should honestly claim only liveness ('14/14 reachable') and cede the health verdict to the strip.

findings.title: Board ignores the canonical cell_tone it was consolidated onto, and re-derives state colors in a fourth dialect
findings.evidence: GET /api/butlers/board is documented as THE single source of activity/cell_tone "for every butler-status surface" (butlers.py:283-288), but cell_tone's only consumer is SystemPage.tsx:77 — StatusBoardCell.tsx re-derives chip color from activity (lines 51-66) and rail color from eligibility (lines 106-113) via local maps, using Tailwind stock palette (text-emerald-600, bg-emerald-500, bg-amber-500, text-destructive) while BoardHeader's dot uses bg-green-500 (BoardHeader.tsx:51-54) — two different greens for 'healthy' on one page, and none of them the spec's exactly-three tokens --red/--amber/--green (openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:81-88, defined in index.css:78-127).
findings.detail: Residue of bu-86c4c.17: the consolidation landed for data but the verdict-to-color mapping is still duplicated client-side on the board's home surface, and the status dots bypass the spec-mandated StateDot primitive (spec.md:261). The in-flight bu-86c4c.6 lint would catch the raw-palette classes but not the ignored cell_tone contract — consuming the server tone is the structural fix that makes drift impossible.

findings.title: Degradation is signaled by an unexplained amber dot but never names itself; overdue/unknown counts computed and rendered nowhere
findings.evidence: The hook exposes overdue, eligibilityUnavailable, hasPerEntryErrors, heartbeatSourceError, registrySourceError (use-butler-status-board.ts:98-119), yet grep shows zero /butlers renderers — BoardFooter.tsx:109-146 renders only ACTIVE/OFFLINE/QUARANTINED/SESSIONS/SPEND/AVG LOAD (no OVERDUE, no UNKNOWN cell) and its sole SourceDegradedNote covers the cost source (lines 155-161). A registry outage or per-entry schema failure surfaces only as the header pill flipping amber (BoardHeader.tsx:50-55) with no text anywhere naming which source degraded.
findings.detail: Violates 'every degraded source names itself'. /system has SystemVerdictBanner naming these conditions; the roster board — the surface the owner actually triages from — has an amber dot and silence. Footer stat cells are also inert divs (no drill-down; bu-9d5vp covers RuntimeSummaryKpi, not this footer).

findings.title: No page-scoped keyboard or palette surface for the board's own queue
findings.evidence: ButlersPage.tsx registers zero commands (no useRegisterCommands anywhere under components/butlers/ or the page — grep shows only ApprovalsPage/IssuesPage register page commands); GlobalActionsRegistrar.tsx offers only "Trigger <butler>". The needs-you strip rows are plain links (NeedsYouStrip.tsx:78-85) and the grid is tab-order only — no j/k or arrow traversal, no 'jump to first needs-you', and a quarantined butler cannot be restored from the palette.
findings.detail: North star: clear the queue in under a minute without touching the mouse, one command palette from a single registry. Distinct from in-flight bu-86c4c.15 (inline remedy verbs on signals): this is the navigation/palette half — reaching and traversing the queue by keyboard. Today the fastest keyboard path to restore is ~N tabs through cells to find the chip.

audits.jarvis_gap: The board is genuinely close: one round-trip canonical liveness, a needs-you strip that leads, undoable restore, stable roster order, honest '—' chips for per-row outages. What separates it from JARVIS-grade is verdict integrity at the edges and closure of the act loop: the one owner action on the page (restore) doesn't reflect in the same frame; the lead judgment line can assert 'all healthy' precisely when the system cannot know; two backend fetch failures still fabricate calm zeros or false OVERDUE alarms instead of naming themselves; the header pill, strip, and footer can render three disagreeing verdicts at once; and the canonical cell_tone contract the consolidation shipped is unconsumed on its own home surface, leaving color semantics re-derived in stock-Tailwind dialect. Eligibility state changes are also the only liveness transition that never streams — everything else rides the event bus while quarantine/restore waits for the poll.
audits.ideal: The board opens with a single Dispatch-voice verdict sentence that is provably derived — "All 14 healthy" only when every row's liveness is verified, otherwise "12 healthy, finance silent 3d against a daily cadence, registry unreachable for 2" — where every clause links to its butler or its degraded source. Below it, the grid renders each tile's rail, chip, and tone from the server's one canonical cell_tone in the spec's three state tokens, with unknown rendered as loudly as offline. Quarantine and restore are events on the fleet bus: an owner pressing r on a strip row (or invoking "Restore finance" from the palette) sees the tile flip to eligible in the same frame with a 5s undo, and a server-side quarantine appears within a heartbeat, not a poll. Every count in the footer is a door — OFFLINE:2 filters the grid — and every fetch failure anywhere in the pipeline names itself as a source note rather than shipping a zero, so a calm board is always an earned verdict, never a default.

moves.title: Same-frame restore: optimistic board patch + eligibility events on the fleet bus
moves.why: The board's only owner action currently lies for up to 30s after succeeding (finding 1), and eligibility is the sole liveness transition with no stream path — the exact 'applies in the same frame' and 'live event stream' clauses of the north star.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/hooks/use-general.ts (useSetEligibility onMutate/onSuccess: optimistic patch of ["butlers","board"] row eligibility/activity/cell_tone + invalidate), frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts (new 'eligibility' patch entry), src/butlers/api/routers/events.py EVENT_TYPES + emit on quarantine/restore writes to switchboard.butler_registry.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1 (S): invalidate + optimistic patch in useSetEligibility — fixes the visible lie with no backend change. Slice 2 (M): backend eligibility event emission + registry cache-patch entry so server-side quarantines stream to board and timeline.

moves.title: Truthful all-clear: gate the calm line on proven health and name every degraded source on-board
moves.why: Findings 2, 5, 7: the strip can claim 'All N healthy' during a registry outage, the pill counts overdue/unknown as healthy, and degradation is an unexplained amber dot. The lead verdict must be earned or absent.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/butlers/NeedsYouStrip.tsx (all-clear branch requires zero unknown rows and !sourcesPartiallyDegraded; add 'N unverifiable — <source> unreachable' line), BoardHeader.tsx healthyCount/pillDotClass (subtract overdue+unknown or reword to 'reachable'), BoardFooter.tsx (add OVERDUE and UNKNOWN stat cells from already-computed aggregates; SourceDegradedNote for registry/per-entry errors mirroring the existing cost note).
moves.slice_plan: One PR: all fields already exist in StatusBoardAggregates — this is pure rendering of computed-but-dropped truth.

moves.title: Kill the last two zero-fabrication paths in the board endpoint
moves.why: Findings 3 and 4: stripe-query failure ships a confident empty stripe and SESS·24H=0; cron-query failure manufactures a false OVERDUE alarm via the 5-min fallback. Both violate 'no failed fetch ever impersonates an empty queue' one layer below where the epic's truth amnesty stopped.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py:_fetch_board_hourly_stripe (return availability flag instead of zeros; wire to BoardRow, distinct from schema_unreachable), _fetch_enabled_crons (distinguish query-failure → cadence_status='unknown' from genuinely-no-schedule → 5-min rule), use-butler-status-board.ts mapRow, StatusBoardCell already renders the 'data unavailable' branch.

audits.jarvis_gap: Post-.18 the butler console has one coherent tab vocabulary, a unified run verb, and real doors on the activity stripe and event rows — the architecture is right. What separates it from JARVIS-grade is truthfulness under failure and voice: the Overview KPI row fabricates calm ("$0.00", "nothing pending", a flat 24-bar stripe) whenever its sources fail, the Activity analytics "Errors" KPI is structurally always zero because it counts a trigger_source value that cannot exist, and the surface opens with a raw KPI grid instead of a synthesized per-butler verdict (the judgment layer landed only on /system). The console also still makes the owner leave it: Run navigates away to /sessions/:id, the 5-event recent feed has no door to the fleet chronicle (which isn't URL-addressable by butler anyway), and none of the page's verbs are registered in the command palette.

findings.title: Activity analytics 'Errors' KPI is fabricated — it can never be nonzero
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerActivityTab.tsx:301-307 derives errorsCount from session kinds where kind === "error", but kinds are GROUP BY trigger_source (src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:564-568) and the valid trigger_source vocabulary is {tick, external, trigger, route, healing, dashboard, qa} + schedule:/deadline: prefixes (src/butlers/core/sessions.py:25) — "error" is not a possible value. Real failures live in the sessions `success IS FALSE` column (src/butlers/api/read_models/sessions_v1.py:390 already computes failed_count).
findings.detail: The KPI confidently renders '0 errors' regardless of how many sessions actually failed, and the code comment even asserts 'zero errors is the correct interpretation'. This is the purest 'fabricated number' sin on the surface: the owner's five-second health read on a butler is answered with a metric that is hardwired to say fine. Fix: expose failed_count (success IS FALSE) from the read model on the session-kinds or latency-stats endpoint and wire the KPI to it; make a nonzero value a door to sessions filtered to failures.

findings.detail: Violates the state contract landed in bu-86c4c.2 on this page's own opening row: a failed spend fetch impersonates a free day, a failed approvals fetch impersonates an empty queue (the panel below it correctly shows ErrorLine, so the KPI and its detail panel can actively contradict each other), and a failed status board impersonates a silent butler. audits.ideal: The ideal /butlers/:name opens with one sentence the system wrote itself, in the Dispatch serif voice: "Nominal. Six ticks on schedule, $0.41 spent, one approval waiting — expires in 3h." Every clause is a door (ticks → sessions filtered to today, spend → Spend tab, approval → that approval's dossier), and when any input to that sentence is degraded the sentence says so by name instead of rounding to calm. Below it, the same KPI grid — but every cell is a door, every number provably sourced, the Errors count wired to real success=false sessions and red only when true. The command bar is the butler's throat: typing a prompt and hitting Enter spawns a session that streams live into a drawer on this same screen, the owner watching tool calls land without ever leaving the console; Cmd+K carries every verb on the page (pause with quarantine reason shown, resume, run, jump to any tab or System section) so the whole detect→diagnose→act loop is keyboard-complete. The recent feed ends in a door to the fleet chronicle pre-scoped to this butler via a URL-addressable filter, making the butler console a lens over the One Timeline rather than a silo. Failure anywhere — board, spend, approvals, sessions — renders as a named, dated degradation line in the exact spot the number would have been, so the owner's trust in every figure that does render stays absolute.

audits.ideal: /sessions opens with a one-line synthesized verdict in Dispatch voice — "212 sessions since midnight, 96% ok; the 8 failures cluster in finance's 06:00 cron, all the same expired-token stderr" — where every clause is a filter link, sitting above the window-true KPI strip and butler-hued stripe chart that already exist. A running session's dossier is alive: elapsed time ticks, tool calls append as the fleet bus streams them, and the moment the session ends the verdict line rewrites itself — so "ask a butler, watch it work, read why it failed, retry" completes on one screen without touching the mouse.

audits.jarvis_gap: The .10/.9 rebuild is real and holds: server-side heartbeat classification, honest per-source degraded_sources, keyset pagination with SQL-level error filtering, WS-invalidated live tail with an unpin-safe "N new events" pill, and a typed drawer with no raw JSON. It moves the surface from weak to solid. What separates it from JARVIS-grade: the URL contract is half-built (drawer is URL-backed, filters are not, and a shared ?event link silently renders nothing); a dead API after first paint impersonates a calm idle fleet; notification rows dead-end at a generic list; trace_id — which sessions already persist — never reaches the timeline event, so the chronicle is not on the trace-id spine; and the rows speak a fourth and fifth color outside the three-state Dispatch vocabulary while butler identity is plain text instead of the ButlerMark. Action failures (Load older, Save view) fail silently to console. No synthesized verdict opens the page (attention strip is filed as bu-ddo0n; the editorial verdict line above it is not).

findings.title: Dead API after first paint impersonates a quiet fleet
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-timeline-ledger.ts:131-133 — isError is only true when events.length === 0; use-timeline.ts placeholderData keeps the previous page forever. Once any page has rendered, every subsequent head-poll failure is invisible: rows freeze, LiveStatusBadge (live-status-badge.tsx:53-56) decays to plain 'Idle' — indistinguishable from a genuinely quiet fleet. degraded_sources only covers per-source SQL failure inside a successful response, not total fetch failure.
findings.detail: This is the errors-impersonating-empty sin in its stale-data form: the owner reads calm where the console has actually lost its feed. The surface already has the degraded-banner slot (TimelinePage.tsx:176-184); a 'stream stale since HH:MM — retry' strip when head.isError && events.length > 0 closes it. Additionally, while unpinned the badge computes freshness from the committed snapshot's first event (TimelinePage.tsx:162), so 'Idle' can render directly above a pill counting live arrivals — two contradictory liveness signals on one screen.

findings.title: Half-built URL contract: filters unshareable, ?event deep links silently render nothing
findings.evidence: TimelinePage.tsx:76-78 — selectedButlers/selectedTypes/activeViewId are plain useState (no useSearchParams), while the drawer IS URL-backed via useEventDrawerState (?event=<id>). TimelineLedger.tsx:302-311 renders the drawer only inline under a matching loaded row, so a reloaded or shared ?event URL whose event is not in the newest 50 (pushed off by new arrivals, or filtered out) shows a plain timeline with zero indication anything was requested.
findings.detail: The donor ledger this page was rebuilt on URL-backs its range/filters (TimelineTab.tsx:1091,1131 'URL-backed'); the rebuild adopted the drawer param but dropped filter persistence — a refresh resets every facet and the drawer param survives without its context. Drill-down dead end: the one URL the system hands the owner for 'this exact event' is only valid for ~one page-turn of time.

findings.title: Row type dots speak a 4th and 5th color outside the three-state Dispatch vocabulary; butler identity is bare text, not the ButlerMark

audits.ideal: The fleet chronicle opens with one synthesized editorial line above the stream — "Quiet afternoon: 41 sessions across 9 butlers, one failed delivery to Telegram needs retry" — where every clause is a live link (the attention strip of bu-ddo0n supplies the triage rows; the verdict sentence above it is the judgment layer). The stream itself is the honest ledger it already nearly is: hour groups, hairline rows, live tail with the N-new pill — but every piece of view state (facets, butlers, view, drawer, scroll anchor) lives in the URL so any moment is shareable and restorable, and a ?event deep link either finds its row or says plainly "this event is older than the loaded view — jump to its hour". Every row is on the trace-id spine: session and error rows carry trace_id through to the transcript and back to the originating ingestion event; notification rows land on their exact delivery record with the retry verb inline (bu-6t8ix). Failure never impersonates calm — a dead poll paints a "stream stale since 14:32 — retry" strip in the same slot the degraded-sources banner already owns. Rows speak pure Dispatch: neutral mono type words, state color only on genuine failure, the ButlerMark as the only hue. Heartbeats are excludable at the server, and the whole surface is keyboard-first (j/k/enter, / to filter — bu-ddo0n) under the one command palette.

But the surface is still a passive legacy-dialect card list, not the fleet's triage inbox: a grouped issue ("Seen 47x") can never be opened to its 47 occurrences anywhere in the product (the audit-log API has no result/error-group predicate), a dead butler still raises no badge outside the page, every fetch live-pings the whole fleet inline (page stalls ~10s exactly when a butler is down), acking an unreachable issue silently bounces back within one poll, there is no verdict line, no time window, no keyboard triage loop, and none of the Dispatch primitives (Row/StateDot/ButlerMark/Mono) that now exist are used here. Detect works; diagnose dead-ends one hop in; act is partial.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: issue groups still have no path to their root evidence — drill-down dead-ends one hop in
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/audit_grouping.py:199-204 builds the link from only actor (single-butler) and action=session (scheduled): a multi-butler warning group emits bare /audit-log with zero predicates; even the best case (actor=X&action=session) lands on ALL of that butler's session rows, successes included, not this group's occurrences. The audit-log API cannot scope tighter: src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:291-316 accepts only offset/limit/since/actor/action/key/kind — no result=error, no error-signature predicate. Meanwhile IssuesPanel.tsx:149 renders only the one-line description; issue.error_message, issue.type, and the per-butler breakdown (issue.butlers) are in the payload but never rendered and there is no row expansion.
findings.detail: "Seen 47x · First … · Last …" is a claim the owner can never verify: no surface in the product can list those 47 occurrences or reach the failing session/trace from them. This is the exact defect class bu-86c4c.4 fixed elsewhere (real anchors with full predicates) but the issues→evidence hop needs a backend predicate that was never added, and it is NOT covered by bu-9d5vp (that bead covers KPI cells, egress actors, audit request_id, spend rules, message threads). Fix needs either GET /api/audit-log?result=error&group=<signature> or GET /api/issues/{issue_key}/occurrences reusing the shared CTE, plus inline row expansion (DisclosureRow) showing full error text, ButlerMark chips per affected butler, and session/request_id links into the trace spine.

findings.title: Acknowledging a live 'unreachable' issue silently bounces back within one poll — the control lies
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:212-222 stamps reachability issues with first_seen_at = last_seen_at = datetime.now(UTC) on EVERY fetch; the frontend acks with that timestamp as the recurrence watermark (use-issues.ts DismissIssueVariables); _still_acked (issues.py:95-111) then finds last_seen_at > watermark on the very next fetch and un-acks it. The optimistic cache removal (use-issues.ts) makes the button look like it worked.
findings.detail: For an ongoing condition the ack is a no-op with a ≤5-minute fuse: the issue vanishes, then reappears with no explanation — and because it is no longer 'still acked' it does not even appear under Show acknowledged for restore. Acknowledge-until-recurrence semantics are right for event groups but wrong for live conditions; unreachable issues need explicit snooze durations (1h / 24h / until-recovery) or an 'acknowledged while down' state, plus a 'recurred after ack' marker when a group resurfaces.

findings.title: Every issues fetch live-pings the entire fleet inline — the page stalls precisely when a butler is down
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:32 (_STATUS_TIMEOUT_S = 5.0), :141-170 (per-butler get_client + ping, each with a 5s timeout, retry loop), :205-210 (asyncio.gather over all butlers on every GET /api/issues — including the include_dismissed=true view, so toggling 'Show acknowledged' re-pings the fleet). Frontend refetch paths: use-issues.ts polls every 5 min, the event bus invalidates ["issues"] on every audit error, and both dismiss/undismiss invalidate both views.
findings.detail: When any butler is down (the moment this page matters most) initial load blocks ~5-10s behind a skeleton, and every ack/restore triggers another fleet-wide ping storm as its invalidation settles. Reachability should be a cached background watcher (daemon-side or a ~15s in-process cache with event-bus push on transitions) so GET /api/issues reads state in milliseconds and can carry an honest 'checked Ns ago' provenance stamp.

findings.title: Keyboard triage is absent, and the one palette command acks an unnamed issue blind
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/IssuesPage.tsx:75-88 registers a single 'Acknowledge issue' command that silently acks issues[0] (whatever is newest at that instant) with no preview of which issue it will ack; IssuesPanel.tsx:196-204 uses one global isDismissing flag that disables EVERY row's Acknowledge while one ack is in flight, serializing bulk triage; use-issues.ts wires no onError/onSuccess feedback, so a failed ack silently rolls back (the row reappears looking like a UI glitch) and a successful ack has no undo toast.
findings.detail: The north star is 'clears that queue in under a minute without touching the mouse'. bu-86c4c.14 delivered keyboard triage on /approvals only; the same loop is missing here: no j/k roving row focus, no e=acknowledge / o=open-evidence / u=undo, and the palette command performs a state change on an item the owner cannot see. Per-row pending keyed by issue_key, an undo toast (undismiss already exists as the inverse), and focused-row-scoped commands are all straightforward with existing pieces.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: unbounded all-time aggregation with zero triage tools — stale groups live in 'active' forever
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/issues.py:64 calls build_audit_group_query() with no where_extra and no limit — a full-table grouping scan of public.audit_log on every fetch (and every 5-min poll and event-bus invalidation); audit_grouping.py:22 explicitly says 'Callers apply their own window/LIMIT constraints' and this caller applies none. audits.ideal: /issues is the fleet's triage inbox and reads in the same Dispatch hand as the rest of the console. It opens with a one-line synthesized verdict in the editorial voice ("2 critical — pantry unreachable 43m, ping failing; 3 warning groups, none new since Tuesday") over a summary strip (N critical / N warning / last change), and the shell badges the critical count so the owner only visits when pulled. Below, a severity-first ledger of grouped signals built on Row/StateDot/ButlerMark/Mono: red/amber dots, mono error signatures, butler chips that link, occurrence sparklines, a default 7-day window with range toggle and severity/butler pills. Every row is a door: expand inline to the group's actual occurrences (full error text, per-butler breakdown, each occurrence carrying its session/request_id into the trace spine) and every issue type carries its remedy verb on the row — ping, run schedule now, open session. Reachability is a cached live stream with a "checked 12s ago" provenance stamp, so the page renders in milliseconds even mid-outage. Acknowledgement is a triage state, not a mute: event groups resurface flagged "recurred after ack," live conditions get explicit snooze durations, every ack is one keystroke with an undo toast, and j/k + e/o clears the whole queue mouse-free in under a minute. Nothing is claimed that cannot be opened; nothing stalls; silence genuinely means health.

audits.jarvis_gap: The audit log is the fleet's ledger of record, but it opens as a raw, noise-dominated data dump instead of a judgment: no synthesized verdict, heartbeat rows drowning privileged actions, and — the deepest cut — the outcome of every audited operation (result/error/metadata, persisted since core_122) is deliberately withheld from the reader, so the one surface meant to prove what the system did cannot say whether any action succeeded. Filters are exact-match text fields that fire per keystroke and produce lying empty states, a URL deep-link silently overrides the visible filter input, the expanded detail row renders at the bottom of the table instead of under the clicked row, and the page has no live-event path, no palette commands, and none of the Dispatch dialect that its sibling Trust Console reel already speaks.

audits.ideal: The audit log opens as the household's ledger of record in full Dispatch voice: a serif lede synthesizes the period ("Eleven privileged actions since yesterday — two failed, both messenger webhook rotations; heartbeats nominal") with every clause a live link into the pre-filtered view it describes. The default lens is privileged actions with an outcome column in the three state colors; heartbeat/GET noise sits behind a labeled toggle that names its count. Every row is a keyboard-operable disclosure that expands in place to show note, IP, request_id (linked to its trace), structured metadata, and — for failures — the error text plus a one-keystroke jump to the matching /issues group and the remedy verb. Filters are honest facets: actor and action are typeahead menus fed by the ledger's own distinct values, matching as you type against known vocabulary so an empty result always means "zero such entries"; all filter state (actor, action, since, kind, key, cursor) lives in the URL, so any slice is shareable, palette-addressable, and restored on refresh. New rows arrive over the fleet event bus and slide in live under keyset pagination that never shifts under the reader; every arriving failure pulses once in the state color and settles. Nothing is withheld: what the system recorded is exactly what the owner sees.

moves.slice_plan: 1) Emit a lightweight 'audit' event from append() for all rows (throttle/batch heartbeat-class actions server-side); 2) add an auditPatch to event-cache-registry invalidating ['audit-log'] (and have issuePatch invalidate it too as an interim S-sized slice); 3) convert the endpoint to cursor pagination (ts DESC, id DESC — the house convention from /api/ingestion/events), dropping the per-fetch COUNT(*); keep offset accepted during transition only if trivial, else remove (compat waived).
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py (append + list), src/butlers/api/routers/events.py, frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts, frontend/src/hooks/use-audit-log.ts, frontend/src/pages/AuditLogPage.tsx pagination controls

audits.jarvis_gap: The Trust Console's forward path (pending queue → dossier → decide, ranked by expiry+blast radius, keyboard triage with undo window, per-approval URLs, autonomy ledger with revoke) landed and holds. What is missing is the backward half of trust and the last mile of honesty: a decided approval's dossier cannot prove who decided it, when, why it was denied, or what actually happened when it ran (execution_result never reaches the detail endpoint; deny reason is string-mangled into decided_by and never rendered); the queue can silently render a partial fleet as a complete one; the autonomy-suggestions strip renders fetch errors as nothing; and the page's own defining keyboard surface (j/k/a/d/x) is invisible — absent from the help sheet, absent from the page, with undo reachable only by mouse. The surface also opens with a static header instead of a synthesized verdict, and autonomy use-counts are numbers without doors.

findings.title: Decided dossier omits the decision itself — no decided_by, decided_at, deny reason, or execution result
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:660-830 (Dossier body renders title/why/evidence/proposed_action/target_contact only; no branch ever reads detail.decided_by or detail.decided_at) despite the History comment at ApprovalsPage.tsx:1103-1106 claiming "decided_by/decided_at shown". Backend: _pending_action_to_detail (src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:273-302) omits execution_result entirely (ApprovalDetail in frontend/src/api/types.ts:2751-2778 has no field for it), and the deny reason is HTML-escaped and concatenated into decided_by as "human:… (reason: …)" (src/butlers/modules/approvals/operations.py:267-270) — unrecoverable as structured data.
findings.detail: History rows advertise auditability ("every decided approval opens its read-only dossier"), but the drill-down dead-ends one hop before the evidence: the owner sees the proposal, a colored status word, and nothing else — not who decided (human vs system:expiry vs auto-rule), not when, not the reason they themselves typed into the deny box, not whether the executed tool call succeeded or what it returned. For a page whose charter is "trust is never invisible", the decision record is the one thing it cannot show. Requires adding execution_result + parsed reason to the detail payload and a Decision section in the Dossier; reason should move out of the decided_by string into its own column.

findings.title: Partial-fleet aggregation impersonates a complete queue — per-butler pool failures swallowed with no degraded marker
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1546-1548 (list_approvals_flat: `except Exception: logger.warning("Failed to query pending_actions for flat list")` then continues and returns 200 with the remaining butlers' rows) and approvals.py:1608 (list_approvals_history, same pattern). The response envelope (ApiResponse[list[ApprovalSummary]]) carries no sources_degraded/aggregates_available field; frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1431-1447 therefore renders a partial queue — or "No pending approvals." — indistinguishably from a healthy empty one.
findings.detail: The truth-amnesty child (.1) fixed fetch-level errors (QueryBoundary checks isError before isEmpty), but this is one layer deeper: the fetch succeeds while N of 9 butler schemas silently failed to answer. An approval waiting in a broken butler's schema vanishes from the console with zero indication — the exact 'failed fetch impersonating an empty queue' the north star forbids, moved server-side. Fix mirrors the ingestion degraded-mode convention: return the list plus `sources_degraded: [butler,…]`, and render a named-source warning strip above the rail.

findings.title: Autonomy-suggestions strip renders fetch errors as nothing — error impersonates empty on the autonomy-promotion surface
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1144-1161: `const { data } = useAutonomySuggestions(...); const suggestions = data?.data ?? []; if (suggestions.length === 0) return null;` — isError/isLoading are never read, on the same page that uses QueryBoundary three times, and in direct violation of the contract documented in frontend/src/components/ui/query-boundary.tsx:16-20 ("a query that has ERRORED must never fall through to the empty branch").
findings.detail: When GET /autonomy-suggestions fails, the banner silently disappears; pending promotion/demotion suggestions — decisions the fleet is waiting on to expand or contract its own autonomy — are hidden with no degraded-source naming. Because the section is invisible-when-empty by design, the error state needs a distinct minimal treatment (a one-line named-source failure row), not a full empty-state.

findings.title: The page's defining keyboard surface is undiscoverable, its undo is mouse-only, and the palette 'Approve next' bypasses the undo window
findings.evidence: j/k/a/d/x are bound in ApprovalsPage.tsx:1332-1374 but: (1) the ? help sheet lists only static rows + g-chords generated from the route registry (frontend/src/components/ui/shortcut-hints.tsx:19-41) — no mechanism exists for page-scoped shortcut rows, so triage keys appear nowhere; (2) no hint text anywhere in ApprovalsPage's rendered output mentions them; (3) undoing a scheduled decision requires clicking the sonner toast action or the dimmed rail row (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1321-1324, 364-369) — no key (u/Esc/z) cancels, and focus has already advanced to the next item (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1379-1388); (4) the command-palette entry "Approve next" (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1400-1411) calls approveMut.mutate(effectiveSelected) directly — it approves the CURRENT selection, not the next item, and fires instantly with no undo window, unlike the keyboard 'a' it shadows; Deny/Defer have no palette entries at all.
findings.detail: The north star is clearing the queue in under a minute without the mouse. The keys exist but only a code-reader knows them; the one recovery affordance in a blind-fire flow is the only step that demands the mouse; and the palette variant of the same verb silently drops the safety net and mislabels its target. Fix: a useRegisterShortcuts() page-scoped registry feeding ShortcutHints (mirror of the command registry from .7), a one-line mono hint in the rail footer, a u/Esc binding for 'undo last scheduled decision', and palette approve routed through scheduleDecision with an honest label.

findings.title: Dossier error branch is off the page's own state contract — bare dead-end with no retry, no alert role, no 404-vs-network distinction
findings.evidence:
frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:483-489: `if (error || !data?.data) return
failed to load dossier
` — plain muted text, no QueryBoundary, no onRetry, no role="alert", no sourceLabel, and a 404 (pruned/foreign id from a stale notification or bookmark — the exact deep-link entry the per-approval URLs were built for) renders identically to a network failure.
findings.detail: The rest of the page adopted the bu-86c4c.2 contract (QueryBoundary with retry + role=alert); the center pane — the surface a Telegram notification deep-links into — did not. A stale /approvals/:id link should say "this approval no longer exists — it may have expired or been decided" with a door to History; a network failure should say the source and offer Retry.

findings.title: Autonomy ledger use-counts and provenance are numbers without doors — no drill-down from a rule to the actions it auto-approved
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/approvals/autonomy-panel.tsx:88-94 renders `{rule.use_count} uses` as inert text; ApprovalRule.created_from (frontend/src/api/types.ts:2804) is never rendered or linked; ApprovalAction.approval_rule_id exists (types.ts:2725) but no endpoint or UI filters history by rule (list_approvals_history at src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1561-1608 supports only since/limit).
findings.detail: The panel's charter is "every active standing rule, its live use count" — but 'this rule fired 7 times' cannot be verified: the owner cannot see the 7 actions, so the number is a claim without evidence (drill-down dead end, sin #3). created_from likewise never links back to the originating approval dossier. Needs a rule_id filter on the history endpoint plus links from the count and from created_from. Distinct from bu-9d5vp (dashboard KPI cells / egress / audit request_id / spend rule links — none touch the autonomy panel).

findings.title: Stalled approvals (approved-but-never-dispatched) silently fall off the console after 30 newer decisions
findings.evidence: _WAITING_STATUSES = {"pending"} (src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1500) keeps stalled 'approved' actions out of the rail; their only surface is HistorySection's fixed last-30 fetch (frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1061-1067, getApprovalsHistory(undefined, 30)) ordered by decided_at DESC with no status filter, no pagination, and no way to load more.
findings.detail: The page invests heavily in stalled honesty — amber-never-green statusColor (ApprovalsPage.tsx:164-179), the 'stalled' relabel, an inline Retry dispatch verb — yet a stalled approval from two days ago drops off the visible last-30 window and then exists nowhere on the console. An action the owner approved that never ran is arguably the single most attention-worthy state the page owns; it belongs in the actionable queue (rail, ranked above fresh pendings) or a dedicated stalled strip, not the history tail.

findings.title: Expiry countdowns never tick and the rail's ranking rationale is invisible
findings.evidence: expiryCountdown (frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:229-245) is computed once per render with no interval; the page's only guaranteed re-render sources are stream events and the 5-minute reconciliation refetch (ApprovalsPage.tsx:1211-1218), so a chip reading "expires in 3m" can sit unchanged past the actual expiry. rankScore's blast-radius component (ApprovalsPage.tsx:196-227) reorders the rail by a keyword heuristic (notify/send/delete → tier 3) but no row shows why it ranked where it did — only the countdown is visible.
findings.detail: A countdown that does not count is a small fabrication: the number was true at render time and quietly stops being true. A 30s interval re-render (or a deadline-scheduled one) fixes it. Separately, the owner cannot see the 'blast radius' half of the ranking — an 'outbound' / 'internal write' eyebrow chip on rail rows would make the sort self-explaining and expose misclassifications of the regex heuristic instead of hiding them.

audits.ideal: The Trust Console opens with a one-line synthesized verdict in the Dispatch voice — "Three decisions waiting; the nearest expires in 40 minutes. One approved action never ran. The fleet acted unsupervised 12 times today under 4 standing rules." — and every clause is a door: waiting → the ranked rail, never-ran → the stalled item, 12 times → history filtered to auto-approvals, 4 rules → the autonomy ledger. The rail ranks by expiry and blast radius and says so on each row (an "outbound"/"internal" eyebrow beside a live-ticking countdown), and it names any butler whose queue could not be read rather than presenting a partial fleet as whole. The dossier is complete in both directions: pending, it shows why/evidence/entities with the floating decision cluster; decided, it shows the full verdict — who decided (human, expiry, or the named standing rule), when, the deny reason as first-class data, and the execution result with its error payload and an inline retry when dispatch failed. Triage is keyboard-complete and self-teaching: j/k/a/d/x/u are printed in the rail footer and the ? sheet via a page-scoped shortcut registry, undo is one keystroke, and the palette verbs share the same undo window as the keys. Every number on the surface is a door — a rule's use count opens the exact actions it authorized, created_from opens the approval that spawned the rule — and every fetch failure names itself, including the autonomy-suggestions strip, so the console's calm is earned rather than assumed.

moves.title: Complete the decision record: render verdict + execution result in the dossier
moves.why: The console's charter is provable trust, but /approvals/:id for a decided action shows the proposal and hides the decision — no decided_by/decided_at, no deny reason, no execution outcome. This is the highest-leverage honesty gap on the surface and the terminal hop of the drill-down spine (history row → dossier → nothing).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Backend: add execution_result, decided_by, decided_at (already present), and a structured `reason` to ApprovalDetail; migrate deny reason out of the decided_by string into its own column (operations.py reject_action), keeping a parse fallback for old rows. 2) Frontend: add a Decision section to Dossier (actor humanized — 'you', 'system: expiry', 'rule: <name>' linking to the autonomy panel; timestamp; reason in serif; execution result with success/error and the returned payload in mono), plus inline Retry dispatch when status=approved. 3) Tests: decided-dossier render for each terminal status.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:_pending_action_to_detail (273-302); src/butlers/modules/approvals/operations.py:reject_action (228-300, reason column); frontend/src/api/types.ts:ApprovalDetail (2751); frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx Dossier body (660-830) and the existing RetryDispatchButton (1026-1059).

moves.title: Honest aggregation: degraded-sources envelope on queue, history, and suggestions
moves.why: Two silent-partial paths (per-butler pool failures swallowed server-side; suggestions fetch error rendered as null) let a broken fleet impersonate a calm one — the exact defect class the north star names as the console's defining property.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Backend: collect failed butler names in list_approvals_flat/list_approvals_history and return `sources_degraded: [str]` alongside data (same 200-always convention as ingestion's aggregates_available). 2) Frontend: a named-source warning strip above the rail ('finance, health unreachable — queue may be incomplete') when non-empty. 3) AutonomySuggestionsSection: read isError and render a one-line role=alert failure row with retry instead of null.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:1507-1560 (flat), 1561-1608 (history); frontend/src/api/types.ts response envelopes; frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1144-1161 (suggestions), 1428-1477 (rail); pattern precedent in CLAUDE.md 'Degraded-Mode Response Envelope'.

moves.title: Keyboard-complete triage: page-scoped shortcut registry, undo key, palette parity
moves.why: The five-second triage loop exists but is a secret: no surface teaches j/k/a/d/x, undo demands the mouse, and the palette's 'Approve next' both mislabels its target and drops the undo window. This closes the 'clear the queue without touching the mouse' promise end-to-end.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add useRegisterShortcuts() mirroring the command registry (bu-86c4c.7) so pages contribute rows to ShortcutHints; register j/k/a/d/x/u here. 2) Print a one-line mono hint in the rail footer ('j/k move · a approve · d deny · x defer · u undo'). 3) Bind u (and Esc when nothing else owns it) to cancel the most recently scheduled decision. 4) Route the palette command through scheduleDecision, rename it 'Approve selected', and add Deny/Defer siblings.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/lib/command-registry.ts (pattern to mirror); frontend/src/components/ui/shortcut-hints.tsx:19-57; frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1308-1325 (scheduleDecision), 1332-1374 (key handler), 1400-1411 (palette); complements in-flight bu-86c4c.6/.15 without overlapping (neither touches shortcut discoverability).

moves.title: Trust verdict line: the console opens with judgment, every clause a door
moves.why: The judgment layer (.17) landed only on SystemPage; Approvals — the surface most explicitly about the owner's attention — opens with a static header. The metrics already exist server-side (get_metrics: pending count, auto-approval rate, expired today, active rules) and are already consumed elsewhere, so this is synthesis + wiring, not new data.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Compose a verdict line from getApprovalsFlat + getApprovalMetrics + stalled-approved count: 'N waiting; nearest expires in Xm. K approved actions never ran. The fleet acted autonomously M times today under R rules.' in the SystemVerdictBanner idiom (skeleton, all-clear, problems variants). 2) Wire each clause: waiting → rail focus, expiry → that approval's URL, never-ran → stalled strip/filter, M times → history filtered to rule-decided, R rules → autonomy panel. 3) Honesty rule: any clause whose source is degraded names itself or is omitted, never zero-filled.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/system/SystemVerdictBanner.tsx (idiom to reuse); src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:get_metrics (1358-1485); frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx header (1416-1421); depends on move 5's rule-filtered history for the 'M times' door.

moves.title: Every rule auditable: rule→uses and created_from drill-downs; stalled items rejoin the queue
moves.why: Autonomy is the console's highest-stakes ledger, yet its use counts are unverifiable claims and a stalled approval — the most attention-worthy state the page owns — falls off the visible surface after 30 newer decisions.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Backend: add rule_id and status filters to list_approvals_history (actions already carry approval_rule_id). 2) AutonomyPanel: use_count becomes a link opening History filtered to that rule; render created_from as a link to the originating approval's dossier. 3) Move stalled 'approved' items into the actionable surface: either include them in the waiting rail (rank tier above fresh pendings, amber, with Retry inline) or a dedicated 'never ran' strip pinned above History; either way they must never age out invisibly.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/api/routers/approvals.py:list_approvals_history (1561-1608) and _WAITING_STATUSES (1500); frontend/src/components/approvals/autonomy-panel.tsx:88-94; frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:HistorySection (1061-1130) and rankScore (223-227); distinct from bu-9d5vp's dashboard-scoped drill-down list.

audits.jarvis_gap: The calendar is the fleet's richest workspace — unified provider+butler projection, drag editing with undo ghosts, recurrence scopes, NL quick-add, find-time, conflict radar, cross-domain overlays, audit trail with session links — but it is a mouse-driven, polled, verdict-less surface. It opens with a date headline and an event count, not a judgment; everything that needs the owner (butler proposals, duplicates, conflicts, failed syncs) is hidden behind unbadged toggle pills or buried two clicks deep in a dialog; the page contributes zero verbs to the one command spine and has exactly one keydown handler in 6,472 lines; state arrives on 30–60s polls instead of the fleet event bus; and the overlay/briefing layer that fuses other butlers' knowledge into time is opt-in-per-URL, non-interactive, and a drill-down dead end. Detect works; diagnose and act require hunting.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: Zero keyboard surface — calendar registers no commands in the one command spine and has one keydown handler in 6,472 lines
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2017 is the ONLY keydown on the page (Enter inside the search input); grep confirms the page never imports src/lib/command-registry.tsx (the per-page verb API that ApprovalsPage.tsx and IssuesPage.tsx already use, built by bu-86c4c.7); the CalendarSearchPalette opens only via a mouse pill (line 4135); Today/prev/next (4217-4238), view/range pills (4188-4212), Create event (4160-4175), quick-add, find-time, sync are all mouse-only. The old dossier flagged this ("exactly one binding (calendar)"); the epic landed the global spine but no calendar verbs or keymap.
findings.detail: North star: clear the queue "without leaving the screen or touching the mouse." From Cmd+K you can navigate TO /calendar but cannot Create event, Quick add, Find time, Jump to today, or Search events. Grid drag create/move/resize additionally has no keyboard analogue, so the page's flagship interactions are pointer-exclusive.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: The needs-you queue is invisible — proposals, duplicates, and conflicts are fetched only after the owner manually opens their panels, with no counts anywhere
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2384-2390 (useCalendarProposals gated on `enabled: proposalsPanelOpen`), 2397-2401 (duplicates gated on panel open), toolbar pills at 4241-4292 render bare labels "Activity / Find time / Proposals / Duplicates" with no badge; conflict radar is enabled only on week/day (radarEnabled → conflictsAvailable, line 2322), so month and list ranges show no scheduling issues at all.
findings.detail: Butler-extracted event proposals awaiting accept/dismiss are the purest "what needs you" queue on this surface, and the owner cannot know any exist without clicking an unbadged pill. Violates "sees exactly what needs them" — the five-second health check is impossible here.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: Conflict radar's degraded mode impersonates a clean week
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/calendar/ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:160-163 — comment reads "Silent degraded mode and clean windows render nothing"; `if (!available || issues.length === 0 || dismissed) return null;`. When the conflicts read fails server-side (issues_available:false), the banner is byte-identical to "no conflicts."
findings.detail: Direct violation of the earned-calm contract ("no failed fetch ever impersonates an empty queue") and of the calendar's own shipped degraded-states convention (bu-5rmhbo, PR #2658) which mandates a visible 'context unavailable' rendering. The dossier flagged this at minor; on a safety surface (double-bookings) it is major.

findings.title: Calendar is not on the fleet event bus — state arrives by 30–60s polling, and butler-made mutations appear up to a minute late with no live signal
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:148-156 — EVENT_CACHE_REGISTRY covers approval/spend/session/notification/issue/ingestion/heartbeat only; no calendar event type. frontend/src/hooks/use-calendar-workspace.ts:108 (workspace refetchInterval 30_000), :134,:157,:201 (60_000 polls for meta/accounts/etc.); the page never imports use-event-stream.ts.
findings.detail: The bus (bu-86c4c.8) was built exactly so surfaces stop polling; the registry's own docs say adding a surface means one registry entry. A butler creating/moving an event via MCP, a sync completing, or an audit row landing should patch the workspace/conflicts/audit caches in the same frame — instead the grid is stale for up to 30s while the Live indicator claims the app is live.

findings.title: Overlay pills and briefing chips are drill-down dead ends — fused cross-domain signals cannot reach their root evidence
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:964-1000 — OverlayPill is documented and built as "Non-interactive context, so it renders as a static chip, not a button"; a finance bill overlay (with amount badge) has no path to /spend or the bill record, a travel leg no path to the trip, a relationship date no path to /entities. handleBriefingSelect (2692-2699) only navigates the grid to the chip's day. lib/calendar-overlays.ts contains no link/ref plumbing; the overlay contribution contract carries no target reference.
findings.detail: "Every clause of that prose is a door — one keystroke from any signal to its root evidence." The fusion layer (RFC-0020, epic bu-1ajgg9) surfaces other butlers' judgments into time but severs the trace spine at exactly the moment the owner wants to act on one. Not covered by bu-9d5vp (which lists dashboard KPI cells, egress actors, audit request_id, spend rules — not calendar overlays).

findings.title: A failed sync source never names itself on the canvas — the grid silently thins while degradation hides two clicks deep
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx — per-source sync_state/staleness renders ONLY inside the Sources dialog (5669-5673, StateDot + formatStaleness) and as a per-entry chip in the detail panel (1777-1782). The masthead shows just "N events" + a "Sync now" pill (4126-4141); the Sources pill annotates hidden count but not failed count (4149-4157). No canvas-level banner, no masthead dot, nothing in the eyebrow when a Google source's sync_state is "failed" or 26h stale.
findings.detail: "Every degraded source names itself." A dead OAuth token means the week grid is quietly missing events — the most dangerous failure a calendar can have — and the owner has to suspect it, open Sources, and scan rows to find out. The sync-health cockpit (bu-wwftzj) built the diagnosis room but no alarm.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: Calendar satellites still speak pre-Dispatch dialect, including undefined CSS tokens that render invisible backgrounds
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/calendar/ConflictRadarBanner.tsx:92,125,173,178,190 — raw Tailwind amber-500/emerald-600, rounded-lg card, rounded-full count pill, ⚠ emoji, shadcn text-muted-foreground/hover:bg-muted on the calendar's most safety-critical banner. frontend/src/pages/calendar/QuickAddBar.tsx:21 — rounded-full pills vs Design Language §4c ("4px 10px / 1px border / 3px radius / mono 11px … The system has no rounded[-full pills]", openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:242-245). CalendarAgendaView.tsx:63,71 and CalendarPortabilityDialog.tsx:228 use var(--surface), which is defined nowhere in index.css — hover/file-input backgrounds silently resolve to nothing.
findings.detail: Distinct from in-flight bu-86c4c.6 (which is the lint/CI ENFORCEMENT mechanism): these are the concrete component fixes the old dossier named that the epic did not land. Accept-proposal renders as a green emerald button — a fourth 'green' meaning — inside a surface whose page-level chrome (PILL_BASE, StateDot, KindTag) is otherwise exemplary Dispatch.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: Two timezones on one surface — masthead and search palette use browser tz while the grid renders workspace tz; no now-line to anchor either
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2125 (`timezone` = browser Intl zone) vs 2144 (`defaultTimezone` = workspace zone used by all grid bucketing/labels); masthead eyebrow prints browser tz at 4118; CalendarSearchPalette and detail panel receive browser `timezone` at 5371/5381; moved-ghost day bucketing uses browser-local isSameDay at 4951-4952 while every other bucket uses tzDayKey(defaultTimezone); the time grid draws no current-time line and always scrolls to fixed 7.5h (528, 2666-2669).
findings.detail: When browser and workspace zones differ, the eyebrow labels the grid with the wrong zone, search-result times disagree with grid times for the same event, and the undo ghost can render on the wrong day — quiet fabrication of temporal fact on the one surface whose whole job is time. A now-line is also the cheapest possible orientation signal and is absent.

audits.ideal: The JARVIS-grade calendar opens with a verdict, not a grid: one Dispatch-voice sentence above the masthead — "Quiet week: 14 events, one collision Thursday 15:00, 3 butler proposals waiting, travel calendar stale 26h" — where every clause is a door (collision → radar expanded on the event pair, proposals → panel with accept/dismiss under j/k+Enter, stale source → sources row with a re-auth verb). Counts for proposals, duplicates, and conflicts are always fetched and worn as badges; degraded reads say "conflicts unavailable" in amber text rather than vanishing; a failed sync source names itself in the masthead the moment it fails. State arrives over the fleet WebSocket — a butler booking dinner via MCP materializes on the grid in the same frame with a provenance flash, and the audit trail scrolls live. The entire surface is keyboard-native: t/←→ move time, d/w/m/l switch ranges, c creates, q quick-adds, / searches, and every one of those verbs also lives in the global Cmd+K spine so "find time with Sarah next week" is reachable from any page. Every fused signal is traversable: a finance-bill overlay chip opens the bill in /spend, a travel ribbon opens the trip, a briefing chip opens its source record — the trace spine unbroken from a pixel on the grid to the session that put it there. One timezone (the workspace's) governs every label, a now-line anchors the day, and the whole thing is drawn in one hand — hairline rules, mono eyebrows, three state colors — including the conflict banner and quick-add chips that today still wear another product's clothes.

moves.title: Calendar joins the one command spine + full page keymap
moves.why: Fixes the critical finding: the fleet's richest workspace is 100% mouse-driven while the registry API (bu-86c4c.7) sits unused one import away. This is the single highest-leverage move on the surface — every existing feature (create, quick-add, find-time, sync, search, today, range) becomes a one-keystroke verb.
