findings.title: Live-stream MTD double-counts against the polled baseline — the headline number inflates over time
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:1243-1260 adds the monotonic `streamedCostUsd` (never reset; frontend/src/hooks/use-spend-stream.ts:98) on top of `forecast.mtd_usd`, while the forecast query refetches every 120s (SpendPage.tsx:1235) and each refetch's server-computed MTD already includes those same streamed calls.
findings.detail: Every 2-minute forecast poll re-absorbs events the counter still holds, so a long-lived tab overstates MTD by the cumulative streamed spend since mount; projected EOM is derived from the inflated MTD (SpendPage.tsx:1254) so the red over-ceiling alert (1281-1335) can fire on a fabricated number. The comment's claim 'No subtraction needed' is only true until the first baseline refetch. Fix: reset the counter when the forecast query resolves, or have the server return an `as_of` timestamp and count only events newer than it. Related: the hook's `status` is never consumed anywhere (only `streamedCostUsd` is destructured at 1243), so when the WS is closed the 'live' page silently degrades to 2-minute-stale numbers with no indicator — violates 'every degraded source names itself'.

Worst case is rules: a failed fetch renders the calm config statement 'No routing rules are configured; rules evaluate top-to-bottom…', telling the owner their spend caps are gone when the fetch merely failed — and the backend compounds it by returning HTTP 200 with [] when the DB manager is absent (src/butlers/api/routers/spend.py:1269-1270). Only TopSessions/BySchedule handle isError, and even those render a bare muted sentence with no retry or role=alert.

findings.title: Movers strip fabricates '+$X · new' deltas when one of its two summary queries fails

findings.detail: Asymmetric failure — prior-window query errors while current succeeds — renders every butler as a red positive mover marked 'new', a synthesized ranked signal built from a failed fetch (sin #1, fabrication, not mere empty-conflation). Symmetric failure renders the serif 'No spend change vs the prior window.' The movers strip must render only when both windows resolved, and name the degraded window otherwise.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: backend zero-fills unreachable butlers into summary/breakdown totals with no degraded marker in the envelope

findings.detail: Old dossier critical #3 lineage (per-butler failures return zeros) survives the .11 merge on the DB-fallback path: when the DB path is down and a butler MCP is unreachable, MTD, breakdown bars, and movers all silently under-report with no way for the frontend to say 'health butler's spend is missing from these totals'. findings.title: Butler identity hue broken on the spend chart — same butler wears different colors on /spend vs dashboard, and reshuffles per window

findings.title: Money controls have no keyboard surface: drag-only rule reorder, Enter-dead ceiling edit, zero palette verbs registered

findings.detail: Early in the month a 2-day linear extrapolation can trip the page's only role=alert red banner while the system itself has flagged the number as low-confidence. 'No number is ever fabricated' includes not presenting a known-shaky projection with the same weight as a firm one — the KPI sub-line and alert copy should carry the confidence ('projected $87, low confidence — 2 days elapsed').

findings.title: Deleting a routing rule is instant, unconfirmed, and un-undoable — one mis-click silently lifts a spend cap
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/SpendPage.tsx:936-944 ('Remove' button onClick fires deleteMutation.mutate(id) directly; mutation at 1158-1165 has no confirm step and success toast offers no undo).
findings.detail: The rule's full definition (condition/action/position) is in hand at click time, so an undo toast that re-creates it at the same position is cheap; alternatively an explicit confirm. Design-bar recovery criterion: destructive actions are undoable or confirmed — this is neither, on the control that enforces max_cost_per_call caps.

audits.ideal: The ideal /spend opens with one deterministic Dispatch verdict sentence — "On pace: $41.20 through 12 days against a $100 ceiling, projected $87 with normal confidence; finance (+$6.10) drove the week" — where every clause is a door (ceiling → inline edit, mover → butler spend tab, confidence → forecast chart), followed by a posture strip whose MTD ticks live from a WS stream that is provably single-counted (server as_of anchor), wears a visible LIVE/RECONNECTING eyebrow, and whose fourth cell is today's burn rather than calendar trivia. Every aggregate names its gaps ("health unreachable — totals exclude it") via a degraded envelope, every section renders through the three-way QueryBoundary contract so a dead backend can never impersonate $0, and the movers strip only speaks when both comparison windows resolved. Butlers wear their canonical identity hue and letter-mark in the stacked chart, movers, sessions, and schedules — the same color as everywhere else in the console. Governance is one continuous keyboard-first motion: a schedule row's "cap this" prefills the rule form, rules reorder with Alt+arrows, ceiling saves on Enter, rule deletion undoes from the toast, and "Set ceiling"/"Add routing rule" live in the cmdk spine; saved_7d receipts stay on each rule so the owner sees the money their judgment saved.
audits.jarvis_gap: The .11 merge genuinely landed: one nav-visible surface with the right posture→what-changed→why→controls spine, an honest per-butler-per-day chart (real by_butler data, no re-fabrication), real saved_7d receipts computed by a scheduled job, and live drill-downs to butler spend tabs and sessions. What separates it from JARVIS-grade is truth discipline on the numbers themselves: the live MTD double-counts against its own polling baseline, four sections still let errors impersonate empty despite the epic having shipped QueryBoundary for exactly this, movers can fabricate a ranked signal from a failed fetch, unreachable butlers zero-fill totals with no degraded marker, and a computed confidence rating is thrown away before render. Add that the money controls are mouse-only and butlers lose their identity hue on this one chart, and the surface reads as a well-structured report rather than a trustworthy instrument — the structure of earned calm without its proof obligations.

moves.title: Truth pass: QueryBoundary everywhere + degraded envelope + both-windows-or-silent movers

audits.jarvis_gap: The house-ledger redesign gives /memory an honest templated voice, a deep-linked attention rail, and a real provenance spine (fact ↔ episode ↔ session), but the surface still lies quietly at the aggregation layer (every fleet-wide number silently deflates when a pool fails, with HTTP 200 and no marker), its remedy loop measures the fleet but repairs one butler's pool, its search orders by recency instead of relevance and truncates with counterfeit counts, and its most prominent numerals — the KPI strip, the pipeline band, the red dead-letters figure, every recent-activity row — are prose without doors.

findings.title: Memory fan-out swallows per-pool failures — every fleet-wide number silently deflates with no degradation marker
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:118-131 — `_run` catches bare `Exception` and returns None (logged at DEBUG as 'pool lacks memory tables or query failed'), conflating 'butler has no memory module' with 'query errored'. Every /api/memory endpoint (stats at :182, facts/rules/episodes lists, inspect at :2150, reembed/pending at :2205) sums the surviving pools and returns HTTP 200 with no pools_failed/sources_unavailable field, unlike the repo's aggregates_available convention.
findings.detail: If one butler's pool times out, 'Active facts 3,182' becomes a smaller confident number and the Voice sentence narrates it as truth. This is invisible to the frontend even after bu-mkd5r threads isError — the request succeeds. Violates 'no number is ever fabricated; every degraded source names itself'. NEW signal: bu-mkd5r covers only frontend isError threading, not partial-truth 200s.

findings.title: Re-embed act loop measures the fleet but remedies one pool — and its dry run can POST an empty butler
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/HousekeepingBand.tsx:346-355 — comment claims the run 'targets the same pool the counts were measured on', but the counts come from useReembedPending() with NO butler (use-memory-reembed.ts:21-27 → memory.py:2205-2214 fans out and sums ALL pools) while the POST targets only the alphabetically-first butler (HousekeepingBand.tsx:352-354, 419-420; memory.py:2252-2254 `db.pool(body.butler)` single pool). handleDryRun (line 392) posts `butler: defaultButler ?? ""` → 404 when the butlers list hasn't loaded.
findings.detail: Owner sees 'AttentionRail: 137 rows on an old embedding' (fleet-wide), clicks re-embed, one pool is fixed, completion line says 're-embedded 12 rows', the rail count barely moves — an act loop that cannot complete. Fix: per-pool drift breakdown + per-pool (or fleet-wide) run endpoint; delete the stale comment. Not covered by bu-6t8ix (retry-consolidation/retire-rule) — this verb EXISTS and mis-aims.

findings.title: Memory search orders by recency not relevance, truncates per-kind, and renders counterfeit group counts
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:2013 (`row_limit = offset + limit` per kind per pool), :2036-2041/:2070-2074/:2104-2108 (all three tiers `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT` — plainto_tsquery match with no ts_rank), :2132-2133 (`total = len(merged)` — bounded by row_limit, not a true total). frontend/src/components/memory/SearchResults.tsx:44 (SEARCH_LIMIT=50, no pagination in results mode), :62-68 + :81/:94/:107 (GroupHeader count = truncated group.length, rendered as 'FACTS · 50' as if complete), :141 (meta.total ignored).
findings.detail: A query matching 400 facts shows the 50 most RECENT matches labelled 'FACTS · 50'; the best-matching older fact is unreachable by any keystroke. The page's one search affordance — the primary signal→evidence path — cannot be trusted to find things, and its counts are fabricated-by-truncation.

findings.title: Overture KPI cells and pipeline numerals are inert — including the red dead-letters figure
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/MemoryOverture.tsx:70-93 (KpiStrip: Pending / Active facts / Proven rules / Last write-up are plain <Mega> spans, no links), :115-151 (PipelineBand: episodes/pending/facts/fading/rules/proven are plain PipeStat spans), :140-147 (the `dead letters N` fragment turns --red when N>0 but is a non-interactive span). Exact deep-links already exist for each: /memory?register=episodes&status=pending|dead_letter, ?validity=fading, ?register=rules&maturity=proven (use-memory-url-state.ts vocabulary; AttentionRail uses them at :201, :227).
findings.detail: The band that answers 'is remembering working' offers zero doors; the only route from the red dead-letters signal to evidence is scrolling to the rail below. NEW: bu-9d5vp's 'inert KPI cells' is butler-detail RuntimeSummaryKpi scoped, and unlike those, these cells HAVE existing routes to link to.

findings.title: Recent-activity rows are drill-down dead ends by design
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/AttentionRail.tsx:15-17 (header comment: 'No color, no severity, no links.') and :127-149 — ActivityRow renders mono time · ButlerMark(tone=neutral) · truncated summary with no anchor, though useMemoryActivity items carry `type` and `id` (keyed at :285 as `${item.type}-${item.id}`) that map directly onto /memory/facts/:id, /memory/rules/:id, /memory/episodes/:id.
findings.detail: Twenty live signals of what the house just learned, none of them a door — the row's own key proves the route exists. The graduated redesign spec mandated linkless quiet rows, but backward compatibility is waived and the north star ('every clause is a door') supersedes; the fix is a whole-row link identical to LedgerRow's pattern.

findings.title: /memory contributes zero verbs to the command palette

No memory page or component registers commands; GlobalActionsRegistrar.tsx contains no memory entries. Only the nav chord 'm' exists (nav-config.ts:75).

findings.title: 'N important facts fading' rail action drops its own predicate on click
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/AttentionRail.tsx:234-243 — the condition counts validity=fading ∧ importance_min≥8 (useFacts at :173-178), but the action links to /memory?register=facts&validity=fading, and use-memory-url-state.ts supports no importance param, so the target lists ALL fading facts with no way to isolate the N high-importance ones (FactsRegister rows don't display importance either).
findings.detail: The signal names a precise set; the door opens onto a superset with no marker. Add an `importance_min` URL param to the ledger state + a corresponding filter chip so the drill-down preserves the full predicate (same class as the bu-86c4c.4 'full predicates' rule, new instance).

findings.title: The facts ledger hides authorship: no butler mark and no butler filter on the mixed-pool register
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/memory/FactsRegister.tsx:93-153 — LedgerRow renders subject·predicate / content / belief with no source-butler mark, though facts are fanned out from 9 per-butler schemas and Fact.source_butler is in the payload; EpisodeRow DOES carry ButlerMark (EpisodesRegister.tsx:169-172, 'the sole carrier of butler hue'). MemoryBrowser.tsx:51-54 accepts a butlerScope prop but MemoryPage.tsx:21 never passes one, and no butler filter exists in use-memory-url-state.ts.
findings.detail: Butler hue is the system's identity axis (Dispatch), yet the owner cannot see or ask WHOSE belief a ledger row is without clicking into the detail page — 'Wei · favorite_coffee' could be the relationship butler's or the health butler's fact. Add a quiet source-butler mark to LedgerRow and a `butler` URL filter shared by all three registers.

audits.ideal: The ideal /memory is the house's epistemology console: it opens with the templated Voice verdict it already has, but every numeral in the KPI strip and pipeline band is a door into a pre-filtered register, and the verdict is provably complete — any butler pool that failed to answer names itself in a degraded note rather than silently vanishing from the sums. The one search affordance is relevance-ranked with true per-kind totals and pagination, so the owner is genuinely one `/`-keystroke and one Enter from any belief the house holds; every activity row, fact row, and attention condition carries its full predicate through the click, and the provenance spine (episode → fact → superseding fact → session trace) that the detail pages already run stays unbroken from the overture down. Remedies aim where the measurement was taken: re-embed shows per-butler drift and repairs the pools it counted, dead-lettered episodes retry inline (bu-6t8ix), and Confirm/Retract, register switches, and filters all live in the single command palette. Each ledger row wears its author's hue, the register can be leaned to one butler's lane, and a fully healthy page still renders zero state-color pixels above the fold — earned calm, now earned all the way down to the aggregation layer.

findings.title: Owner-plex ranking failure fabricates a calm household: zero capacity meters + "No one is owed a call."
findings.evidence: PlexPage.tsx:2097-2104 renders AttentionRail whenever isOwnerMode, outside the isError guard. On rankingError, rankingLoading=false so tierCounts=layoutOwnerPlex([],null) all-zeros (PlexPage.tsx:1431-1434) → capacity meters render 0/5…0/500 (1308-1352), and attention=[] with attentionLoading=false renders the serif empty "No one is owed a call." (1262-1266). Meanwhile the canvas shows "Failed to load the graph." with no retry and no source named (1967-1974).
findings.detail: The two systemic sins at once: fabricated zeros and an error impersonating an empty queue, on the flagship landing surface. The flanks must key off the same three-way state contract as the canvas (loading/error/data), the error placard must name the degraded source (dunbar ranking endpoint) and carry a Retry, and no meter may render a number derived from a failed fetch.

findings.title: Halo fetch error is silently indistinguishable from "no organizations/places exist"
findings.evidence: PlexPage.tsx:1437 destructures only `data` from usePlexHalo(isOwnerMode); use-entities.ts:203-210 exposes isError but nothing reads it. On a 4xx/5xx (including the endpoint's own owner_required 403, router.py:3783-3785) haloLayout stays null and OwnerPlexCanvas renders exactly the no-satellites layout (halo=null branch, PlexPage.tsx:408).
findings.detail: The owner cannot tell a degraded dimension halo from a genuinely person-only graph. Minimum fix: a quiet mono placard on the halo band ("organizations · unavailable · retry") when the query errors.

findings.title: Neighbour-mode dossier: failed facts/dates fetches impersonate empty ("Nothing recorded yet.")
findings.evidence: PlexPage.tsx:1103-1106 destructures only data/isLoading from useEntityFacts and only data from useEntityCoreDates. On error, facts=[] hits the !factsLoading && facts.length===0 branch → "Nothing recorded yet." (1199-1203); a dates error silently removes the Dates section (1169).
findings.detail: Same class as the flank finding but on the drill-down surface: the dossier is the evidence pane of the hop spine, so a lying empty here corrupts the owner's read of a specific person. Both queries need isError → named-source error rows with retry.

findings.title: The "Worth attention" verdict is fabricated in the view layer with magic constants, not by the relationship butler
findings.evidence: PlexPage.tsx:1387-1403 hardcodes TIER_CADENCE_DAYS and TIER_URGENCY_WEIGHT in the frontend; 1489-1518 computes overdue/urgency client-side, with the comment "the contact-keyed overdue endpoint was retired with public.contacts". The manifesto (roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md, "Relationships decay without interaction") makes decay/health scoring the butler's doctrine that drives its weekly-review recommendations.
findings.detail: North star: every surface opens with the system's own synthesized verdict. Here the console's judgment can diverge from what the butler actually recommends (its decay model, its weekly review), and each attention row carries no reason or evidence link beyond "Nd since contact" — no per-item explanation of why THIS person outranks that one, and no trace to the interactions the claim rests on. The verdict belongs server-side with reasons attached.

findings.title: Find-as-you-type returns a false "0 matches" for anyone in the tier-1500 periphery or beyond the halo cap, with no escape hatch
findings.evidence: searchSpace is built only from rendered marks (PlexPage.tsx:1704-1715); PLEX_NODE_TIERS excludes 1500 (plex-layout.ts:27) and halo arcs cap at top-20 per type (router.py:3760-3764), so a familiar-face's name yields "find x · 0 matches · esc clears" (PlexPage.tsx:2060-2076) even though the entity exists and the same string would hit in the Cmd-K Finder.
findings.detail: A canvas-scoped search is honest only if it says its scope. The zero-match state should offer "enter searches all entities" (reusing useEntityFinderSearch) and hop to the hit via ?center=, so the plex's find covers the whole graph instead of quietly excluding ~the largest tier.

findings.title: Drag-to-retier is not same-frame and has no undo: the node snaps back to the old ring until the ranking refetch lands
findings.evidence: useUpdateEntityDunbarTier (use-entities.ts:505-520) has no onMutate/optimistic cache write — only onSuccess invalidation of dunbar-ranking. handleRetier (PlexPage.tsx:1760-1773) awaits mutateAsync then toasts; during mutate+invalidate+refetch the drag state is already cleared (handleDragEnd, 439-446) so the node visually reverts to its pre-drag ring, then jumps again. The success toast has no Undo action even though the API trivially supports it (tier:null / previous tier).
findings.detail: Violates the north-star action contract ("every owner action applies in the same frame with undoable rollback") on the page's single manual write. Fix: onMutate patches the dunbar-ranking cache (tier + dunbar_tier_override), onError rolls back, and the toast gains Undo restoring the prior tier/pin state.

findings.title: Keyboard users have no path to the micro-dossier or to pin/unpin: hover-only card, drag-only retier
findings.evidence: PlexNode binds onHoverStart/onHoverEnd only to onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave (PlexPage.tsx:312-313) — no onFocus/onBlur — so tabbing to a mark never opens the hover card containing "Open record" and "Unpin tier" (1061-1077). Tier pinning is exclusively pointer-drag (draggable, 746; handlePointerDown 262-289); the legend itself says "drag a person to pin a tier" (2091-2094). No arrow-key traversal between marks; Tab order over ~600 absolutely-positioned buttons is the only walk.
findings.detail: The a11y floor (bu-86c4c.16) landed axe tests but this is a behavioral keyboard gap axe cannot see. Focus should mirror hover (open the dossier card), and a focused mark needs key verbs (Enter=center exists; add o=open record, p=pin-to-ring picker / unpin).

findings.title: Circles label badges paint white text over arbitrary owner-supplied hex — AA contrast unguaranteed and un-lintable
findings.evidence: CirclesPage.tsx:62-65 (BADGE_TEXT="#fff", labelBg returns label.color ?? categoryHueVar), applied at 198 and 230; CreateLabelDialog accepts any hex (109-133) with no luminance check, so a #ffee00 label renders white-on-yellow.
findings.detail: The contrast-locked token work (bu-86c4c.16/bu-kx3xc) cannot protect runtime-supplied colors. Either compute foreground (black/white) from the hex's relative luminance at render, or drop free-hex entirely and constrain labels to the categoryHueVar ramp (Dispatch dialect prefers the latter: one hue system).

audits.ideal: The ideal /entities is the household's social instrument: the plex opens with the butler's own verdict rendered as a Dispatch-voice line above the rings ("Two inner-circle ties are fading — Sarah, 12 days over cadence; Mom's birthday in 6 days"), every clause a door — click or keystroke lands on the person centered in the plex with the evidence (interactions, facts, decay curve) in the dossier flank. The canvas is fully keyboard-native: type to find across the WHOLE graph (periphery and beyond-cap satellites included, falling through to the Finder index when off-canvas), arrows walk marks, focus opens the micro-dossier, single keys pin/unpin tiers, and every write applies in the same frame with an Undo in the toast. The four lenses (Plex, Index, Concentration, Circles) are one instrument, not four tabs: any row anywhere offers "view in plex" so the hop-trail spine extends from every list, a circle can be projected onto the rings as a highlight lens, and a concentration row's dominance is one hop from the triples that earned it. Failure is always named: a dead ranking endpoint shows an amber source-named placard with retry — never zeroed capacity meters or a serif "No one is owed a call" — and the attention verdict itself is computed by the relationship butler from its manifesto's decay model, arriving with reasons and trace-ids, so the console reports judgment it can prove rather than judgment it invented.
audits.jarvis_gap: The plex is the closest thing the console has to a signature JARVIS surface — real radial ego-graph, halo, hop trail, find-as-you-type, drag-to-retier, all wired to live endpoints — but it fails the earned-calm test precisely where it matters: a failed ranking fetch fabricates a perfectly calm household (zero meters, "No one is owed a call"), its one synthesized judgment (worth attention) is a frontend heuristic with magic constants rather than the butler's own decay-model verdict with evidence, its flagship interaction (retier) is neither same-frame nor undoable, and its keyboard story stops at click-to-center. The sibling lenses are honest and functional but siloed — no path from Index/Concentration/Circles rows back into the plex spine.

audits.ideal: The ideal entity page opens with judgment in the Dispatch voice: one 44px Display headline (the only h1), a serif verdict synthesizing tier, trajectory, and open loops — "Inner-circle friend, last touched 9 days ago, one unsettled loan, birthday in 12 days" — where every clause is a door (loan → the loan row, birthday → core date, 9 days → the interaction's session). Below it, exactly what needs the owner: a duplicate warning backed by a per-entity duplicates endpoint that can never silently miss, delta-since-last-visit rows one keystroke away, and manifesto verbs (log interaction, gift idea, draft reach-out — the in-flight .15 scope) inline on the signals they answer. Every subsection obeys the three-way state contract — skeleton, named degraded source, or true empty — and no KPI ever shows a number the system didn't compute. Every fact, timeline entry, thread, and provenance row carries an id-keyed link to its authoring session on the trace spine. The whole surface is keyboard-first from the moment it mounts: focus lands on the detail root, j/k walk the arrival scope with an 'n of m' position mark, a visible hint strip teaches m/e/Esc, and every curation verb — one name per operation, undo-toast for the reversible ones — is registered in the single command registry so ⌘K reaches merge, set-tier, archive, and forget without the mouse. audits.jarvis_gap: The Settings suite is functionally deep (live WS console, one-time secret ceremonies, reason-gated permission flips) but fails the console's defining property — earned calm through honesty — at its most visible point: when a subsystem dies, the KPI strip confidently prints fabricated zeros ($0.00 spend, 0 active butlers), and the audit reel renders a fetch failure as 'No recent audit entries.' Its judgment surfaces are doors to nowhere: a failed model shows a bare ✗ with no error, no timestamp, no trail; the permissions matrix — the sovereignty control at the heart of the governance chamber — is inert for every inherited cell, which on a default system is the whole grid. And /settings/models still speaks a foreign dialect (bg-yellow-500 fills, a white-on-red BLOCKED word-badge) that the three-token Dispatch language explicitly bans. Detect works; diagnose and act stall one hop past the headline.
audits.ideal: The ideal /settings is the household's constitution room: it opens with a one-sentence synthesized verdict in the Dispatch voice ('All governance nominal; codex CLI needs re-auth — one decision pending') where every clause is a keyboard-reachable door, followed by a KPI strip that renders an em-dash plus a named degraded-source marker — never a fabricated zero — whenever a subsystem cannot prove its number. The permissions matrix is fully operable: every cell, inherited or explicit, flips through the reason-gated modal (inherited cells show their default provenance and become explicit on flip, exactly as the spec's mutation scenario demands), a legend teaches ●/○/dim on-surface, and each flip lands as a linked entry in a date-aware audit reel that doubles as the cross-settings changelog with diff drill-down. Every model row carries its verification evidence (when, latency, last error) one disclosure away, with Test/Verify-all as palette verbs; destructive actions (webhook delete, model delete) share one confirm-with-consequences ceremony; the whole chamber lives under one sub-nav shell (bu-rxtyx) speaking pure three-token Dispatch, and every governance verb — verify all, export data, add webhook, grant permission — is one Cmd-K away.

findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/pages.tsx:1314 passes credential.provider ('telegram_bot', 'homeassistant') and pages.tsx:1880 passes credential.category ('llm', 'general') to WhatBreaks; the backend endpoint exact-matches WHERE provider = $1 (src/butlers/api/routers/secrets_v2.py:1985-1997) against catalogue slugs 'telegram'/'home_assistant' (src/butlers/catalogue_bootstrap.py:83-106), so both queries return []. Additionally secrets_v2.py:1977-1981 and 2016-2026 degrade pool-unavailable/table-missing to HTTP 200 empty with no degraded flag, so infrastructure failure also impersonates that empty claim.
findings.detail: The one component the spec calls the WhatBreaks source-of-truth affordance tells the owner that Telegram, Home Assistant, and every system key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY included, via category slug) has zero dependents. An owner acting on that claim ('nothing depends on it, safe to delete') gets an outage. The inventory endpoint already alias-resolves via _infer_provider_from_type (secrets_v2.py:1084-1095) — the breaks-catalogue endpoint just never adopted it. The degraded-200 also violates the repo's own aggregates_available convention (errors impersonating empty): the FE 'unavailable' branch (WhatBreaks.tsx:115-121) can never fire.

The probe response type SecretsProbeResult carries real latency_ms (frontend/src/api/types.ts:7339-7350, populated from public.secret_probe_log per secrets_v2.py:3170-3199), and the inventory adapter explicitly contracts 'never a fabricated 0ms' (use-secrets-inventory.ts:174-183).

findings.title: Failure and empty states are dead ends, and the attention voice line misstates CLI failure modes

audits.jarvis_gap: The passport is structurally excellent — real inventory, wired verbs, honest sublines after the truth amnesty — but it still tells confident lies at the decision points: WhatBreaks answers 'nothing depends on this' for most credentials because of an unadopted slug alias, the system-page plaque shows green over a failing state, the test verb fabricates 0ms, and 'nobody yet'/'no expiry' assert unknowns as facts. Its doors are half-hung: the system audit link 422s, KPI counts and the verdict headline are terminal text, and the entire surface is mouse-only with zero palette commands despite the command spine existing. State arrives by 5-minute polling, not the fleet event bus, and green is unearned — 'warn = never probed' rows sit until a human presses test.
audits.ideal: The ideal /secrets is a credential ledger the owner can trust with deletions: it opens with a verdict whose every clause is a door ('2 need hand' focuses the pinned group; 'Telegram sick' opens that page), the spine walks with j/k and '/', and cmd-K carries the page's verbs (probe, re-authorize, rotate, add) scoped to the focused credential. Every claim is earned: dependency maps come from an alias-resolved catalogue that names itself when degraded, states on the plaque and spine are one contract, latency is measured or absent, and unknowns say 'not tracked' rather than 'nobody'/'no expiry'. A scheduled verification sweep probes every set credential daily so green means 'verified <time>' not 'set once', and a horizon strip forecasts the next thing that will break (test-mode consent in 3d, CLI token in 9d) each with its one-key remedy. Mutations and probe results arrive over the fleet event bus in the same frame, and each stamp deep-links into the audit spine without ever landing on an error.

audits.jarvis_gap: The epic's two verified landings hold: fabricated mastery is purged (ReviewTimeline.tsx:48-55 now renders the real entry.mastery_score and falls back to a labeled status chip when null) and quiz-history rows gained real keyboard semantics (QuizHistoryList.tsx:113-129 role/tabIndex/keydown). Almost nothing else from the redesign reached this surface. /education is the clearest case of a pre-Dispatch island in a post-Dispatch app: the same education data rendered inside ButlerDetail's education tab (redesigned in .18) uses chartColor(), isError threading, and the shared dialect, while the dedicated page one route over still speaks 2025 shadcn — bold headings, card grids, nine hardcoded light-only hue families, raw #3b82f6 recharts fills, an uncontrolled tab set hiding the only time-critical signal, and zero commands in the palette registry. The deeper JARVIS gap is unchanged from the old dossier: the education butler is a live agent walking a five-phase teaching state machine and making time-bound promises (spaced reviews, curriculum builds), and the page still shows only its database artifacts — useTeachingFlows remains exported and imported by nothing, and a curriculum request still evaporates into a toast. The page reads the butler's tables instead of standing in for the butler; there is no verdict, no visible commitment, and no unbroken path from an overdue review to the session that scheduled it. (Error-impersonating-empty on this page is real but already owned by open bead bu-mkd5r and therefore not re-reported.)

audits.ideal: The page opens with the tutor's own verdict in the Dispatch voice — one serif line synthesized from data already on hand ("Two reviews overdue on Linear Algebra; the TCP/IP curriculum finished its diagnostic overnight — teaching resumes at your word.") — above a hairline KPI strip (due now / overdue / concepts mastered this week / next scheduled review) where every cell is a door. Below it, the manifesto's "learning territory" is the full-height centerpiece: a theme-tokened concept map (three state colors plus neutral, an always-visible legend, butler hue only on the letter-mark) whose every node, review row, and struggling concept opens the same node dossier drawer — mastery trajectory, full quiz transcript with evaluator notes, SM-2 schedule, and a trace-id link to the butler session that taught or quizzed it. The butler's agency is a first-class surface: each curriculum card carries its live teaching-flow phase chip and every promise (a requested curriculum, a scheduled review) renders as a tracked in-progress commitment until it resolves, updated over the fleet event bus in the same frame the butler acts. Errors name themselves with retry, empties are one serif-italic sentence, and the whole queue — open overdue review, request curriculum, jump to curriculum — clears from the command palette without touching the mouse.

audits.jarvis_gap: The page has the right editorial skeleton (Voice, KPI strip, attention, recent-days index, below-fold day detail) and the IEA epic will fix the data model, but as an instrument it fails "moves as fast as thought" and "one keystroke from any signal to evidence": every day-step blanks the entire page to a skeleton (no placeholderData, no adjacent-day prefetch), there is not a single keyboard or palette route to any archive action, the primary drill-down (Gantt episode → drawer) is mouse-only and invisible to screen readers, the Refresh control never refreshes the editorial half it sits under, two fetch failures render as empty days, and the source-state strip asserts today's adapter health on any past day. Judgment prose exists but its provenance (templated vs LLM) is silently dropped, and no clause of it is a door.

findings.title: Every day-step blanks the whole page to a skeleton; no keepPreviousData, no adjacent-day prefetch
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-chronicles-briefing.ts:33-43 (useQuery with no placeholderData/keepPreviousData; queryKey changes per date) + frontend/src/pages/ChroniclesPage.tsx:218 (`loading={!data && !isError}`) + frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:371-409 (loading replaces all children with WorkspaceSkeleton). Stepping prev/next changes the query key, data becomes undefined, and the Voice, KPI strip, attention list, recent-days index, and the entire drilldown unmount into a skeleton until the fetch lands. The Elaboration cross-fade path (isFetching opacity, Elaboration.tsx) is dead code for date changes because data is never retained across keys. prevIsoDay/nextIsoDay are deterministic, yet nothing prefetches the adjacent days.
findings.detail: Archive browsing (stepping back through days) is this page's hottest path — the design-bar 'Pace' and 'Habit' questions both fail. The north star demands owner actions apply in the same frame; here even a read-only navigation flashes the whole instrument away.

The 'stale' indicator (ChroniclesPage.tsx:211,254-262) is derived from that briefing query's voice_source.
findings.detail: Walkthrough 'Repetition' failure: owner sees 'stale', clicks Refresh, spinner completes, headline/voice/KPI/attention/stale pill all unchanged — feedback failed, repeat clicks follow. Fix is one shared per-day invalidation family covering both halves of the page.

findings.title: Point-events fetch failure impersonates an empty day (no trail, no scrub snaps, no degradation notice)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:95 destructures only `data` from useChroniclesPointEvents; isError is discarded. On failure, Scrubber gets snapMs=[] (line 164) and FloatingMapMinimap gets trailPoints=[] (line 178), rendering exactly like a day with no movement. Contrast: byDay/byCategory correctly pass isError+onRetry to their charts (lines 185-196).
findings.detail: Five-sins instance (error impersonating empty), new — not in the 2026-07-03 dossier's landed fixes, which covered chart/list surfaces, not the scrubber/map evidence feed.

findings.title: Source-state strip asserts TODAY's adapter health on any past day, and swallows its own fetch errors into null
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/SourceStateBadgeStrip.tsx:172-186: useChroniclesSourceState() takes no date; rendered unconditionally inside the day-scoped drilldown (ChroniclesDrilldownPanel.tsx:155). On /chronicles?date=<last month>, badges claim sources are 'active'/'no recent data' as of now, presented as context for that day's reconstruction. Additionally rows fall back to [] on error and the component returns null (lines 186, 209) — a failed fetch removes the strip entirely. Off-token `bg-yellow-500 text-white` (line 113) is a fourth state color outside the Dispatch triad.
findings.detail: A retrospective page needs per-day evidence coverage ('which sources contributed to THIS day, which were silent'), not live ops state. IEA plans per-activity evidence chains but no day-level coverage surface, so this is unclaimed territory.

findings.title: Gantt episodes — the page's main drill-down door — are mouse-only and invisible to assistive tech
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/chronicles/GanttSwimlaneInner.tsx:318-324: `<g role="button" onClick=...>` with no tabIndex and no onKeyDown, nested inside the timeline SVG declared `role="img"` at line ~600-601 — role=img flattens all descendants for screen readers, so the role=button children are unreachable by both keyboard and AT. EpisodeDrawer (evidence, corrections) is therefore reachable only by pointer.
findings.detail: New instance beyond bu-f310e (which targets DisclosureRow on facts/rules/audit HTML rows, not SVG interactive marks) and beyond the landed axe floor (bu-86c4c.16), since axe does not flag unfocusable SVG role=button under role=img reliably. audits.jarvis_gap: The QA dossier is structurally the most JARVIS-shaped surface in the product — claim-anchored diagnosis prose with numbered footnotes cross-highlighting an evidence log is exactly "every clause is a door." But the doors are painted on: cross-highlighting is hover-only and evidence lines terminate in plain text with no trace-id/session/patrol links, so the spine ends at prose. Worse, the surface still fabricates on its default screen — every in-flight case's fix panel claims "Escalated to user," the new patrol pulse strip renders findings-dispatched patrols as clean-green because it string-matches the wrong status value, and the KPI strip prints "0 awaiting CI · 0 escalated" while the summary fetch is failing. The five-second health verdict is impossible: the API ships staffer_status, last/next patrol, circuit breaker, and credential health, and the page renders none of them. And the whole surface registers zero palette commands — the one page about the system healing itself cannot be triaged without a mouse.

The stage is available two lines up (CaseDossier.tsx:87) and unused.

Un-landed old minors: dual severity vocabularies with lossy color mapping (QaPatrolDetailPage.tsx:34-40: 0/1 both destructive, 3/4 both muted) vs 3-level cases; drafted and closed PR dots identical (CaseList.tsx:15-20); native window.confirm on force patrol (QaOverviewPage.tsx:394); investigation-detail API errors still render 'Investigation not found.' (QaInvestigationDetailPage.tsx:39-48).

audits.ideal: /qa opens with a verdict masthead in the Dispatch voice — "Staff is healthy. Last patrol 4m ago, clean; next in 6m. Two cases need you." — synthesized from the summary fields the API already ships (staffer_status, last/next patrol, breaker, credentials), with a red banner and one-keystroke jump to /secrets when the breaker trips or the GH token is missing. The pulse strip tells the truth per status (green only for clean, amber for findings-dispatched, pulsing for running, red for error), the rail states "25 of 41 · load more" from meta.total, and the empty state radiates earned calm ("No open cases — last patrol 4m ago, clean"). The dossier stays the crown jewel but every clause becomes a real door: claim footnotes and evidence rows are focusable, cross-highlight on focus as well as hover, and each evidence line and journal tick links to its session, trace, and originating patrol in one keystroke. The fix panel is stage-aware — "escalated" appears only when the case is escalated, with the reason and a decide-now verb; in-flight cases say "diagnosing, started 3m ago." Everything is palette-registered (force patrol, filter by severity/state/butler, next/previous case via j/k, dismiss, retry), all timestamps share one viewer-local clock, and no fetch failure ever wears the costume of an empty queue.

findings.title: Timeline aggregates freeze at mount: histogram, hour totals, and footer rollup use a window whose 'to' (and 'from') never advances
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ingestion/TimelineTab.tsx:1857-1863 — rangeWindow is useMemo'd on [range] only, so `now` is captured once at mount/range-change. The ledger query deliberately omits the upper bound (lines 1902-1913, comment explains the freeze hazard), but histogramParams passes the frozen `to` (line 1938) and the footer rollup passes `to: effectiveWindow?.to ?? rangeWindow.to` (lines 1988-1990). Hour-group header counts are sourced from that histogram (lines 1117-1128, labeled 'Honest hour totals').
findings.detail: The fleet event bus correctly invalidates ['ingestion','events-histogram'] and ['ingestion','window-rollup'] on every new event (event-cache-registry.ts:126-130), but the refetch re-runs with the same frozen window, so any event received after mount is server-side filtered out of the aggregates. Failure scenario: owner leaves /ingestion open (its whole point as a live console); new rows stream into the ledger while the flame strip stays flat, hour headers under-count the very rows below them, and the footer 'events' figure contradicts the visible list. Also the 'from' edge never slides forward, so '1h' silently becomes '1h + time-open'. Fix is small: recompute the window on a coarse tick (e.g. 30-60s, aligned with LiveStatusBadge's wall-clock tick) or send open-ended windows the server clamps to now.

findings.title: Errors impersonate empty on /ingestion/connectors and /ingestion/filters; roster ignores aggregates_available and renders fabricated zeros
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/ConnectorsRoster.tsx:101-107,139-147,170-173 — useConnectorSummariesWithAggregates() destructures only data/isLoading; a failed fetch renders the serif empty state 'No connectors registered.' plus a KPI band of zeros. Line 105-106: the aggregates_available flag is mentioned in a comment but never read — 'events · 24h' (lines 134-137, 201) and the 24h sparklines render 0 as if real when Prometheus is down, violating the degraded-envelope contract in CLAUDE.md §Degraded-Mode Response Envelope. Same sin on filters: FiltersPipeline.tsx:97-98 captures rulesError but passes it only to ChannelDefaultsBlock (line 370); GateSection renders 'No rules at this gate. Policy lives in code.' (GateSection.tsx:114) on a rules fetch failure.
findings.detail: Failure scenario: API restart or transient 500 while the owner checks connectors → the console asserts the house has zero connectors and zero traffic, the exact 'failed fetch impersonating an empty queue' the north star forbids. The timeline's own ledger has a proper isError + Retry branch (TimelineTab.tsx:2213-2228), so the pattern exists in-surface and just wasn't applied to the siblings. Fix: isError branches with retry on roster and gates, and a 'metrics unavailable' eyebrow + em-dash KPIs on the roster when aggregates_available is false (FiltersPipeline already does this at line 327-330).

findings.title: Spend view fragments the ledger into duplicated hour groups, each repeating the same full-hour histogram totals

findings.title: Custom saved-view delete is a one-click destructive action with no confirm and no undo
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ingestion/TimelineTab.tsx:440-459 — a 10px trash button sits inside each view pill (opacity-60, brightening on hover) and fires onDeleteCustomView on click; :1811-1828 — handleDeleteCustomView mutates DELETE immediately and toasts 'Saved view deleted' with no undo affordance.

audits.jarvis_gap: The bones are genuinely good — live fleet-bus invalidation, an honest event drawer with audited payload gating and reasoned empty states, URL-backed trace/minute scoping that survived verification — but the surface still behaves like a monitoring tool the owner interrogates rather than an instrument that reports. It opens with static copy ('Last 24 hours, newest first.', 'Where signals come from.') instead of a synthesized verdict; its aggregate numbers freeze at mount while the ledger underneath stays live, so the longer the owner trusts it open the more it quietly lies; two of its four pages can render a failed fetch as an empty house; its sub-pages and every frequent verb are invisible to the command palette; and the trace spine only points inward, so the root evidence surface cannot answer 'what did this signal cause?' in one keystroke. It also remains the last surface speaking two visual dialects (blue as a fourth state color, filled state badges), which will trip the incoming language-enforcement CI.
audits.ideal: The ideal /ingestion opens with a computed Dispatch verdict line — 'Quiet pipeline: 412 signals in 24h, all dispatched; gmail needs reauth; $0.84 spent.' — where every clause is a door (reauth → connector detail, $0.84 → spend view, 412 → the ledger below), synthesized client-side from the rollup, connector summaries, and filter stats already being fetched. Beneath it, the ledger is a genuinely live instrument: windows slide with the clock, the flame strip grows new minutes as events land, and hour totals always agree with the rows they head. Every number that cannot be proven names its degraded source; every fetch failure says so and offers retry; every state is one of exactly three colors. From any row: j/k to move, Enter for the drawer, and from the drawer one keystroke to the raw payload, the spawned sessions, or the full trace across the house in either direction (event → trace → chronicle, chronicle → trace → event). Every verb — replay selected, switch view, scope to trace, jump to connector — lives in the single palette registry, and connectors/filters are one g-chord away. Failure looks like an amber sentence naming the broken source with a retry verb; empty looks like a serif reassurance that the quiet is real, proven by a live badge that decays on a wall clock.

audits.ideal: The owner lands on /system and reads one Dispatch-voice sentence that is provably true: "Instance healthy — v0.4.2, up 12 days, backed up 3h ago, all 9 butlers beating, all 4 connectors listening, last verified just now" — or a severity-ranked problem list where every clause is a door (offline connector → its connector page, failed insights → the exact blocked candidates with a requeue verb, posture regression → the settings row that fixes it) and every remedy completes inline without leaving the screen. The verdict is structurally incapable of lying: any feeding source in error state converts the healthy assertion into a named "cannot verify backups — source unreachable, retry" clause, and connector ingress health carries the same weight as butler heartbeats. Below the sentence, eyebrow-titled hairline sections (no cards) elaborate: heartbeats as keyboard-navigable rows sharing the one severity token vocabulary, a theme-aware topology map drawn entirely from index.css tokens with a keyboard-operable node index beside it, DB footprint with a real growth sparkline from a size-history endpoint, egress and posture as sovereign ownership facts. State arrives over the fleet event bus — a backup completing or a connector dying updates the verdict in the same frame — and the whole page is reachable and operable from the command palette in under five keystrokes.

audits.jarvis_gap: The one-command-spine (bu-86c4c.7) genuinely landed — single route registry feeds sidebar, palette Pages, g-chords, and the '?' sheet — but the shell still fails "the first use needs no docs, the tenth use needs no mouse": the console's hottest loop (approvals j/k/a/d/x triage) is advertised nowhere in the product, the command registry carries no keybinding metadata so the palette can never teach shortcuts, the palette is invisible until you type (no browsable verbs, no recents, substring-only matching), and two page-local key handlers (memory '/', chat Ctrl+Shift+arrows) were built outside the spine — one of them now dead-colliding with the global '/' binding.
audits.ideal: Every keyboard path in the console flows through one shortcut+command registry: PaletteCommand grows a `binding` field, a shared useRegisterShortcut hook both binds page-scoped keys and feeds the '?' help sheet (with an "On this page" section) and the palette's inline kbd column — so a shortcut cannot exist without being advertised, by construction. The palette is browsable at empty query (recent commands and destinations above the entity-pinned set), fuzzy-matches verbs and nouns, and shows each entry's chord inline. Sidebar tooltips carry their g-chords; every badge-bearing attention surface has one. The Approvals triage interaction (j/k roving focus + undoable verb scheduling) is a shared hook applied to every triage list — Dashboard attention, Issues, Notifications — with its verbs visible in a persistent footer hint strip, matching the finder's own ↑↓/↵/⇥ footer pattern.

findings.title: Approvals j/k/a/d/x triage verbs are advertised nowhere in the product
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ApprovalsPage.tsx:1332-1374 binds j/k roving focus and a/d/x undoable decisions; grep confirms zero <kbd>, KbMono, aria-keyshortcuts, or hint copy anywhere in the file. The '?' help sheet's STATIC_SHORTCUTS (frontend/src/components/ui/shortcut-hints.tsx:19-23) lists only Ctrl+K, /, ? plus g-chords — page-scoped shortcuts have no representation at all. The north-star loop ('clear the queue in under a minute without touching the mouse') is invisible to anyone who hasn't read the source.
findings.detail: The finder itself proves the house pattern exists — its footer strip (EntityFinder.tsx:718-735) advertises ↑↓/↵/⇥/esc inline. Approvals (and any future triage surface) needs the same persistent hint strip, plus rows in the help sheet.

findings.title: Global '/' (command menu) collides with MemorySearch's '/' focus binding — both fire on /memory
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:41-45 binds bare '/' to open the command menu (window keydown, preventDefault). frontend/src/components/memory/MemorySearch.tsx:82-96 independently binds bare '/' on window to focus the memory search input, with a comment claiming "'/' focuses the input from anywhere on the page". Neither stops propagation, so on /memory both handlers run: the palette opens and its requestAnimationFrame focus (EntityFinder.tsx:286) steals focus from the memory input — MemorySearch's binding is dead code that also documents false behavior.
findings.detail: Two components claiming the same bare key with no arbitration is exactly what the single-spine work was meant to end. Either delete the MemorySearch handler or route page-scoped key claims through a registry that detects conflicts.

findings.title: PaletteCommand has no binding metadata — the palette can never display shortcuts inline, and the help sheet can never show page-scoped keys
findings.evidence: frontend/src/lib/command-registry.tsx:36-45 — PaletteCommand is {id, label, keywords, perform}; no binding/shortcut field. EntityFinder.tsx:698-715 renders Action rows with label only. shortcut-hints.tsx:19-41 builds the help sheet from a hardcoded STATIC_SHORTCUTS array plus route chords — there is no channel by which ApprovalsPage's a/d/x, ChatPanel's chords, or any future page shortcut can reach it.
findings.detail: The discoverability bar says 'the palette is where shortcuts are learned' and 'displays each entry's keybinding inline'. The registry is the right unifying mechanism and it is one field + one render column away.

findings.title: Palette is invisible until the first keystroke: Actions, Pages, butlers all hidden at empty query; no recents anywhere
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:366-375 (actionMatches gated on lowerQuery.length >= 1), :324-331 (pageMatches same), :344 (butlerMatches same). Empty query renders only the owner-pinned entity set (:509-539). A user opening Cmd+K sees people — never learns that 'Trigger <butler>', 'Approve next', or 'Acknowledge issue' exist. No recents store exists for commands or destinations.
findings.detail: Skill contract: 'shows recents first'; empty states teach. The empty-query view should stack recent commands/destinations above the pinned entities, making the verb layer browsable.

findings.title: Finder preview pane and Tab-hop track the first entity even when a Page/Action/Session row is highlighted
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:390-413 — activeResult falls back to entityResults[0] whenever activeValue doesn't start with 'entity:' (e.g. 'page:…', 'action:…'). So with an Action row highlighted, the preview pane shows an unrelated entity, and the Tab handler (:449-452) hops the user to /entities?center=<that entity> — an action unrelated to the highlighted item. The footer advertises '⇥ hop' unconditionally (:728-731).
findings.detail: activeResult should resolve from the actually-highlighted value; Tab (and the footer's ⇥ hint) should only be live on entity rows.

findings.title: Substring-only matching in the one palette — no fuzzy, no typo or word-order tolerance

'aprove', 'approve nxt', or 'spend page' (word order) match nothing; cmdk's built-in scorer is bypassed and no fuzzy scorer replaces it.
findings.detail: Server-ranked entity results are fine; the client-side groups (pages/butlers/actions) need a shared fuzzy scorer — one utility, applied to all three, so match quality stays consistent across groups.

audits.jarvis_gap: The north star demands the console "reads as one instrument built by one hand"; today it is two coexisting design systems — a real, well-tokenized Dispatch layer (minority) sitting on a shadcn base layer that is still the DEFAULT: the default typeface is the spec-forbidden system-ui/Roboto stack, the shared page-shell and empty-state primitives render off-language for 24+ pages each, the same semantic gray has two values depending on dialect, forbidden skeleton-pulse ships on 46 sites, and chart/status color speaks four dialects with state hues carrying second meanings. The in-flight lint bead (bu-86c4c.6) can stop NEW drift but cannot flip the defaults; until the base layer itself is Dispatch, every un-redesigned surface and every new page is born off-language.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: Default typeface is the forbidden system-ui/Roboto stack; Inter Tight is opt-in and flagship pages never opt in
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:8 sets `:root { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, ... Roboto, sans-serif }` — the spec's explicitly forbidden primary faces (openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:143). index.css:247-249 admits it: "The :root font-family rule above remains the body default; opt-in consumers reference these variables directly." The app shell (components/layout/Shell.tsx:41-89) applies no family; only Sidebar.tsx:472,516,809 opts into font-sans. Grep: DashboardPage, ApprovalsPage, SessionsPage, TimelinePage, SpendPage, SystemPage, AuditLogPage, ButlersPage contain ZERO `font-sans` — their body text renders in system-ui/Roboto. Only 28 of ~400 component files reference font-sans at all.
findings.detail: This was in the 2026-07-03 dossier's summary ("stock shadcn system-ui body font") and did not land in any merged epic child. It is a runtime-default problem, not a lint problem — bu-86c4c.6 (diff-time token lint) cannot fix text that renders wrong today. The fix is one line (`font-family: var(--font-sans)` on :root/body) plus deleting the per-component opt-ins.

findings.title: Shared page-shell and empty-state primitives are still old-language, so every page using the shared path is off-spec by default
findings.evidence: components/ui/page.tsx:106 renders `<h1 className="text-3xl font-bold tracking-tight">` — 33px/700 matches neither Display (44/500) nor Title (24/500); spec.md:157-162 says "Display weight is 500, never 700". page.tsx is imported by 24 non-test files. components/ui/empty-state.tsx:10-18 renders icon + `font-semibold` heading + description paragraph + action (24 consumers) vs spec.md:349-353 "one serif-italic sentence with no trailing explanation... no illustration". page.tsx:78-79,217 also bakes `animate-pulse` skeleton blocks into the shared loading state. 23 `font-bold` headline sites overall (EducationPage.tsx:46, SessionDetailPage.tsx:92, ButlerDetailHeader.tsx:156, BoardHeader.tsx:97 — whose comment at line 13 cites "text-2xl font-bold" as the 'design-language.md H1 standard', a stale contract contradicting the Dispatch spec).
findings.detail: page.tsx has a second, conformant EditorialHeadingBlock (Display 44/500) — the two heading dialects live in the same file, selected by archetype. The old HeadingBlock path is what new pages get by default. Rewriting these two primitives moves ~48 consumer surfaces into the language in one diff.

findings.title: Skeleton-pulse and spinners ship on 46 sites though the Motion Vocabulary forbids them; the sanctioned FetchingDim pattern has 3 consumers
findings.evidence: spec.md:319-320: "Forbidden: ... shimmer, skeleton-pulse, count-up animations". components/ui/skeleton.tsx uses `animate-pulse` (shared primitive); 46 animate-pulse/spin/bounce/ping sites across components (page.tsx x8, SettingsPermissionsPage x5, EntityDetailPage x5, TimelineTab x5, live-status-badge, PulseStrip, ButlerHeartbeatTile...). Meanwhile components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx (built by bu-86c4c.13 exactly to replace "the list blanking to a skeleton/spinner") is imported by only 3 files.
findings.detail: The global prefers-reduced-motion floor (index.css:673-682) silences these only for users who set the OS flag — by default the console pulses on every load, violating "calm is the feature". Pattern built once (FetchingDim), never generalized: the exact failure mode this lens hunts.

findings.title: Dual token vocabulary renders the same semantic role at two different values — muted text is a different gray per dialect
findings.evidence: index.css defines both vocabularies with mismatched values: shadcn `--muted-foreground` light = oklch(0.556 0 0) (index.css:29) vs Dispatch `--mfg` = oklch(0.46 0 0) (index.css:109); shadcn's "muted" actually matches Dispatch's TERTIARY `--dim` (0.55, index.css:115). Usage split: 1,378 `muted-foreground` sites vs 174 `var(--mfg)` — so ~89% of muted text renders at what Dispatch considers tertiary/timestamp contrast, including text the bu-86c4c.16 contrast work deliberately darkened --dim to protect. Same duplication for --card vs --bg-elev, --destructive vs --red.
findings.detail: This is deeper than "two dialects mix on one screen" (known): the SAME role has two rendered values, so adjacent labels on one page differ in contrast by which import their component used. Fix is aliasing, not migration: redefine the shadcn names as `var(--mfg)` etc. in index.css and 1,378 sites snap to canonical values in one diff.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED: Butler hue identity collides (11 butlers into 8 slots) and the spec's canonical mapping table is fiction
findings.evidence: components/ui/ButlerMark.tsx:51-63 KNOWN_BUTLERS has 11 entries; :104-105 `CATEGORY_VARS[idx % CATEGORY_VARS.length]` with 8 slots → qa shares chronicler's hue, relationship shares education's, travel shares finance's. spec.md:116-131 canonical table lists butlers that do not exist (memory, calendar, household — memory is a module per the repo's own notes) and disagrees with code on every row (spec: relationship=cat-1; code: relationship=cat-2-via-wraparound).
findings.detail: Flagged in the old dossier ("butler hue identity collides, doc and code mappings disagree entirely"), not landed by any merged child. Butler-hue-as-identity is a named pillar of the north star; three identity collisions defeat it everywhere ButlerMark and SessionStripeChart render. Fix: explicit per-butler token map sized to the roster (add --category-9..11 or per-butler tokens), spec table generated from the same constant.

findings.title: Chart color language is fragmented across four dialects despite bu-86c4c.5's chart-colors.ts claiming single source of truth
findings.evidence: lib/chart-colors.ts:4 ("Single source of truth for recharts stroke/fill colors") has 7 consumers, but 8+ chart components bypass it: education hardcodes #3b82f6 (MasteryTrendChart.tsx:55-56, CrossTopicChart.tsx:42) and 5 raw hexes (MindMapGraph.tsx:18-27); chronicles AggregatePieChart.tsx:298 and AggregateStackedBar.tsx:238,242 fill from lane-taxonomy raw hexes; hex-heatmap.ts:33-37 builds a red→amber→green ramp for VISIT DENSITY (a rarely-visited place renders in error-red — all three state colors repurposed for a non-state meaning); MeasurementChart.tsx:54 carries its own oklch literal fallback; SessionStripeChart.tsx:198 uses butlerHueVar (defensible as identity but unregistered as a sanctioned chart channel).
findings.detail: The .5 fix repaired the hsl(var()) plumbing but never migrated the fleet. The mechanism gap: chart-colors.ts only models one channel (generic series). It needs four semantic channels — series, butler-identity, category, and a neutral sequential ramp for density — so every chart has an in-language answer.

findings.title: State hues carry second meanings and hardcoded fills break one theme or the other
findings.evidence: components/chronicles/lane-taxonomy.ts:122-136: lane 'eat' = #f59e0b — the EXACT --amber/degraded value — and 'rest' = #059669 (a fourth green), each lane double-encoded as a tailwind class AND a hex twin (9 unnamed hexes). components/topology/TopologyGraph.tsx:57-99 introduces a SECOND amber (#eab308 yellow-500) for degraded, blue #3b82f6 as a fourth status state (staffer-ok), purple edges (:270), and hardcodes dark-slate panel fills #1e293b/#0f172a (:185,:215) that are wrong in light mode; components/chronicles/GanttSwimlaneInner.tsx:632 zebra-stripes with rgba(0,0,0,0.02/0.04) — invisible/wrong in the CANONICAL dark theme (dark-primary doctrine, spec.md:17-18). components/chronicles/MapWidgetInner.tsx:40,180 uses hsl() red/blue literals.
findings.detail: One hue, one meaning is the first rule of the lens: amber currently means both 'degraded' and 'lunch'; two different ambers both mean 'degraded' depending on page. These are exactly the graph/canvas surfaces (topology, gantt, map) that a className-lint like bu-86c4c.6 will miss because colors flow through JS constants and SVG props, not tailwind classes.

findings.title: NOT-LANDED (partial): Dispatch atoms privately forked; micro-typography splinters into unsanctioned scales
findings.evidence: components/secrets/passport/atoms.tsx re-implements Eyebrow (:39), Voice (:106 — line-height 1.55 and arbitrary `size` prop vs spec 16px/1.6), Display (:139), PillBtn, plus its own dot/pill atoms — a full parallel kit shadowing components/ui/*. 69 inline `uppercase tracking-[0.14em]` eyebrow re-implementations vs 16 files importing ui/Eyebrow; tracking fragments into 9 values (0.14/0.12/0.10/0.1/0.08/0.06/0.04/0.02/0.01em). Voice prose renders at 15px in ingestion/timeline/EventDrawer.tsx:201-403, TimelineTab.tsx:2215, timeline/TimelineEventDrawer.tsx:62 and 17px in qa/ClaimAnchoredBlurb.tsx:43. Off-scale sizes: text-[15px] x21, text-[12px] x19, text-[8px] x3, text-[17px] x3. Status dots hand-rolled in 17 files (25 sites) vs 5 StateDot consumers; 44 files still import shadcn Card and 28 shadow-* sites persist in a "surfaces, not cards / one elevation" language; notifications/notification-stats-bar.tsx:35-59 is a full KPI fork (Cards + text-2xl font-bold + emerald/red + Title Case) alongside overview/KpiStrip (32px/500) and butler-detail KpiCell (28px mono).
findings.detail: The dossier counted "7 Eyebrow definitions, 2 Voices"; the forks still exist and inline re-implementations grew. The mechanism gap is that primitives exist but nothing makes the fork more expensive than the import — an eslint no-restricted-syntax on `tracking-[0.14em]`+`uppercase` outside ui/Eyebrow.tsx, and on `font-serif` sizes ≠16px outside ui/Voice.tsx, would make the primitive the cheapest path.

moves.title: Flip the base layer: make Dispatch the default, not the opt-in
moves.why: One diff moves every un-redesigned surface most of the way into the language and stops the drift compounding: set the root font to var(--font-sans) (killing the forbidden system-ui/Roboto default), rewrite ui/page.tsx HeadingBlock to Display/Title 500, rewrite ui/empty-state.tsx as a single Voice-italic sentence. The ~48 consumers of these two primitives inherit conformance for free, and every FUTURE page is born in-language — which no lint can achieve.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/index.css:8 (root font-family); components/ui/page.tsx:106 (HeadingBlock → Display/Title tiers, collapse the two-dialect fork with EditorialHeadingBlock); components/ui/empty-state.tsx (new API: one sentence, drop icon/description/action); delete Sidebar.tsx font-sans opt-ins; existing axe/a11y tests and e2e specs guard regressions.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: root font default + remove per-component font-sans opt-ins (verify flagship pages render Inter Tight). Slice 2: page.tsx heading unification. Slice 3: empty-state rewrite + sweep of its 24 consumers for copy (serif-italic sentence).

moves.title: Token aliasing: collapse the dual vocabulary by redefinition, then deprecate
moves.why: 1,378 muted-foreground sites cannot be hand-migrated, but they don't need to be: redefining the shadcn token names as aliases of Dispatch tokens (--muted-foreground: var(--mfg); --card: var(--bg-elev); --destructive: var(--red); --accent et al.) snaps the entire legacy fleet to canonical VALUES in one index.css diff, ending the two-grays-for-one-role defect. The in-flight bu-86c4c.6 lint then only has to ban the legacy NAMES in new code, a far smaller contract.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/index.css :root and .dark blocks (lines 18-48, 413-443); src/lib/contrast.test.ts (reads token literals — update expected values); visual sanity pass on shadcn ui/ components that assumed the old --muted-foreground lightness.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: alias the text/surface tokens + fix contrast tests. Slice 2: alias state tokens (--destructive→--red) and delete now-dead duplicates. Slice 3: hand bu-86c4c.6 the deprecated-name list.

moves.title: One chart registry with four semantic channels
moves.why: chart-colors.ts models only generic series, so every chart with a different need (butler identity, activity category, density) invents its own dialect — including repurposing the red→green STATE ramp for visit density. Extending the registry to four named channels (series: --chart-1..5; butlerIdentity: butlerHueVar; category: lane hues promoted to named index.css tokens; densityRamp: a neutral→accent sequential scale replacing hex-heatmap's red→green) gives every chart an in-language answer and makes the JS-constant color paths (topology, gantt, map) auditable in one file.
moves.integration_points: lib/chart-colors.ts (extend); index.css (add --lane-* named tokens, a sequential ramp, and topology panel tokens); migrate components/education/{MasteryTrendChart,CrossTopicChart,MindMapGraph}.tsx, components/chronicles/{lane-taxonomy.ts,AggregatePieChart,AggregateStackedBar,hex-heatmap.ts,GanttSwimlaneInner,MapWidgetInner}, components/topology/TopologyGraph.tsx; eslint no-restricted-syntax on fill="#/stroke="# in tsx.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: registry channels + lane tokens in index.css. Slice 2: chronicles migration (taxonomy, pie, stacked bar, gantt zebra via --border-soft, heatmap neutral ramp). Slice 3: topology + education migration (theme-correct panel fills, one amber, StateDot colors). Slice 4: lint rule.

moves.title: Butler-hue registry sized to the roster, spec table generated from it
moves.why: Identity is the point of butler hues; three modulo collisions (qa=chronicler, relationship=education, travel=finance) defeat it fleet-wide, and the spec's canonical table names butlers that don't exist. An explicit roster→token map with ≥11 distinct slots, consumed by ButlerMark, charts, AND the spec doc (generated table), makes hue-identity a single source of truth that cannot silently wrap.
moves.integration_points: components/ui/ButlerMark.tsx:51-106 (replace idx%8 with explicit map; add --category-9..11 to index.css light+dark with the same muted-chroma treatment); openspec/specs/dashboard-design-language/spec.md:116-131 (regenerate table from the constant, drop memory/calendar/household); consumers butlerHueVar in SessionStripeChart.tsx:198 unchanged.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: tokens + explicit map + collision test (assert all roster butlers map to distinct vars). Slice 2: spec table sync + doc note that butlerHueVar in charts is the sanctioned identity channel.

moves.title: Retire pulse: FetchingDim and honest static placeholders as the only loading language
moves.why: The Motion Vocabulary forbids skeleton-pulse yet the shared Skeleton primitive propagates it to 46 sites, while the purpose-built FetchingDim (bu-86c4c.13) has 3 consumers — the clearest built-once-never-generalized case in the codebase. Making FetchingDim + static dim placeholders the only loading treatment (and deleting ui/skeleton.tsx) is what 'calm is the feature' means at 60fps.
moves.integration_points: components/ui/skeleton.tsx (delete), components/ui/page.tsx:78-79,217 (loading blocks → static dim bars, no animation), components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx (promote; document with placeholderData pattern), the 17 files with animate-pulse status dots (live-status-badge, PulseStrip, ButlerHeartbeatTile → StateDot static states); add animate-pulse/animate-spin to bu-86c4c.6's forbidden-class list so it cannot return.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: page.tsx + skeleton.tsx replacement (covers the majority of sites via the shared shell). Slice 2: status-dot pulse removal folded into a StateDot adoption sweep (25 hand-rolled dots → StateDot). Slice 3: lint entry.

audits.ideal: The console has exactly one visual language, enforced by defaults rather than discipline: the root stylesheet IS Dispatch (Inter Tight/Source Serif/JetBrains Mono by inheritance, one token vocabulary where shadcn names are aliases of Dispatch values), the shared primitives (page shell, empty state, Eyebrow, Voice, StateDot, KpiStrip, FetchingDim) are the cheapest possible path so forks are never worth writing, every color in JS or SVG flows through one chart registry with four semantic channels, each of the 11 butlers owns a distinct hue emitted from one generated map that also renders the spec's table, and the only motion anywhere is the four-entry vocabulary — no pulse, no spin, no second amber, no red that means lunch. A new page written by a tired agent at 3am comes out in-language because there is no other language left in the tree.

audits.jarvis_gap: The speed policy (bu-86c4c.13) and fleet event bus (.8) built the right primitives, but their reach stops at the surfaces that shipped them: every drill-down in the console lands cold (zero prefetch calls in the entire frontend), three legacy per-page WebSockets still run beside the multiplexed bus and double-invalidate the same keys, bus-covered surfaces still poll at 15–30s while Approvals alone got the blessed 5-minute-reconciliation demotion, and the optimistic-mutation doctrine is a comment, not a mechanism — so hot loops like memory-fact triage still round-trip pessimistically while the north star demands same-frame apply and one-keystroke signal-to-evidence.
audits.ideal: Every navigation the owner is about to make is already warm: RowLink/DisclosureRow/palette-highlight prefetch the destination's detail queries on hover/focus via one route-registry-driven map; exactly one WebSocket exists, exposed as a subscribable bus that pages consume instead of opening their own; refetchInterval values are three named policy tokens (LIVE_FALLBACK for bus-covered, UNCOVERED, OFF) enforced by lint; every useMutation call site is machine-classified OPTIMISTIC or HONEST-PENDING through two blessed wrappers; and no filter, window, or keystroke change ever blanks a list — placeholderData + FetchingDim is the floor everywhere.

findings.title: Zero prefetching anywhere — every drill-down lands cold
findings.evidence: grep for prefetchQuery/prefetch across frontend/src returns no fetch-warming call sites (only the placeholderData comment in components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx:5); the shared row-navigation primitives RowLink (components/ui/RowLink.tsx:65) and DisclosureRow (components/ui/DisclosureRow.tsx:60) have no prefetch affordance; the only onMouseEnter handlers in the app set local hover state (e.g. components/qa/EvidenceLog.tsx:86, components/ingestion/timeline/HourFlameStrip.tsx:201).
findings.detail: The drill-down spine (.3/.4) made every signal a door, but opening any door — Sessions row → ['session-detail', butler, id] (hooks/use-sessions.ts:72), fact/entity/approval detail, timeline anchors — always starts the fetch after navigation. With a 30s staleTime default (lib/query-client.ts:6) a hover-triggered prefetchQuery would make nearly all drill-downs render instantly from cache. The skill's bar: 'preload what the user will probably want next' — currently nothing is.

findings.title: Three legacy per-page WebSockets survive the fleet event bus, and approvals events double-invalidate
findings.evidence: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1209 still mounts useApprovalsStream whose handler invalidates ['approvals','flat'|'history'|'detail'] (hooks/use-approvals-stream.ts:147-150) — the exact keys the bus registry also invalidates on the same event (hooks/event-cache-registry.ts:55-61), so every approval transition triggers two refetches per key. SpendPage.tsx:1243 opens a second socket (useSpendStream), SettingsConsolePage.tsx:524 a third (useSettingsConsoleStream).
findings.detail: Root cause is a mechanism gap: RootLayout.tsx:23 consumes useEventStream() but exposes only status — there is no context/subscribe API for pages to receive raw events from the singleton socket, so any page needing event payloads (Spend's live cost ticker, Settings console lines) must open its own connection. The registry's own doc (event-cache-registry.ts:11-15) says the bus exists so the pattern is built 'once instead of a fourth time', yet the first three copies were never retired.

findings.title: Poll demotion applied to Approvals only; bus-covered surfaces still poll at 15–30s
findings.evidence: ApprovalsPage.tsx:1206-1214 demotes its poll to a 5-minute reconciliation sweep ('a safety net… not the primary update path'). But ['butlers','board'] polls every 30s (hooks/use-butler-status-board.ts:191) despite sessionPatch invalidating it (event-cache-registry.ts:83); ['timeline'] is invalidated by session, notification, AND ingestion patches (event-cache-registry.ts:87,103) yet the ledger head polls at 15s (hooks/use-timeline-ledger.ts:29,64) atop useTimeline's 30s default (hooks/use-timeline.ts:19); ingestion events default to a 30s poll (hooks/use-ingestion-events.ts:113) despite ingestionPatch (event-cache-registry.ts:126-130); SpendPage keeps 60–120s intervals (SpendPage.tsx:603,1155,1235,1293) despite spendPatch.
findings.detail: Every bus event that invalidates these keys triggers a refetch AND the poll keeps firing — redundant load, and the inconsistency means the 'live via bus, poll as safety net' contract exists on exactly one page. NOT-LANDED in spirit: the old dossier's polling critique was resolved only where the epic child touched.

findings.title: Optimistic-mutation policy is a doc comment with no enforcement; hot-loop OPTIMISTIC-class mutations remain pessimistic
findings.evidence: Only 8 files adopted the shared helpers (use-issues, use-notifications, use-approval-decisions, use-priority-contacts, use-contacts, use-qa, use-schedules, ApprovalsPage) vs ~40 files still on plain useMutation. Clear OPTIMISTIC-class stragglers per the module's own classification (hooks/use-optimistic-mutation.ts:10-16): useConfirmFact/useRetractFact (hooks/use-memory.ts:119,137 — invalidate-on-success only), thread-affinity override upsert/delete (hooks/use-thread-affinity.ts:70,85), saved-view update/delete (hooks/use-timeline-saved-views.ts:82,98), channel-default toggle (hooks/use-channel-defaults.ts:50), ingestion-rule enable/disable (hooks/use-ingestion-rules.ts:74), finance bulk metadata patch (hooks/use-finance.ts:99).
findings.detail: Confirm/retract fact is the memory-curation triage loop — the exact keyboard-clearing flow the north star says must apply in the same frame. Nothing distinguishes a call site that was reviewed and classified HONEST-PENDING from one nobody looked at; bu-86c4c.6 covers Dispatch language linting, not mutation classification.

findings.title: Never-blank policy misses filter/window-keyed lists — day/week/filter navigation blanks the surface
findings.evidence: placeholderData: (prev)=>prev adopted on ~15 hooks + FetchingDim on 3 pages (SessionsPage, AuditLogPage, NotificationsPage), but absent from: chronicles episodes keyed on params (hooks/use-chronicles.ts:90-95 — day navigation blanks the Gantt swimlane), calendar workspace keyed on time-range params (hooks/use-calendar-workspace.ts:105-110 — week/month nav blanks the grid), all 7 finance queries keyed on params (hooks/use-finance.ts:27-83), and education/health equivalents.
findings.detail: These are exactly the interactions where the previous window's data is the correct skeleton. The FetchingDim doc (components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx:5) names the pairing as the contract, but the contract is opt-in per hook.

findings.title: Global search blanks between debounced keystrokes
