findings.evidence: hooks/use-search.ts:23-27 keys the query on debouncedQuery with no placeholderData — each debounced keystroke creates a fresh queryKey whose data is undefined, so results flash empty while the user extends their query; only the 300ms debounce (use-search.ts:10) masks it.
findings.detail: One-line fix (placeholderData: (prev)=>prev + isFetching dim) on the highest-frequency typing surface in the console.

findings.title: refetchInterval zoo — every hook hand-picks a number, no policy tiers
findings.evidence: Intervals in live code span 2s (hooks/use-whatsapp.ts:73), 5s (hooks/use-butler-logs.ts:27, use-backfill.ts:65), 15s (use-memory.ts:72,185; use-education.ts:75; use-messenger.ts:30; use-timeline-ledger.ts:29), 30s (dozens: use-health.ts, use-qa.ts:55, use-general.ts, use-chronicles.ts defaults…), 60s, 120s, and 5min — with no shared constants or documented rule for which tier a surface belongs to.
findings.detail: The skill's bar: 'cache invalidation states its rule.' Without named tiers, bus-covered vs uncovered surfaces are indistinguishable at the call site and every new hook re-decides — this is how finding 3's drift keeps regenerating.

moves.title: Intent prefetch through RowLink/DisclosureRow + route registry
moves.why: Makes every drill-down in the spine render instantly from cache — the single biggest perceived-latency win available, and it lands at one integration point instead of per-page.
moves.integration_points: components/ui/RowLink.tsx and DisclosureRow.tsx (add optional prefetch prop wired to onMouseEnter/onFocus with a ~75ms intent delay); lib/route-registry.ts (register detail-query builders — e.g. session-detail, memory-fact, approval-detail — beside their routes so rows AND cmdk palette highlight share one prefetch map); lib/query-client.ts (queryClient.prefetchQuery with existing 30s staleTime).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: usePrefetchOnIntent hook + RowLink prop, wired to SessionsPage rows → ['session-detail']. Slice 2: timeline ledger rows + approvals rail. Slice 3: palette-highlight prefetch from the route registry.

moves.title: One socket: subscribable event-bus context, retire the three legacy streams
moves.why: Eliminates duplicate invalidation (2× refetch per approval event today), drops to a single WS connection app-wide, and unblocks any future page needing live payloads without a bespoke socket.
moves.integration_points: layouts/RootLayout.tsx (wrap in EventBusProvider exposing subscribe(type, cb) backed by the existing onEvent param of use-event-stream.ts:34); SpendPage.tsx:1243 (port streamedCostUsd ticker to subscribe('spend')); SettingsConsolePage.tsx:524 (port console lines to a bus event type — may need the settings-console payload added to src/butlers/api/routers/events.py EVENT_TYPES); ApprovalsPage.tsx:1209 (delete the call); then delete use-approvals-stream.ts, use-spend-stream.ts, use-settings-console-stream.ts.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: provider + subscribe API + delete useApprovalsStream (pure win, no backend change). Slice 2: spend ticker port. Slice 3: settings-console port + backend event type.

moves.title: Poll-policy tokens keyed to bus coverage, lint-enforced
moves.why: Turns the blessed Approvals pattern (bus-live + 5-min reconciliation) into the default for every bus-covered surface and makes the interval zoo impossible to regrow.
moves.integration_points: New lib/poll-policy.ts exporting POLL.RECONCILE (5min, bus-covered), POLL.UNCOVERED (30s), POLL.OFF; demote use-butler-status-board.ts:191, use-timeline-ledger.ts:29, use-timeline.ts:19, use-ingestion-events.ts:113, SpendPage.tsx:603/1155/1235/1293 to POLL.RECONCILE; eslint no-restricted-syntax rule banning numeric refetchInterval literals (frontend CI already runs eslint — the enforcement lane exists).
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: tokens + demote the four bus-covered surfaces. Slice 2: sweep remaining hooks onto tokens + lint rule.

moves.title: Mutation classification made mechanical: two blessed wrappers + lint ban on bare useMutation
moves.why: The policy's own doc demands every call site be classified but nothing checks it; making classification structural converts the remaining ~40 files from 'unreviewed' to 'explicitly OPTIMISTIC or HONEST-PENDING' and can never drift.
moves.integration_points: hooks/use-optimistic-mutation.ts (add a thin useHonestPendingMutation re-export so intent is declared in code); eslint no-restricted-imports banning useMutation from '@tanstack/react-query' outside the two wrappers; convert the six named stragglers — use-memory.ts:119/137 (confirm/retract fact, do first: hot triage loop), use-thread-affinity.ts:70/85, use-timeline-saved-views.ts:82/98, use-channel-defaults.ts:50, use-ingestion-rules.ts:74, use-finance.ts:99 — to useOptimisticListMutation.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: convert confirm/retract fact + saved-views. Slice 2: remaining four. Slice 3: wrapper + lint rule + mechanical rename of all HONEST-PENDING sites.

moves.title: Never-blank floor: shared windowed-list query wrapper
moves.why: Generalizes placeholderData+FetchingDim from 3 pages to every filter/window-keyed surface so changing a day, week, filter, or search query never blanks what the owner is reading.
moves.integration_points: New useWindowedListQuery wrapper (or just add placeholderData:(prev)=>prev) in hooks/use-chronicles.ts:90, use-calendar-workspace.ts:105, use-finance.ts:27-83, use-search.ts:23; pair each consuming page with components/ui/fetching-dim.tsx per its documented contract.
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: search + chronicles episodes (highest-frequency interactions). Slice 2: calendar workspace + finance + education/health sweep.

audits.jarvis_gap: The a11y floor (bu-86c4c.16) is real — jsx-a11y lint, contrast-locked tokens, a CSS reduced-motion kill-switch, and one gold-standard drawer — but its reach is a lottery by surface. The two signature JARVIS surfaces are the least accessible: the ONE command spine (EntityFinder) is a fake modal that leaks Tab focus behind its own overlay and never restores focus, and the live event-stream heartbeat degrades silently for anyone not looking at the pixels ("every degraded source names itself" is currently visual-only). Each accessibility pattern was built once, correctly, in exactly one place — modal choreography in the ingestion drawer, reduced-motion gating in one sparkline, real-page axe tests on 3 of 38 pages — and never generalized into a mechanism, so every new surface re-rolls the dice.
audits.ideal: One overlay contract, one announcer, one motion policy, one axe gate — all mechanisms, not conventions. Every modal/drawer/palette in the app gets identical choreography (focus-in, trap, Escape, focus-restore, sr-only status region) from a single shared implementation, enforced by lint so a hand-rolled `fixed inset-0` overlay cannot merge. A single shell-level live region narrates what the pixels already say: stream connected/reconnecting/down, route changes, new-event counts. prefers-reduced-motion governs ALL motion — CSS, recharts mount animations, smooth scrolls — via shared helpers with a lint ban on raw escape hatches. And the real-routed-page axe test iterates the route registry, so a page cannot exist without an axe pass. The result: the keyboard-only, screen-reader, and motion-sensitive operator gets the same five-second verdict and under-a-minute queue-clear the sighted mouse user gets.

findings.title: The one command spine (EntityFinder) is a fake modal: Tab leaks focus behind the overlay, no dialog semantics, no focus restore
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx:431-453 — the palette is a raw div overlay + cmdk Command, with no role="dialog"/aria-modal and no focus trap. The onKeyDown at :449 only preventDefaults Tab when `activeResult` (an ENTITY result) exists; when the query matches only pages/butlers/actions (activeResult null, :390-413 derives it exclusively from entity lists), Tab moves focus to the page BEHIND the black/60 overlay while the palette stays open. On close (Esc/select), focus is never returned to the header trigger — the focused input unmounts and focus falls to <body>. Every Radix Dialog/Sheet in ui/ does all of this correctly; the app's single most important surface is the one exempt from it.
findings.detail: Also: input at :468 is outline-none (acceptable inside a single-field palette, but part of the same hand-rolled divergence). Fix is to render through the shared dialog choreography (or cmdk's own Command.Dialog which wraps Radix), keep the Tab=hop override, and preventDefault Tab when no entity is active.

findings.title: Modal/drawer choreography was built once (ingestion EventDrawer) and not generalized — four overlays, four different a11y qualities
findings.evidence: Gold standard: frontend/src/components/ingestion/timeline/EventDrawer.tsx:554-575 (focus-in on open, Escape closes + returns focus to triggering row, sr-only role="status" live region at :674). Its sibling built on the SAME useEventDrawerState: frontend/src/components/timeline/TimelineEventDrawer.tsx:129-142 (/timeline, bu-86c4c.10) has NONE of it — no focus-in, no Escape handler, no focus restore, just an aria-label and a close button. frontend/src/components/calendar/CalendarAgendaView.tsx:44-48 declares role="dialog" aria-modal="true" with no focus trap, no focus-in, no Escape — aria-modal without focus management hides the background from screen readers while keyboard focus remains in it (worse than no ARIA). frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerManagementTab.tsx:32-53 ModalBackdrop: Escape only, no dialog role, no focus trap/restore.
findings.detail: The failure scenario for CalendarAgendaView: SR user opens agenda, presses Tab, lands on controls the SR reports don't exist (aria-modal excludes them); keyboard user opens ButlerManagementTab modal, Tab walks out into the page behind it. One shared choreography (Radix or a useModalChoreography hook extracted from EventDrawer) fixes all four.

findings.title: Reduced-motion floor is CSS-only; recharts mount animations and smooth scrolls escape it, with three divergent chart conventions
findings.evidence: frontend/src/index.css:660-680 is the global floor, but it only reaches CSS animation/transition. Recharts animations are rAF-driven: 7 chart files leave the default mount animation running with no gating (frontend/src/components/costs/CostChart.tsx, education/CrossTopicChart.tsx, education/MasteryTrendChart.tsx, chronicles/AggregatePieChart.tsx, butler-detail/ButlerFinanceFinancesTab.tsx, system/DbSizeTile.tsx, health/MeasurementChart.tsx — all import recharts, zero isAnimationActive), ~8 files hardcode isAnimationActive={false}, and exactly one gates on the hook (butler-detail/ButlerHealthMeasurementsTab.tsx:336,344 via usePrefersReducedMotion). Five scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"}) sites also ignore the preference: pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:2918, pages/CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:2711, components/ingestion/TimelineTab.tsx:1145, components/chat/MessageThread.tsx:266, components/ingestion/timeline/EventDrawer.tsx:627.
findings.detail: usePrefersReducedMotion exists (frontend/src/hooks/use-prefers-reduced-motion.ts) and is used by only 2 non-test components. Mechanism, not symptom-fixes: a shared chartAnimationProps() default + a smoothScrollIntoView() helper, plus a no-restricted-syntax lint entry (the codebase already uses this pattern for hsl(var()) in eslint.config).

findings.title: Live event-stream state changes and live-tail arrivals are never announced — 'every degraded source names itself' is visual-only
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/layout/LiveIndicator.tsx:56-69 — the shell heartbeat swaps its text Live→Reconnecting→Offline inside a plain span (title tooltip only, no role="status"/aria-live), so a screen-reader user never hears the fleet stream drop; the same span is `hidden ... sm:inline-flex`, so on mobile NO user gets the degraded-stream signal at all. frontend/src/components/timeline/NewEventsPill.tsx:22-33 — the "N new events" affordance mounts/updates silently (no live region), so an SR user paging history never learns events accumulated. Contrast: the ingestion EventDrawer already ships an sr-only role="status" region (EventDrawer.tsx:674) proving the pattern exists in-repo.
findings.detail: One shell-level sr-only aria-live="polite" region fed by useEventStream status transitions (debounced: announce only open→reconnecting→down edges) covers LiveIndicator, and the same region can take route-change announcements (see SPA navigation: page.tsx manages document.title at frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:338-343, but title changes are not announced by SRs in SPAs and Shell has no route announcer or skip-to-content link — frontend/src/components/layout/Shell.tsx:89).

findings.title: Secrets passport strips keyboard focus visibility on ~10 edit fields (WCAG 2.4.7)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/pages.tsx:1471,1971,2022,2042,2638,3110,3134,3150,3172 — textareas/inputs (including the rotate-credential paste field) with `outline-none` and no focus-visible replacement in className or inline style (verified :1460-1480: static border var(--border-strong), no focus style). frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/Spine.tsx:53 — the '/' credential search input, same. The passport's bespoke design-token system diverged from shared ui/input.tsx, which carries a proper focus ring.
findings.detail: A keyboard user rotating a credential — the single most sensitive write on the page — cannot see which field has focus. Fix inside the passport's token language: a focus-visible ring on var(--fg) or border-strong→fg swap, applied via one shared passport field class.

findings.title: Real-routed-page axe testing covers 3 of 38 pages — the pattern exists but was never generalized
findings.evidence: Only frontend/src/pages/ButlersPage.a11y.test.tsx, frontend/src/pages/ButlerDetailPage.a11y.test.tsx, and frontend/src/components/ingestion/TimelineTab.a11y.test.tsx exist (repo-wide grep for jest-axe/vitest-axe), against 38 page components in frontend/src/pages/. The ButlersPage file's own header (:1-19) documents why stub-based axe was theater and how the real-page + mocked-data-layer pattern works — that rationale applies to every other page, including ones with confirmed violations this sweep found (EntityDetailPage, CalendarAgendaView).
findings.detail: Generalize via the route registry (frontend/src/lib/route-registry.ts ALL_ROUTES): one parameterized suite that mounts each registered route with the standard data-layer mocks and runs axe across its loading/empty/error/populated states, with an explicit allowlist for pages needing bespoke mocks.

findings.title: Icon-only edit controls with no accessible name on the entity rename flow
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx:3072-3100 — three ghost icon Buttons (Check=save, X=cancel, Pencil=start-edit) around the canonical-name editor have no aria-label, sr-only text, or title; their only content is a lucide icon. jsx-a11y has no enabled rule for nameless buttons and no axe test covers this page, so the lint+axe floor structurally cannot catch this class.
findings.detail: SR announces three blank 'button's on the primary identity-editing control of the entity dossier. Same-page symptom of finding 6 (axe coverage); direct fix is three aria-labels, mechanism fix is the registry-driven axe sweep.

findings.title: Global single-key shortcut guard misses SELECT and contentEditable targets
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-keyboard-shortcuts.ts:20-21 — the editable-target guard checks only tagName INPUT/TEXTAREA (window-level keydown, 4 window keydown listeners repo-wide). A native <select> or any contentEditable region focused while typing 'g'/'j'/'k'/'/' fires page shortcuts. NOTE: bu-5o22a (shared editable-field keydown guard) is the in-flight home for this mechanism — this is scope input for it (the shared guard must cover SELECT, contentEditable, and open-modal suspension), not a new bead.
findings.detail: Reported only as an extension of known bu-5o22a scope; the guard should also suspend page-level single-key shortcuts while any dialog/palette is open, which the shared overlay contract (move 1) can expose as state.

moves.title: One overlay contract: shared modal choreography + lint ban on hand-rolled overlays
moves.why: Four overlays currently ship four different a11y qualities (findings 1-2); the correct implementation already exists in EventDrawer. A single mechanism makes the next drawer accessible by construction — including the command spine, the console's front door.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Extract useModalChoreography (focus-in, trap, Escape, focus-restore, optional sr-only status region) from ingestion EventDrawer; 2) migrate EntityFinder (keep Tab=hop but trap Tab when no entity active; restore focus on close; add role=dialog/aria-modal), TimelineEventDrawer, CalendarAgendaView, ButlerManagementTab ModalBackdrop; 3) add no-restricted-syntax lint entry flagging `fixed inset-0` + z-50 overlay JSX outside src/components/ui/, mirroring the existing hsl(var()) guard.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/ingestion/timeline/EventDrawer.tsx (source of truth), frontend/src/components/layout/EntityFinder.tsx, frontend/src/components/timeline/TimelineEventDrawer.tsx, frontend/src/components/calendar/CalendarAgendaView.tsx, frontend/src/components/butler-detail/ButlerManagementTab.tsx, frontend/eslint.config.js

moves.title: Shell announcer: one sr-only live region for stream state, route changes, and live-tail arrivals
moves.why: Earned calm must be perceivable without sight: today the fleet stream degrades, routes change, and new events accumulate in total silence for SR users (finding 4), and on mobile the stream indicator vanishes entirely.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add a single aria-live=polite sr-only region to Shell; 2) feed it debounced useEventStream status EDGES ('Fleet stream reconnecting', 'Fleet stream offline', 'Fleet stream restored'); 3) announce route changes from the existing Page title effect (page.tsx already owns titles); 4) have NewEventsPill publish its count to the same region; 5) render LiveIndicator on mobile (dot-only) instead of hiding it.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/layout/Shell.tsx, frontend/src/components/layout/LiveIndicator.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/use-event-stream.ts, frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:338, frontend/src/components/timeline/NewEventsPill.tsx

moves.title: Motion policy for JS: chart animation defaults + smooth-scroll helper honoring prefers-reduced-motion, lint-enforced
moves.why: The CSS reduced-motion floor gives false confidence — all recharts mount animations and 5 smooth scrolls bypass it, and chart animation handling has three divergent conventions across 26 chart files (finding 3).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Add chartAnimationProps() beside src/lib/chart-colors.ts returning {isAnimationActive: !prefersReducedMotion}; apply to the 7 ungated chart files (or standardize on isAnimationActive={false} everywhere — charts on an operator console arguably should never mount-animate); 2) add smoothScrollIntoView(el, opts) that downgrades behavior to 'auto' under reduced motion; migrate the 5 call sites; 3) lint: no-restricted-syntax for `behavior: "smooth"` and a rule requiring isAnimationActive on recharts series components.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/lib/chart-colors.ts (sibling module), frontend/src/hooks/use-prefers-reduced-motion.ts, frontend/eslint.config.js, 7 ungated chart files + 5 scrollIntoView sites listed in finding 3

moves.title: Registry-driven axe sweep: every route in ALL_ROUTES gets a real-page axe pass
moves.why: The axe floor is correct but reaches 3/38 pages; nameless icon buttons on EntityDetailPage prove violations live in the uncovered 35. Route-registry iteration turns per-page tests into a structural gate — a new page cannot ship without one (finding 6-7).
moves.slice_plan: 1) Build a shared mount harness (MemoryRouter + QueryClient + standard data-layer mocks, following ButlersPage.a11y.test.tsx's documented pattern); 2) parameterized suite over ALL_ROUTES with a per-route mock/skip manifest — start permissive (skip-with-reason), burn down; 3) fix violations it surfaces (EntityDetailPage aria-labels first); 4) CI treats a route absent from both the suite and the skip manifest as a failure.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/lib/route-registry.ts (ALL_ROUTES), frontend/src/pages/ButlersPage.a11y.test.tsx (pattern source), frontend/src/test/setup.ts, frontend CI eslint/vitest job

moves.title: Passport focus restoration: one focus-visible treatment for all bespoke secrets fields
moves.why: Keyboard focus is invisible on the credential-rotation and search fields of the most sensitive write surface in the console (finding 5) — a WCAG 2.4.7 failure introduced by the passport's parallel token system.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Define one passport field focus style inside its token language (e.g. focus-visible border-color var(--fg) + 1px ring) as a shared class/const guarded by the existing passport design-token lint rule; 2) apply to the ~10 outline-none fields in pages.tsx and Spine.tsx; 3) extend src/lib/contrast.test.ts to assert the focus indicator pair meets 3:1 in both themes.
moves.integration_points: frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/pages.tsx, frontend/src/components/secrets/passport/Spine.tsx, frontend/src/lib/contrast.test.ts, the passport design-token eslint guard

audits.jarvis_gap: The fleet's perception surface is email-heavy and manual-entry-heavy: gmail/calendar/drive/google-health/owntracks/spotify/steam/home-assistant/telegram/whatsapp/discord/live-listener all exist, but three manifesto-level promises are structurally unfulfillable with current sources — finance sees only spend that emails a receipt, travel promises real-time delay/gate alerts with no flight-status feed, and chronicler/lifestyle have no signal for the largest share of a knowledge-worker's day (screen and browser activity). A JARVIS perceives the owner's money, movement-in-progress, and attention directly; today those arrive late, by email, or not at all.

findings.title: Travel manifesto promises real-time delay/gate alerts but no flight-status source exists anywhere
findings.evidence: roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md ('We will alert you to delays and gate changes before the airlines announce them'; 'surfaced the moment they happen') vs src/butlers/connectors/ containing no flight/airline connector and openspec/specs/ having no connector-flight* spec; travel ingestion is gmail-email-only and travel.legs (roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:53) stores static booking data with no live-status columns. The promise is binding per vision.md rule 6 and is currently impossible to fulfill.
findings.detail: Airlines announce gate changes/delays via their ops APIs long before (or instead of) email. Email-only ingestion means the butler learns of a delay when the owner's inbox does — often after the owner is already at the wrong gate.

findings.title: Finance butler perceives only spend that emails a receipt; no bank/transaction feed connector
findings.evidence: roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md ('The answers come from your actual email history'); openspec/specs/finance-data-import/spec.md is manual CSV import (Chase/Amex/CapitalOne header detection); openspec/specs/bulk-transaction-ingestion exists as a normalization path but no connector feeds it — grep of src/butlers/connectors/ shows zero bank/plaid/simplefin references.
findings.detail: Card-present transactions, bank transfers, ATM withdrawals, and merchants that don't email receipts are invisible. The manifesto's 'never surprise you with a bill' and 'find any transaction' promises silently degrade to 'any transaction that happened to email you'.

findings.title: Chronicler's evidence base has no digital-activity source despite an adapter-registration path built for it
findings.evidence: roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md ('LLM sessions, the calendar events you actually attended, the Spotify session summaries, and, over time, everything else the system honestly knows'); openspec/specs/chronicler-source-compatibility/spec.md:52-59 defines the chronicler_adapter registration mechanism for new sources; no connector captures screen time, app usage, or browsing.
findings.detail: For a desk-working owner, screen activity is the majority of waking evidence. Chronicler can currently reconstruct music, meetings, and location, but the 6 hours between them are a blank — the biggest single hole in retrospective time.

findings.title: Weather is consumed as an input by three butler skills but no weather source exists in the system
findings.evidence: grep 'weather' hits roster/home/.agents/skills/energy/SKILL.md, roster/travel/.agents/skills/pre-trip-checklist/SKILL.md, roster/switchboard/.agents/skills/message-triage/SKILL.md — yet src/butlers/modules/ and src/butlers/connectors/ contain no weather module/connector and openspec/specs/ has none (seasonal-awareness is calendar-period-based, not meteorological).
findings.detail: Sessions that need weather must ad-hoc web-search inside an ephemeral LLM run or fabricate — the latter violates the no-fabrication doctrine. A deterministic keyless source (Open-Meteo) makes this a solved, testable input.

findings.title: Lifestyle manifesto covers shows/books/reading but only music (spotify) and gaming (steam) have connectors
findings.evidence: roster/lifestyle/MANIFESTO.md ('Track what you're consuming: the show you just started, the book you're reading, the game you've been playing') vs connector inventory in src/butlers/connectors/ — video, reading, and browsing consumption all require manual owner logging.
findings.detail: The taste-mirror promise decays to whatever the owner remembers to log. An ActivityWatch web-watcher bucket (proposal 3) covers most of this passively without a per-service (Netflix/YouTube/Kindle) connector zoo.

findings.title: Order confirmations are already perceived via gmail but delivery progress is not — packages go dark after purchase
findings.evidence: src/butlers/connectors/gmail.py ingests order/shipping emails (finance manifesto explicitly claims receipts), but no connector polls carrier/tracking APIs; no parcel/tracking spec in openspec/specs/; no butler manifesto currently owns delivery logistics.
findings.detail: The system knows a package exists (order email) but cannot answer 'is anything arriving today?' — a classic daily-briefing item. The tracking number is already in the ingested payload; only the polling leg is missing.

findings.title: Structural templates for every proposed connector class already exist, making build costs genuinely M not L
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/connector-google-health/spec.md ('pure polling-and-ingest connector and structurally mirrors connector-spotify' with per-account state diffing); openspec/specs/connector-owntracks/spec.md (webhook-server pattern); .claude/skills/adding-connectors-and-modules/SKILL.md codifies the 4-component pattern (account registry, module, connector, dashboard) with reference checklists.
findings.detail: Bank-feed and flight-status connectors are poll+state-diff clones of google_health/spotify; a parcel connector is a watch-table poller; weather needs no account registry at all (keyless API). None require new core infrastructure — all fit rule 2 (modules only add tools) and rule 7 (transport stays in connectors).

findings.title: Home-domain perception is alive, not dead — bu-zquce.7's original premise is stale, so no home-sensor re-proposal is warranted
findings.evidence: bd show bu-zquce.7 notes: 'home_assistant_rest.py is NO LONGER dead code - PR #2740 (bu-2gfh9) wired HARestPoller/HAFallbackController into home_assistant.py _main as the REST polling fallback'; src/butlers/connectors/home_assistant*.py is a live 8-file pipeline.
findings.detail: Recorded so the synthesizer does not double-count: smart-home and music domains are covered by live connectors; this audit deliberately proposes nothing there.

moves.title: connector-simplefin: sovereign bank-transaction feed for the finance butler
moves.why: Closes the finance butler's largest perception gap — spend that never emails a receipt (card-present, transfers, ATM, subscriptions billed silently). SimpleFIN Bridge is the sovereignty-aligned choice: one owner-held access token, no Plaid enterprise contract, user revocable; add GoCardless Bank Account Data as an alternate provider for EU accounts. Transactions land in the same finance.transactions normalization path CSV import already uses, so every downstream promise (subscriptions, monthly overview, anomaly detection per finance-anomaly-detection spec) immediately gets truer data.
moves.integration_points: New src/butlers/connectors/simplefin.py (poll + state-diff, structurally mirrors connector-spotify/google_health per its spec); public.simplefin_accounts registry migration per .claude/skills/adding-connectors-and-modules/references/account-registry-pattern.md with access token as secured entity_info (RFC 0004 new type simplefin_access_token); RFC 0003 amendment registering channel=simplefin/provider=simplefin; envelopes → Switchboard → finance butler, deduped into finance.transactions via the openspec/specs/bulk-transaction-ingestion pipeline; dashboard account CRUD per dashboard-google-accounts pattern (GET/POST/DELETE /api/simplefin/accounts); new openspec/specs/connector-simplefin + simplefin-account-registry. Serves roster/finance/MANIFESTO.md directly (requires a one-line amendment: 'your actual email history' becomes 'your email and bank feeds').
moves.slice_plan: 1) account registry + token validation + dashboard connect; 2) connector poll loop with first-poll baseline (no historical flood) + ingest.v1 envelopes; 3) finance-side dedupe against email-derived transactions (match on amount+date+merchant fuzzy) so the same purchase seen twice becomes one enriched row.

moves.title: connector-flightstatus: live flight watch fulfilling the travel butler's real-time promise
moves.why: The travel manifesto's most concrete promise ('alert you to delays and gate changes before the airlines announce them') is unfulfillable today — email-only ingestion learns of changes when the airline mails. A watch-based poller (FlightAware AeroAPI personal tier, or aviationstack) turns booked legs into live-tracked objects for the 48h around departure, emitting delay/gate/cancel transition events the travel butler converts to owner notifications.
moves.integration_points: New src/butlers/connectors/flightstatus.py; connector-owned connectors.flight_watches table (flight number, date, PNR-free — populated when the travel butler's email-parsing session calls a new watch_flight MCP tool in roster/travel/tools/, keeping the connector out of the travel schema per vision.md rule 3); migration adding live-status columns (status, gate, delay_minutes, last_status_at) to travel.legs (roster/travel/migrations/001_travel_tables.py:53); RFC 0003 channel=flightstatus/provider=flightaware; API key as secured entity_info; state-diff only emits on change (delay threshold config); new openspec/specs/connector-flightstatus. Serves roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md verbatim — no amendment needed, this is the missing half of an existing promise.
moves.slice_plan: 1) flight_watches table + watch_flight/unwatch tool + auto-watch on leg creation; 2) poller with adaptive cadence (6h out: hourly; 2h out: every 5min) + transition envelopes; 3) travel butler notification templates (gate change, delay >15min, cancellation with rebooking context) + dashboard trip-timeline live-status chips.

moves.title: connector-activitywatch: passive digital-activity evidence for Chronicler and Lifestyle
moves.why: The single biggest hole in Chronicler's retrospective record is what the owner did on their machines — the majority of a desk-worker's day. ActivityWatch is self-hosted, open-source, local-only (REST on localhost:5600) — perfect sovereignty fit, zero cloud dependency. Window/AFK/browser buckets become honest episodes ('coding on butlers 09:12–11:40', 'watched YouTube 40min'), which also passively fulfills Lifestyle's 'track what you're consuming' promise for video/reading without a per-service connector zoo.
moves.integration_points: New src/butlers/connectors/activitywatch.py polling GET /api/0/buckets + /events with cursor per bucket (cursor_store.py already exists); pre-aggregation in the connector (coalesce raw window events into >=N-minute app/domain episodes — never ship raw keystroke-level titles) with sensitivity gating via the existing IngestionPolicyEvaluator source-filter path and control.policy_tier; RFC 0003 channel=activitywatch/provider=activitywatch; no account registry needed (local socket — note the deviation in the spec like owntracks does); Chronicler adapter registered per openspec/specs/chronicler-source-compatibility/spec.md:52 (chronicler_adapter mode) projecting episodes with provenance + retention class; lifestyle butler consumes weekly aggregates for its digest. Serves roster/chronicler/MANIFESTO.md ('everything else the system honestly knows') and roster/lifestyle/MANIFESTO.md; Chronicler needs no amendment, Lifestyle a minor one (passive consumption capture).
moves.slice_plan: 1) connector + episode coalescing + baseline-on-first-poll; 2) Chronicler adapter + retention/sensitivity classes (browser domains only, no full URLs by default); 3) lifestyle weekly-digest integration + dashboard day-ribbon rendering via the in-flight Chronicler redesign's episode surface (bu-jc6htw covers UI, not this source).

moves.title: module-weather: deterministic keyless weather tools + severe-alert emitter
moves.why: Three butler skills already assume weather as an input (home energy, travel pre-trip, switchboard triage) with no source behind them — sessions must web-search or fabricate, and fabrication violates doctrine. Open-Meteo is keyless, free for personal use, and returns structured forecasts; wiring it as a shared module makes weather a solved deterministic input for every butler, plus a tiny alert path for severe conditions keyed to the owner's last-known owntracks location.
moves.integration_points: New shared module src/butlers/modules/weather.py implementing the Module ABC (src/butlers/modules/base.py) with tools weather_current/weather_forecast/weather_alerts (lat/lon or named-place; default = last owntracks position read via a switchboard-brokered lookup, not cross-schema); enable in roster/home, roster/travel, roster/health, roster/switchboard butler.toml [modules.weather]; optional micro-connector (or a scheduled home-butler task — cheaper, no new process) emitting severe-weather envelopes; new openspec/specs/module-weather noting the no-account-registry deviation (keyless API). Serves roster/home/MANIFESTO.md (comfort/energy awareness) and roster/travel/MANIFESTO.md (pre-trip prep); no manifesto amendments required — this backfills promises already made.
moves.slice_plan: 1) module + tools + tests against recorded Open-Meteo fixtures; 2) enable per-butler + update the three skills to call the tool instead of hand-waving; 3) severe-alert scheduled check with notify() on threshold crossings.

moves.title: connector-parcels: delivery tracking that finishes the story gmail starts
moves.why: The system already perceives every order at purchase time (gmail ingests the confirmation, finance records the spend) then goes blind until a delivery email maybe arrives. A watch-table poller against a unified tracking API (17track; carrier-direct fallback) turns tracking numbers the fleet already possesses into arrival awareness — 'two packages arriving today' is a canonical morning-briefing line and an errand-planning input the owner currently supplies manually.
moves.integration_points: New src/butlers/connectors/parcels.py polling a connectors.parcel_watches table (tracking_number, carrier, status, eta, terminal-state cleanup); populated via a new track_parcel MCP tool the general butler calls when its email-triage session sees a shipping confirmation (tracking numbers are already in gmail-ingested payload.raw); RFC 0003 channel=parcels/provider=17track; API key as secured entity_info per RFC 0004; transition-only envelopes (out_for_delivery, delivered, exception) → Switchboard → general butler; briefing contribution via the existing cross-butler-briefing-contribution spec. No butler currently owns delivery logistics: this implies a small amendment to roster/general/MANIFESTO.md (the 'capture anything' second-brain absorbing logistics awareness) — flagging that explicitly rather than inventing a new butler for one connector.
moves.slice_plan: 1) parcel_watches table + track_parcel tool + manual-add from dashboard; 2) poller with per-parcel backoff and terminal-state expiry; 3) general-butler extraction skill (shipping email → track_parcel) + briefing line + notify-on-delivered.

findings.title: Every LLM call in the ecosystem — including 'lightweight' single-turn discretion screening — is a cold CLI subprocess spawn
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core/runtimes/claude_code.py:439 (asyncio.create_subprocess_exec per invoke); src/butlers/connectors/discretion_dispatcher.py:226-239 — DiscretionDispatcher.call() routes through the same RuntimeAdapter.invoke() subprocess path with mcp_servers={} and max_turns=1. No runtime_type in src/butlers/core/runtimes/ (base/claude_code/codex/gemini/opencode) calls a provider API directly. Per-message connector screening (telegram_user_client.py:357, whatsapp_user_client.py:543, live_listener/connector.py:208, home_assistant_pipeline.py:33) each pay full CLI bootstrap for a one-shot yes/no classification.
findings.detail: An interactive Telegram reply chains TWO serial cold spawns: switchboard classification session (pipeline.py:1976-1990, Complexity.CHEAP, full claude CLI + MCP handshake to call route_to_butler) then the target butler's route session (core_tools/_routing.py:546). CLI process startup + MCP discovery is pure overhead on both hops and on every high-volume screening call.

findings.title: Trigger-to-act latency is unmeasured — no phase decomposition anywhere in the spine
findings.evidence: grep for startup/time-to-first-token/spawn-overhead metrics across src/butlers returns nothing; the only timings are total session duration_ms (spawner.py:1741) and switchboard routing_decision_latency_ms (modules/pipeline.py:1994). core/metrics.py has queue-depth gauges but no queue-WAIT, context-assembly, process-startup, or first-stream-event timers.
findings.detail: The pursuit question 'where does the loop waste latency' is currently unanswerable from production data: global-semaphore wait (spawner.py:678), per-butler semaphore wait (712), context fetches (1341-1380), adapter subprocess boot, and model time are all folded into one number.

findings.title: Switchboard classification sessions are mislabeled trigger_source="tick"
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1979-1984 — dispatch_kwargs = {"prompt": routing_prompt, "trigger_source": "tick", ...}. Spend routing rules match on trigger (model_routing.py:446-495), sessions/audit/ledger joins use trigger_source.
findings.detail: Per-message classification spend is indistinguishable from scheduler-tick spend in sessions, audit entries, and spend-rule targeting; an operator rule condition {"trigger": "route"} silently never matches the classifier, and cost-per-inbound-message cannot be computed.

findings.title: Scheduled prompt tasks spawn unconditionally; several pay a workhorse session to conclude 'do nothing'
findings.evidence: core/scheduler.py:1843-1858 dispatches every claimed prompt-mode occurrence straight to spawner.trigger with no precondition support. Roster prompts encode the no-op check inside the LLM: roster/education/butler.toml:78 ('If there are ZERO pending reviews across all maps: do nothing'), roster/travel/butler.toml:49 ('If nothing is upcoming, do not send a message'), roster/finance/butler.toml:54 (STEP 2 early exit).
findings.detail: The deterministic emptiness check (pending-review count, upcoming-trip count, unreconciled-bill count) is evaluated by a full workhorse-tier session instead of a SQL query in the daemon. This is recurring daily/6-hourly waste across the roster.

findings.title: Complexity tier is effectively unused by the roster: 1 of ~60 schedule entries sets it, everything else defaults WORKHORSE
findings.evidence: grep 'complexity' across roster/*/butler.toml matches only roster/chronicler/butler.toml:118 (reasoning, day_close). core/scheduler.py:37 _DEFAULT_COMPLEXITY = Complexity.WORKHORSE.value; spawner.py:530 default WORKHORSE.
findings.detail: The six-tier catalog (complexity-classification spec) and the per-segment classifier tiering (pipeline.py:454-459 routing prompt) exist, but the scheduled-work half of the fleet never exercises cheap-tier routing — trivial status checks and heavy synthesis run on the same tier.

findings.title: Connector discretion spend is a black hole: attributed to '__discretion__' with NULL session_id and no purpose dimension
findings.evidence: connectors/discretion_dispatcher.py:106 (butler_name default "__discretion__"), :251-258 (record_token_usage with session_id=None); token_usage_ledger columns are only catalog_entry_id/butler_name/session_id/tokens (model_routing.py:370-374). All four connector callers use the default butler_name.
findings.detail: High-volume per-message screening (telegram user client, whatsapp, live listener, home assistant) is invisible in per-butler spend views, cannot be drilled to a source, and cannot be targeted by spend rules (trigger_source=None makes trigger constraints fail-closed per model_routing.py:481-483).

findings.title: No conversation/session continuity: every interactive turn re-buys the full context as fresh input tokens
findings.evidence: core/runtimes/claude_code.py has no --resume/--continue support (grep matches only loop keywords); pipeline.py:98-283 reloads and re-serializes conversation history as prompt text per message; core_tools/_routing.py:140-141 re-injects 'CONVERSATION HISTORY:' text into the target session each turn.
findings.detail: A 10-turn Telegram exchange pays classification + target-session cold spawn + full history re-tokenization 10 times. _compose_system_prompt (spawner_context.py:109-139) is cache-prefix-ordered, but cross-invocation provider prompt-cache hits are luck-of-TTL, not designed.

findings.title: Model resolution performs an unconditional round-robin counter WRITE on every spawn
findings.evidence: model_routing.py:262-271 — the next_counter CTE in _RESOLVE_SQL does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE on public.model_round_robin_counters whenever a winning tier exists, even when the tier has exactly one candidate (the common case).
findings.detail: A hot-path row write + now() bump per dispatch across the whole fleet for a tie-break that almost never has ties; trivially gateable on candidate count.

moves.title: API-direct runtime adapter ('api' runtime_type) for single-turn and fixed-tool-schema calls
moves.why: Removes CLI-subprocess bootstrap from the two highest-volume call classes: connector discretion screening and switchboard routing classification. The classification session needs exactly one tool (route_to_butler) with a fixed schema — a direct provider tool-use call returns in model-time only, cutting seconds off every inbound message and every screening decision while keeping intelligence in ephemeral LLM sessions (vision rule 4 intact).
moves.integration_points: New adapter in src/butlers/core/runtimes/ registered via create_adapter (base.py registry); new runtime_type value 'api' in public.model_catalog rows (no schema change — runtime_type is already free text resolved per tier, model_routing.py:_RESOLVE_SQL); DiscretionDispatcher._get_or_create_adapter (connectors/discretion_dispatcher.py:118) picks it up automatically once catalog entries flip; switchboard classifier path modules/pipeline.py:1976-1990 gains a structured tool-use fast lane that maps tool_use blocks to the existing route_to_butler handler (core_tools/_switchboard.py); spec delta on model-catalog + complexity-classification; Models tab (src/butlers/api/routers/model_settings.py) already edits runtime_type per entry.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Adapter + unit tests behind a catalog entry nobody references; 2) flip discretion-tier catalog entries and verify connector screening; 3) classifier fast lane with fallback to CLI adapter on error; 4) spec deltas.
moves.cost_note_manifesto: Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (roster/switchboard/MANIFESTO.md — routing backbone, ingress SLA).

moves.title: Deterministic precondition gates on scheduled tasks (skip the spawn when nothing changed)
moves.why: Stops paying workhorse sessions to evaluate 'is there anything to do' — the check education/travel/finance prompts currently perform inside the LLM becomes a daemon-side deterministic query. Owner payoff: visibly lower spend, fewer no-op sessions polluting the timeline, and the vision marker 'the system is boring, it works'.
moves.integration_points: scheduled_tasks schema (new nullable columns precondition_kind + precondition_ref, core alembic migration); core/scheduler.py cron pass (evaluate before the dispatch at :1843, record outcome 'skipped:precondition' via record_task_dispatched in core/metrics.py); butler.toml [[butler.schedule]] parsing (scheduler.py:_normalize_schedule_dispatch:246) and roster seeds; schedules API (src/butlers/api/routers/schedules.py) + dashboard schedule editor; core-scheduler openspec delta. Precondition kinds: registered deterministic job (reuses dispatch_mode='job' registry) or a read-only SQL count in the butler's own schema.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Schema + scheduler gate + skipped-outcome provenance; 2) API/UI exposure; 3) migrate education review-queue, travel upcoming-trip, and finance bill-reconcile prompts to gated form; 4) spec delta.
moves.cost_note_manifesto: Serves every domain butler's manifesto (acts only when its domain has signal); core-scheduler spec amendment, no new butler.

moves.title: Thread-continuation routing affinity: skip classification for active conversations, and let routing history feed the existing ingestion_rules engine
moves.why: The single biggest interactive-latency lever: a continuation message in a thread the switchboard routed to butler X minutes ago re-runs the full CHEAP classification session today. A short-TTL (sender, thread) → (butler, complexity) affinity map routes continuations deterministically (bypasses_llm=True, same provenance shape as ingestion-policy route_to rules), and consistent long-run history is surfaced as SUGGESTED route_to:<butler> rules for owner approval — building on, not duplicating, the owner-authored static rule engine in the ingestion-policy spec.
moves.integration_points: modules/pipeline.py MessagePipeline.process (insert affinity check after _accept_ingress:1175, before build_prompt:1948); switchboard schema table routing_affinity (sender_identity, thread_identity, target_butler, complexity, last_routed_at, TTL) written where routing outcomes are extracted (_extract_routed_butlers:501); safety valve via the existing corrections loop (core/corrections.py + bu-ec5h8's 'correct' tool) which must invalidate the affinity row; suggested-rule minting into switchboard ingestion_rules (ingestion-policy spec, action='route_to:<butler>', enabled=false pending owner approval via the existing /ingestion-rules API); spec delta on butler-switchboard + ingestion-policy.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Affinity table + bypass with PolicyDecision-style provenance (owner can always see WHY it skipped the LLM); 2) correction-invalidation; 3) suggested-rule miner as a switchboard scheduled job; 4) spec deltas.
moves.cost_note_manifesto: Serves the Switchboard infrastructure contract (classification + routing execution SLAs).

moves.title: Latency spine: per-phase spawn timing persisted on sessions and streamed to the console
moves.why: Makes the trigger→spawn→act loop diagnosable: queue-wait (global + per-butler semaphore), context-assembly ms, adapter process-boot-to-first-stream-event ms, model ms. Without it every other optimization here is flying blind; with it the console's judgment layer can say 'replies are slow because spawns queue 40s behind the global cap' with evidence one keystroke away.
moves.integration_points: spawner.py trigger()/_run() (timestamps already exist at :676-716 semaphore acquisition and :1295 t0; add monotonic marks around context fetches :1341-1380 and adapter first-event); runtime adapters report first_stream_event_at in last_process_info (claude_code.py stream-json loop, codex.py); persist as JSONB phase_timings on sessions via session_complete (core/sessions.py) — the session lifecycle events at sessions.py:217/319 already flow to the fleet event bus (api/routers/events.py:78), so the console gets it free; Prometheus histograms in core/metrics.py; core-spawner + core-sessions spec deltas.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Spawner-side marks + sessions JSONB + metrics; 2) adapter first-event mark per runtime; 3) sessions API/read-model exposure.
moves.cost_note_manifesto: Serves the staffer-archetype/QA contract and the console north star (earned calm, evidence spine); no manifesto amendment needed.

moves.title: Honest spend attribution: purpose dimension on the token ledger + correct classifier trigger_source + per-connector discretion identity
moves.why: Closes the two attribution holes: classification spend masquerading as 'tick' and all connector screening lumped under '__discretion__' with NULL session_id. Owner payoff: /spend and spend rules can finally answer 'what does one Telegram message cost me end-to-end' and cap screening spend per connector.
moves.integration_points: public.token_usage_ledger migration adding purpose TEXT NULL + record_token_usage(purpose=...) (model_routing.py:370-374, 1079-1125); spawner finally-block ledger write (spawner.py:2209) passes trigger_source-derived purpose; DiscretionDispatcher gains a required purpose kwarg and callers pass connector identity (telegram_user_client.py:357, whatsapp_user_client.py:543, live_listener/connector.py:208, home_assistant_pipeline.py:33, api/calendar/quick_add.py:175, api/briefing/prompts.py:155); fix modules/pipeline.py:1981 trigger_source 'tick' → 'classification' (audit the failover-classifier and spend-rule fixtures that match on trigger); surface purpose in spend stream events (spawner.py:2237 emit_spend_event extra) and /spend drill-down; catalog-token-limits + dashboard-spend-dashboard spec deltas.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Ledger column + plumb purpose through both write paths; 2) trigger_source rename with fixture sweep; 3) spend UI/rules exposure of the new dimension.
moves.cost_note_manifesto: No single butler manifesto — implies a small amendment to the Switchboard infrastructure contract (classification is an accounted service) and the spend-governance surface in dashboard-spend-dashboard spec.

audits.jarvis_gap: A JARVIS-grade household staff answers in conversational time and spends proportionally to task difficulty; Butlers' inference loop today treats every thought — a yes/no spam screen, a routing decision, a deep synthesis — as the same heavyweight act: a cold CLI subprocess with MCP handshake, spawned twice in series for every interactive reply, unconditionally for every cron slot, at a default WORKHORSE tier almost nothing overrides. The loop's latency is unmeasured (one duration_ms number), its cheapest calls are its least attributed (discretion spend under '__discretion__'/NULL session, classification labeled 'tick'), and nothing learns: the same sender's fifth message in a thread re-runs the same classification session the first one did. The routing/quota/failover/provenance machinery (model_routing.py, dispatch_attempts) is genuinely strong — what's missing is a fast lane (API-direct single-turn calls, thread affinity), a skip lane (deterministic preconditions instead of LLM no-op sessions), and an instrument panel (phase timings, purpose-tagged spend) so the console can prove the loop is getting faster and cheaper.
audits.ideal: Three call classes, each on its cheapest sufficient substrate: (1) deterministic daemon code for anything decidable by SQL — precondition-gated schedules, thread-affinity continuations, owner route_to rules — spawning nothing; (2) API-direct single-turn tool-use calls for screening and classification, returning in model-time with purpose-tagged spend; (3) full agentic CLI sessions reserved for genuine domain work, with per-phase latency persisted on every session and streamed live to the console. Every token in the ledger carries butler + session + purpose + trigger; the spend page can price 'one inbound Telegram message' end-to-end; the judgment layer cites queue-wait vs model-time when replies slow down; and the classifier's own routing history continuously proposes deterministic rules that shrink its future workload — the fleet gets faster and cheaper the longer it runs.

A single memory substrate whose lifecycle actually runs: every fact carries provenance (episode → session → ingestion trace), confidence that visibly decays and can be confirmed, entities that stay deduplicated at write time, a cross-butler discovery plane so any butler can find knowledge held elsewhere without an LLM round-trip, and retrieval/archival machinery proven at 100k-fact scale — so the graph the owner sees at year 3 is as trustworthy as at week 3.
audits.jarvis_gap: The knowledge-graph machinery is largely SHIPPED BUT DORMANT. Decay/fading/expiry code exists but is wired to nothing (0 fading, 0 expired rows in the live DB); 4 of 9 memory-enabled butlers never consolidate episodes (switchboard: 4,148 pending episodes vs 44 facts); the cross-butler discovery catalog (full spec + table + tools) has 0 rows because enable_shared_catalog is false everywhere; entity dedup is manual and exact-lowercase duplicates already exist at only 787 entities; vector indexes are ivfflat lists=20 built on empty tables, which will silently degrade recall well before 100k facts. The console's 'earned calm — no fabricated numbers' doctrine is violated at the substrate level: docs/modules/memory.md promises a scheduled decay sweep that has never run, so every confidence number shown is an un-decayed write-time value masquerading as a maintained one.

findings.title: Confidence decay/fading/expiry never runs anywhere in the fleet — run_decay_sweep is dead code
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:2354 defines retention-class-aware run_decay_sweep, but it appears in no job registry (_MEMORY_MAINTENANCE_JOB_HANDLERS at src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py:378-381 has only memory_consolidation, memory_episode_cleanup, memory_purge_superseded), no MCP tool, and no roster/*/butler.toml schedule (grep run_decay_sweep hits only storage.py + archived specs). Live dev DB: relationship.facts has 0 rows with metadata status='fading' and 0 validity='expired'. docs/modules/memory.md:121-131 claims 'A scheduled sweep computes effective confidence…' and openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md ('Retention-class-aware decay sweep') REQUIRES it. Read-time scoring does apply exp-decay (search.py:526,747) so ranking decays, but state transitions (fading/expired/archival) never happen — facts are immortal regardless of permanence class.
findings.detail: This is broader than the known 'relationship.facts dormant decay' ledger item: the sweep is unwired for ALL 9 memory-bearing butlers, and the archive_before_delete path for personal_profile/health_log/financial_log classes has never executed. The console showing confidence values implies a maintained lifecycle that does not exist — a substrate-level violation of the no-fabricated-numbers doctrine.

findings.title: 4 of 9 memory-enabled butlers never consolidate or clean episodes — promotion pipeline silently absent where volume is highest
findings.evidence: finance (roster/finance/butler.toml:35), travel (roster/travel/butler.toml:28), switchboard (roster/switchboard/butler.toml:34), education (roster/education/butler.toml:98) all enable [modules.memory] but define NO memory_consolidation/memory_episode_cleanup schedule (grep across roster/*/butler.toml: only general, home, health, relationship, lifestyle schedule them). The module does not self-schedule (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:224 on_startup registers hooks only). Live dev DB: switchboard 4,148 pending episodes vs 44 facts; finance 1,294 pending; education 1,137 pending.
findings.detail: Lifecycle wiring is hand-copied TOML per butler, so the highest-traffic butler (switchboard, which sees every routed message) accumulates raw episodes forever and promotes essentially nothing to durable facts. Episode TTL cleanup also never runs there, so growth is unbounded.

findings.title: Cross-butler discovery catalog is fully dormant: spec, table, tools all shipped, zero rows
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md defines public.memory_catalog as the cross-butler searchable index; enable_shared_catalog defaults False (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:185) and NO roster/*/butler.toml sets it (grep: zero hits); live dev DB: SELECT count(*) FROM public.memory_catalog = 0. memory_catalog_search (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/reading.py:113) therefore returns empty for every butler.
findings.detail: There is currently NO way for one butler to read another's facts short of a full Switchboard LLM round-trip; the sanctioned discovery plane exists but is switched off, and even if switched on today the ~3,600 pre-existing facts would be invisible (write-behind only, no backfill job exists).

findings.title: No entity dedup at creation time — duplicates already present at 787 entities
findings.evidence: Live dev DB public.entities: 9 exact lowercase-name duplicate pairs among non-merged rows, e.g. 'globex' as {organization, person}, 'tzeusii' (owner handle) as {other, person}, 'tzeusy/butlers' twice; 74 entities flagged metadata.unidentified=true; 46 tombstoned merges are all manual (memory_entity_merge). entity_create (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:52) performs no near-duplicate check — only entity_find_by_canonical exists (exact match, entities.py:130), and nothing calls it as a guard.
findings.detail: predicate-taxonomy.md §1 mandates resolve-before-create for ingestion paths, but that contract is enforced only by LLM prompt discipline. Each duplicate fragments the graph (facts split across two anchors), and fragmentation compounds — the 'which Chloe' problem re-enters through the write path.

findings.title: Retrieval will not survive 100k facts: ivfflat lists=20 built on empty tables, unindexable fuzzy-resolve query
findings.evidence: src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/001_memory_schema.py:84,203,330 create IVFFlat indexes with lists=20 at schema-creation time (empty tables) on episodes/facts/rules; pgvector ivfflat centroids are computed at build time and never rebuilt, so cluster quality and the lists count (rule of thumb rows/1000 → ~100 lists at 100k) are both wrong at scale. _fetch_fuzzy_candidates (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:537-575) filters on similarity(canonical_name,$1) > 0.3 plus per-row UNNEST(aliases) subqueries — a predicate shape that cannot use a trigram GIN index, forcing a seq scan of public.entities per resolve call.

findings.title: 'Archival' is a metadata flag, not an archive — archive_before_delete classes get no cold tier
findings.evidence: run_decay_sweep's archive path (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:2443-2456) sets metadata.archived_at + archived_content=true and flips validity='expired' on the SAME row; content never moves anywhere. memory_policies marks personal_profile/health_log/financial_log archive_before_delete=true (openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md seeding table), and RFC 0016 (about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0016-s3-blob-storage-contract.md) provides a blob store that memory never uses.
findings.detail: At years-scale, expired+superseded rows either bloat hot tables (where purge is unscheduled — memory_purge_superseded runs in only 3 of 9 butlers: lifestyle/health/home butler.toml) or get hard-deleted by purge with no recoverable archive, contradicting the fail-closed archive intent.

findings.title: Fact→evidence provenance chain exists in data but has no read surface
findings.evidence: Consolidation writes memory_links provenance edges from every derived fact/rule back to source episode IDs (src/butlers/modules/memory/consolidation_executor.py:209-251), and episodes carry session_id; but neither memory_get (tools/reading.py) nor the dashboard memory router (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py) exposes the chain — no endpoint or tool answers 'why does the system believe this fact'.
findings.detail: The console north star demands every clause be a door to root evidence via the trace spine; for memory facts the spine's data exists (fact → memory_links → episode → session_id) but is unreadable, so fact drill-down dead-ends at the fact row.

findings.title: Spec drift: memory-retention-policy still requires the dropped rule_applications table
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md ('Rule application audit tracking' requirement: rule_applications MUST be created and written on memory_mark_helpful/harmful) vs src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/006_drop_rule_applications.py which drops it. docs/modules/memory.md:148 also still lists rule_applications as an owned table.
findings.detail: Likely falls under open epic bu-17axsl (doctrine-spec-code reconciliation) — flagged here only so the synthesizer can route it there rather than file anew.

moves.title: Module-owned lifecycle: memory self-registers decay sweep + consolidation + cleanup as default scheduled jobs
moves.why: The entire memory lifecycle (decay→fading→expiry, episode promotion, TTL cleanup, superseded purge) currently depends on hand-copied butler.toml cron blocks, and the decay sweep is wired to nothing at all. Making the module register its own deterministic maintenance schedule on startup (with butler.toml able to override cadence, not existence) turns 'decay-by-design but dormant' into 'decay actually running' fleet-wide in one change, and drains the 6,500+ pending episodes in switchboard/finance/education. This is what memory-retention-policy already requires; no new spec needed, just a delta stating jobs are module-default.
moves.integration_points: Add memory_decay_sweep handler to _MEMORY_MAINTENANCE_JOB_HANDLERS (src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py:378) calling storage.run_decay_sweep (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:2354); have MemoryModule.on_startup (src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:224) register default deterministic schedules for memory_consolidation/memory_episode_cleanup/memory_purge_superseded/memory_decay_sweep via the core scheduler; delete now-redundant cron blocks from roster/{general,home,health,relationship,lifestyle}/butler.toml; spec delta to openspec/specs/memory-retention-policy/spec.md + module-memory; update docs/modules/memory.md §Decay. Serves every memory-bearing butler's manifesto implicitly (vision.md: 'the system is boring, it works'); no manifesto amendment needed.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Wire memory_decay_sweep job handler + schedule in the 5 butlers that already have memory cron (pure additive, ships alone). 2) Module-default schedule registration in on_startup with toml override + removal of copy-paste blocks. 3) One-shot catch-up: bounded consolidation backfill for the 4,148/1,294/1,137 pending-episode backlogs (batched, respecting dead_letter states).

moves.title: Turn on the cross-butler fact plane: enable memory_catalog fleet-wide + backfill job + make it the sanctioned cross-butler read
moves.why: The one-API cross-butler fact read the pursuit asks for already exists as spec+table+tools (public.memory_catalog, memory_catalog_search) and is simply off: 0 rows, no toml enables it. Enabling it plus a backfill of the ~3,600 existing facts/rules gives every butler discovery over the whole graph (health butler finds relationship's 'sister due in March' before a briefing) at zero LLM cost, with provenance pointers keeping canonical data in the owning schema — fully consistent with RFC 0006 isolation since grants are catalog-only.
moves.integration_points: Set enable_shared_catalog=true in [modules.memory] for all 9 roster/*/butler.toml (or flip the default at src/butlers/modules/memory/__init__.py:185); new backfill scheduled job (pattern: src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py memory handlers) that upserts existing facts/rules into public.memory_catalog using the UNIQUE(source_schema,source_table,source_id) key from openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md; write-behind already implemented (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/writing.py:381,531); surface memory_catalog_search results in briefing prompts (roster/general eod-tomorrow-prep skill) and the dashboard memory router (src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py) as a 'fleet knowledge' search. Serves the general butler's briefing manifesto and switchboard's routing-context contract; spec delta: default-on + backfill requirement in memory-discovery-catalog.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Flip default + enable in tomls (write-behind starts populating). 2) Backfill job + idempotency test. 3) Consumption: catalog search in briefing context assembly + dashboard cross-butler search tab.

moves.title: Entity hygiene loop: dedup guard at entity_create + nightly merge-candidate queue through approvals
moves.why: Duplicates exist at 787 entities (globex as person AND organization; the owner's own handle duplicated) and every duplicate silently splits facts across anchors — at 10k entities the 'which Chloe' problem returns via the write path. A write-time guard (exact + trigram + alias match → return existing or create flagged) plus a scheduled detector that emits merge candidates into the existing approvals/pending-actions surface keeps the graph convergent with owner-in-the-loop for ambiguous merges, matching predicate-taxonomy's resolve-before-create contract that is today enforced only by prompt discipline.
moves.integration_points: Guard in entity_create (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:52) reusing _fetch_fuzzy_candidates logic; fix the fuzzy predicate to the index-friendly `canonical_name % $1` form + add pg_trgm GIN index migration on public.entities(canonical_name, aliases) (new memory migration after 006); nightly merge-candidate job in src/butlers/scheduled_jobs.py writing to the approvals gate (src/butlers/modules/approvals/gate.py) with auto-merge above a confidence bar and owner review below; merge execution via existing entity_merge (entities.py:1175) which already repoints facts/calendar_event_entities/episodes. Serves roster/relationship/MANIFESTO.md ('a living database of the people in your life') and predicate-taxonomy.md §1; no manifesto amendment.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Trigram index + query-shape fix (pure perf, ships alone). 2) Create-time guard + tests (unidentified-entity path from predicate-taxonomy §1.2 kept working). 3) Nightly detector → approvals queue → dashboard entities page renders candidates with one-key merge.

moves.title: 100k-fact scale hardening: HNSW index migration + synthetic-scale regression harness
moves.why: ivfflat with lists=20 built on empty tables is a time bomb: centroids computed at creation never rebuild, so recall degrades invisibly as facts grow — retrieval starts returning confidently wrong context, the worst failure mode for a system whose doctrine is 'no number is ever fabricated'. pgvector HNSW builds incrementally, needs no list tuning, and removes the rebuild obligation permanently. A checked-in synthetic-scale test (100k facts, measured recall@k + latency budget) makes graph-scale a regression-tested property instead of a hope.
moves.integration_points: New memory migration (src/butlers/modules/memory/migrations/007_*) dropping the three ivfflat indexes (001_memory_schema.py:84,203,330) and public.memory_catalog's ivfflat (per memory-discovery-catalog spec) in favor of HNSW vector_cosine_ops; scale fixture + recall/latency assertions in tests/ using the testcontainers integration path (per butlers-mocked-pool-vs-integration-gap memory, verify against real Postgres); doc update docs/modules/memory.md §Retrieval. Serves all memory butlers; spec delta only to the index bullet in memory-discovery-catalog.
moves.slice_plan: Single PR: migration + scale harness; harness marked slow/nightly to keep CI fast.

moves.title: Honest forgetting: cold-tier archive via RFC 0016 blob store + owner-visible provenance chain ('why do I believe this')
moves.why: Trustworthy-over-years needs both real forgetting and inspectable remembering. Today 'archival' is a metadata flag on a hot row and purge (where it runs) hard-deletes with no recovery, while the fact→episode→session provenance chain already stored in memory_links has no read surface. Shipping (a) an archive writer that snapshots archive_before_delete-class facts to the S3 blob store before expiry/purge with a tombstone pointer, and (b) a provenance-chain read (memory_get?include_provenance + dashboard drill-down fact→episode→session_id) gives the owner both a bounded hot graph and a one-keystroke path from any remembered fact to its root evidence — extending the console's trace-id spine into the memory substrate.
moves.integration_points: Archive writer in run_decay_sweep's archive branch (src/butlers/modules/memory/storage.py:2443) and purge_superseded_facts (storage.py, job at scheduled_jobs.py:360) using the RFC 0016 blob contract (about/legends-and-lore/rfcs/0016-s3-blob-storage-contract.md, src/butlers/storage/); provenance read joins memory_links (consolidation writer: src/butlers/modules/memory/consolidation_executor.py:209-251) exposed via tools/reading.py memory_get and a new GET /api/memory/facts/{id}/provenance in src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py; spec deltas: memory-retention-policy (archive semantics) + module-memory (provenance read). Serves the trust doctrine in vision.md and every memory butler; the dashboard side folds into the existing judgment-layer surfaces rather than a new page.
moves.slice_plan: 1) Provenance chain API + fact drill-down (independent, pure read). 2) Blob archive on expiry with tombstone + restore script. 3) Extend purge job to archive-then-delete for archive_before_delete classes and schedule it fleet-wide (rides on move 1's module-owned schedules).

audits.jarvis_gap: The north star implies a household staff that confers: a butler that notices something outside its domain asks a colleague, waits for an answer, and returns a synthesized verdict to the owner. Today the fleet is a hub-and-spoke fan-out with no return path — route_to_butler is switchboard-only and terminates at {"status":"accepted"} (src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:497-498), domain butlers have zero tools to reach one another, cross-domain interest exists only as prompt text in the switchboard's extraction skill, the daily brief concatenates pre-rendered per-domain strings, and three separate unbudgeted egress paths (notify send, insight broker, decision-loop pushes) compete for the owner's attention with no arbiter. The staff cannot collaborate; each butler is alone with its schema.
audits.ideal: A collaboration fabric with four primitives, all brokered by the Switchboard per MCP-only doctrine: (1) correlated ask/answer delegation — any domain butler can pose a question to a colleague and is re-spawned with the answer (or the timeout) when it lands; (2) durable typed domain-event subscriptions keyed on the entity spine, so relationship learns when finance records a transaction naming a person it tracks without the extraction prompt anticipating it; (3) one attention ledger arbitrating ALL proactive owner egress — coalescing, budgeting, and prioritizing across butlers so simultaneous pings become one composed message; (4) cross-domain case files that bind a multi-butler investigation (symptom + pharmacy charge + doctor) into a single trace-spined story the console and the daily brief render as one narrative. Judgment stays in ephemeral sessions; the daemon carries only correlation state.

findings.title: Cross-butler dispatch is one-way and terminal — no answer ever returns to a caller
findings.evidence: src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:326-498 — route_to_butler builds a route.v1 envelope, dispatches route.execute on the target, and on success returns only {"status": "accepted", "butler": butler}. The target spawns its own session whose output goes to session logs or notify(); there is no result payload, no caller-visible correlation id, and no mechanism to check back. RFC 0021's decision loop (commit 9f647ab1d) adds owner one-tap decisions but no butler-to-butler answer path.
findings.detail: "Delegation with follow-up" (butler A asks B and checks back) is structurally impossible: the requesting session is ephemeral and gone by the time the target runs, and nothing re-invokes the requester with the outcome. Every multi-domain question must instead be pre-decomposed by the Switchboard at ingestion or answered incompletely by one butler.

findings.title: Domain butlers have no tool to reach another butler at all
findings.evidence: route_to_butler registers only on the Switchboard (src/butlers/core_tools/_switchboard.py:19 'Register switchboard-only tools'); grep of roster/*/butler.toml shows [butler.permissions] declared only by messenger, qa, and switchboard — no domain butler has cross-butler access (consistent with about/heart-and-soul/architecture.md 'Domain butlers default to no cross-butler access'). Domain sessions' only outbound surfaces are notify()/remind() (owner-facing) and memory_catalog_search (passive read of summaries).
findings.detail: A health session holding a symptom report cannot ask finance whether a pharmacy charge cleared, cannot ask relationship who the owner's doctor is (beyond stale catalog summaries), and cannot ask travel whether the owner will be abroad when a prescription runs out. The permissions matrix (CROSS_BUTLER_PERMISSION check at _switchboard.py:360) already exists as the authorization primitive but nothing on the domain side can exercise it.

findings.title: Owner-attention egress is fragmented across three unarbitrated paths
findings.evidence: notify(intent='send') delivers direct through Messenger with only per-message quiet-hours priority gating (src/butlers/core_tools/_notifications.py:289-296, quiet-hours gate at :576-621); the RFC 0011 broker budget/cooldown/dedup applies only to the insight pipeline (roster/switchboard/modules/insight_broker.py:1-31, daily cycle in roster/switchboard/butler.toml:58-63); RFC 0021 push-on-park adds a third push path. No table or job arbitrates when two butlers want the owner in the same hour.
findings.detail: Anti-spam is structural for insights but advisory for everything else. Two scheduled tasks firing near-simultaneously produce two Telegram pings with no coalescing — the already-observed calendar double-notify failure mode is one instance of this missing layer, not its full extent. 'Earned calm' at the console has no counterpart at the phone.

findings.title: No standing cross-domain subscription primitive — cross-butler interest lives only in one prompt
findings.evidence: The context bus is a fixed 11-signal user-state vocabulary with per-signal writer permissions (openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md 'Signal Vocabulary'); cross-domain fan-out happens once, at ingestion, driven by the switchboard's signal-extraction skill prompt (roster/switchboard/.agents/skills/signal-extraction/SKILL.md) and conversation-decomposition (openspec/specs/conversation-decomposition/spec.md). No table lets a butler durably register interest in another domain's events.
findings.detail: If finance records a transaction that names a tracked contact, or travel creates a trip that overlaps a medication schedule, the interested butler learns nothing unless the extraction prompt happened to anticipate that exact join at ingestion time. Domain-originated events (job scans, connector ingests routed to one butler) never fan out at all.

findings.title: The daily brief is concatenation, not synthesis — the composing session cannot see any specialist's data
findings.evidence: Specialist contributions are deterministic SQL snapshot jobs writing pre-rendered summary strings to state (src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py:39-51, contribution envelope :60-77); the General butler's prompt renders 'one concise line using the pre-rendered summary field' per domain and permits a cross-domain 'Heads-up' only when highlight strings happen to collide (roster/general/butler.toml:77-89).
findings.detail: The one place the fleet speaks with one voice is assembled from seven strings written before any cross-domain reasoning occurs. The composing session has no tool to pull a detail from a specialist (e.g., the actual departure time behind travel's highlight), so the Heads-up clause can only restate, never investigate.

findings.title: Insight proposals are jobs-only — the LLM sessions where judgment lives cannot propose insights
findings.evidence: propose_insight_candidate is registered as an MCP tool only on the Switchboard ([modules.insight_broker] appears only in roster/switchboard/butler.toml:42); domain butlers submit exclusively from deterministic scan jobs via direct in-process import (roster/health/jobs/health_jobs.py:152 'from butlers.tools.switchboard.insight.broker import propose_insight_candidate'; same pattern in roster/finance/jobs/finance_jobs.py, roster/travel/jobs/travel_jobs.py).
findings.detail: This inverts the doctrine that 'intelligence is in ephemeral sessions' (about/heart-and-soul/vision.md rule 4): the only agents allowed to propose proactive insights are the deterministic SQL scans, while a session that notices something genuinely insightful mid-conversation has no path into the broker and can only notify() directly (bypassing budget/dedup) or stay silent.

findings.title: memory_catalog is a passive cross-butler index — discovery without notification
findings.evidence: public.memory_catalog is explicitly 'a discovery index, NOT a canonical store' (openspec/specs/memory-discovery-catalog/spec.md); the only consumer surface is memory_catalog_search (src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/reading.py:113). Writes to the catalog trigger nothing.
findings.detail: The one existing cross-butler knowledge spine (entity_id-keyed catalog rows) is pull-only: relationship never learns that health wrote a fact about a person it tracks unless a future session happens to search for it. The catalog's entity_id/object_entity_id columns are exactly the join keys a subscription fabric needs — the schema is ready, the delivery mechanism absent.

moves.title: Delegation ledger: correlated ask/answer between butlers with scheduled follow-up
moves.why: Unlocks the defining collaborative behavior — health asks finance whether the pharmacy charge cleared, finance answers from its schema, health is re-spawned with the answer and reports one complete verdict to the owner. Serves every domain manifesto's 'complete picture' promise (health 'pieces only reveal their meaning when held together'; finance 'the answer is already waiting'). Requires a Switchboard infrastructure-contract amendment adding 'delegation brokering' as a responsibility.
